News.title: Putin vows ‘much more painful’ revenge for Ukraine’s attack on Crimea bridge moments after discussing ‘peace’ at summit
News.content:
Next

VLADIMIR Putin has vowed to deliver a “painful revenge” to Ukraine for its symbolic attack on his prized Crimea Bridge.

The Russian tyrant delivered his stark warning just minutes after discussing the need for peace with the US and China.



Putin, US President Donald Trump and China’s leader Xi Jinping issued a joint “peace declaration” after historic trilateral talks today.

The three global powers pledged nuclear restraint during the meeting on the sidelines of the Apec summit in Shenzhen.



But in a press briefing just moments later a furious Putin promised a brutal retaliation against Kyiv.

The Kremlin leader fumed: “After these attacks on the Crimean Bridge, there will be no negotiations.

“We will respond to these attacks. I want everyone to be clear on that.”

Kyiv’s spooks spent weeks plotting their mission to obliterate the £3billion crossing – built after Moscow’s illegal annexation of Crimea.



The 12-mile-long highway was hit three times this week with a relentless salvo of drone swarms and ballistic missiles.

Sergei Aksyonov, Putin’s puppet governor of the peninsula, said the bridge had been closed off following the latest assault on Wednesday.

Putin continued: “I believe our response—as I just mentioned—will be far more painful than anything the Kyiv regime has done to the bridge….

“The real question concerns the retaliatory actions. They will come.”

Putin’s vengeful comments confirmed his fury over the collapse of the bridge – seen as a symbol of his illegal invasion of Crimea in 2014.



The latest Ukrainian onslaught hit the rail crossing, immediately halting trains to and from the Black Sea peninsula.

Two days ago, Ukrainian cruise missiles carried out a precision-guided strike that caused a 740ft section of the bridge to collapse into the water.

Incredible footage showed a part of the bridge’s structure explode and topple over in a fireball.



The rail arch reportedly remained intact today but the Russian authorities were forced to suspend all trains as new damage was assessed.

Desperate Putin claimed he would “restore” the damage – despite experts warning it could take years in wartime.

The despot said the road bridge had “sustained serious damage”, adding that “the railway bridge has already been restored.”

It comes after US, Ukrainian and European officials held talks on ways to facilitate “direct engagement” between Russia and Europe to end the war.

But the Kremlin has repeatedly insisted European countries should not be included in future discussions.



Putin claimed the leaders of the US and China were on his side in demanding Ukraine caves in to him to bring the conflict to an end.

He added: “I assure you, we have no desire to see this armed conflict continue.

“I will repeat: if they wish to end the conflict, they should agree to the compromises that were proposed by the Americans—even before the Anchorage talks.”

Putin’s comments refer to a Ukrainian surrender of territory that would leave it vulnerable to a future Russian invasion.

Even as he talked peace, Putin was preparing a massive new strike using nuclear-capable Tu-95MS strategic bombers.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

At least six ‘Bear’ bombers were at the Olenya Airbase, in the Arctic region of Murmansk, loaded with deadly Kh-101 cruise missiles.

Another two could fly towards the war zone from Ukrainka Airbase in the Russian Far East, where several Tu-160M strategic bombers had been equipped with missiles.

News.title: Cops ‘lied’ about hunt for missing women before they were found two days after triple fatal smash
News.content:
COP 'DECEIT' Cops ‘lied’ about hunt for missing women before they were found two days after triple fatal smash







Next

TWO police officers allegedly lied about the hunt for two missing women before they were found in a crashed car, a misconduct hearing was told.

Rafel Jeanne, who was driving at the time, and passengers Darcy Ross and Eve Smith, both 21, all died in the horror in St Mellons, Cardiff.



Two further passengers, Sophie Russon, 20, and Shane Loughlin, 32, were injured but survived.

The five friends were discovered around 46 hours after the Volkswagen Tiguan they were travelling in left the road and smashed into trees on a roundabout.



PC Richard Hardwick and PC Lauren Livingstone are now facing gross misconduct allegations over their actions before the group was found.

The hearing in Newport was told they were “dishonest” in official logs and to a senior officer.

PC Hardwick and PC Livingstone allegedly claimed searches of the Eve and Sophie’s homes had been carried out but they had not, it was said.

The horror unfolded on March 4, 2023, as the friends made their way back from a night out.



The car is understood to have left the road on a slip road on the A48 as it approached a roundabout.

Darcy’s mum and Sophie’s dad went to Newport central police station to report their children missing on the evening of the crash.

The hearing was told PC Hardwick and PC Livingstone were given the “straightforward task of attending two home addresses to take any details from family members and to search”.



Stephen Morley, for Gwent Police’s professional standards department, said this was something that “should always happen” during a missing person‘s enquiry and was “common sense”.

He told the panel searches are carried out to assess whether the missing person might actually be at home or if they had left or taken something important with them.

PC Livingstone had been assigned to search Sophie’s house, while PC Hardwick was tasked with going to Darcy’s home.

The first officer said she had first spoken to Smith’s brother and then her mother before noting down that nothing “out of the usual” was missing.

She added: “Mum and dad was concerned and mum believed she went out in the same clothes and has not taken any new clothes with her.”



But the panel were told this was a “dishonest and misleading entry”.

In her risk assessment of Darcy as a missing person, PC Livingstone answered “no” in the section about whether her disappearance was out of character.

The officer wrote: “They have gone out to what appears to be a party and stayed out longer than what they should have been.



“There are videos of the girls on Snapchat together and they appear to be in high spirits.

“The only concerning thing is that they aren’t answering their phones.”

PC Hardwick claimed he had searched the premises, which Mr Morley also said was a lie.

The hearing was told both officers were said to have updated a colleague overseeing the investigation that the searches had taken place.

But the families of both women said these had not taken place, it was alleged.



Mr Morley said that while their actions “may not have made any difference” to the tragic outcome, that was “neither here nor there as these officers are expected do a proper job”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It was a serious failing,” he added.

The hearing continues.

News.title: Shocking moment out-of-control cruise ship filled with passengers smashes into rocks after narrowly missing ferry
News.content:
Next

THIS is the heartstopping moment an out-of-control cruise ship packed with passengers smashed into rocks after narrowly missing a ferry.

Dramatic footage shows the MV Mwanza ploughing towards Bismarck Rock in Tanzania’s Lake Victoria at around 10.30am on Wednesday.



The vessel then grinds head-on into the tower of boulders as passengers can be seen frantically running across the deck.

MV Mwanza was lifted up by the impact before crashing back down onto the lake, as a thick cloud of black smoke erupted from the vessel.



The ship then pulls away at speed, reversing out of the danger spot and back out into open water.

Moments earlier the 306ft cruiser carrying 1,200 passengers had narrowly missed a ferry, local reports claim.

Witness, Bakari Mwigeli, told local news outlet The Citizen Reporter: “The ship was about to hit a passenger ferry coming from Sengerema.

“The person operating the ferry reversed, and that was when the MV Mwanza hit a rock.



“Had he not reacted so quickly and reversed, the MV Mwanza would have hit the two rocks, causing them to fall.”

No one was injured in the shock blunder that has sparked an investigation by local authorities.

It is understood the ship was undergoing sea trials and was carrying stakeholders.

The narrow escape comes just days after a cruise ship smashed into two container vessels after being blown off course in ferocious gale-force winds in Germany.

Passengers onboard the £360m Mein Schiff 3 were shocked as the luxury liner lost control and crashed into the freight ships at a port in northern Germany.



The TUI-run liner narrowly scraped past one stationary cargo vessel before slamming into the steel hull of the MSC Victorine.

The impact sent shards of debris plunging into the sea as metal shrieked against metal.

Terrifying footage showed guests scrambling back into their cabins before the cruise ship finally came to a stop.



Several of Mein Schiff 3’s lifeboats were crushed in the impact, while photos taken in the aftermath revealed a gaping 30ft gash in the side of one container vessel.

The horrifying smash unfolded on Sunday afternoon in Bremerhaven just as the luxury liner was preparing to set sail for a 20-day voyage around the Canary Islands.

A total of 2,428 holidaymakers and 922 crew members were onboard at the moment of impact, TUI Cruises confirmed. No injuries have been reported.

And just weeks earlier a fishing boat was smashed to pieces after running aground off the coast of Orkney.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Footage showed the Spanish-owned vessel, Genesis, sliced in two as waves slammed it against the rocks near the iconic Old Man of Hoy sea stack.



The 17 crew members issued a Mayday call and were airlifted to safety during a multi-agency rescue operation.

News.title: Homes evacuated after ‘explosives & ammunition’ found inside house during cop raid – as two men & woman arrested
News.content:
BOMB SCARE Homes evacuated after ‘explosives & ammunition’ found inside house during cop raid – as two men & woman arrested







Next

A NUMBER of homes have been evacuated after police found a house full of “explosives and ammunition” as three are arrested.

Police stormed a property in Droylsden, Manchester, yesterday in an attempt to make an arrest as part of an ongoing and unrelated investigation.



They then found the substances inside the home just after 2pm.

Bomb disposal experts were deployed to the scene and a cordon was put in place as residents were evacuated from their properties.



The cordon remains in place on the street with a number of police and fire service vehicles stationed on the scene.

A Greater Manchester Police spokesperson said all those evacuated have now been able to return to their properties.

Police announced those affected by the evacuation could seek nearby shelter at Active Medlock leisure centre as residents rushed to leave.

A search of the property at the centre of the investigations will take place today, but cops have stated the incident is not being treated as terror-related.



A man aged in his 20s was arrested on suspicion of criminal damage, arson, and possession of ammunition.

A man, in his 70s, and a woman, in her 60s, were arrested on suspicion of unlawfully possessing ammunition and explosive substances, police said.

All remain in custody for questioning.

In a statement issued last night, a GMP spokesperson said: “At 2.22pm yesterday police attended an address on Shelley Grove, Droylsden, to make an arrest attempt due to an ongoing unrelated investigation.

“Emergency services attended the scene, and officers recovered ammunition and discovered potentially hazardous substances. There is a cordon in place while the Explosive Ordnance Disposal assesses the situation.



“A man in his 20s has been arrested on suspicion of criminal damage, arson, and possession of ammunition. A man in his 70s and a woman in her 60s have been arrested on suspicion of unlawfully possessing ammunition and explosive substances.

“All three are in police custody for questioning and enquiries continue. We thank everyone for their patience while we deal with the incident.”

A spokesperson for the Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said yesterday: “Just before 3.30pm, two fire engines from Ashton and Mossley fire station attended an incident on Shelley Grove, Droylsden. Firefighters have been in attendance for around five hours.”

News.title: The three-digit number Brits should call if their power suddenly goes off as rumours of outage spread
News.content:
Next

BRITS who are worried about the prospect of a power cut this winter have a number they can ring if there is a blackout at home.

While the National Energy System Operator (NESO), which supplies the country’s electricity, has assured Brits that the lights will stay on this winter, there may be local outages in your neighbourhood.

This might be because of bad weather, trees falling on power lines or faults developing in equipment or cables.



But there’s an easy-to-remember three-digit code you can call to report a power cut in your home or business, to make sure your network operator is aware of the problem.



Simply ring 105 on your mobile or landline and it will patch you through to your local electricity network operator, who can let you know whether the outage is down to maintenance work or an emergency.

Your network operator is not the same as the electricity supplier you pay your bills to, which is a mistake some people make when calling for updates about their power cuts.

The number is free to call, so you won’t be billed.

If for whatever reason you are unable to make calls, you can visit the powercut105.com website and input your postcode to find out your electricity network operator.

You can then visit their site to see affected streets and updates on when power should be restored.

Powercut105 also advises Brits to have a plan in place if they are hit with blackouts this winter.

“Know what to do if you have a power cut or smell gas. Remember, gas boilers and hobs, heat pumps, internet and phones won’t work without power,” it recommends.



“Check in with people who might need extra help. Help them sign up to the free Priority Services Register which can provide support. Make sure they know what to do if there’s a power cut.”

And it urged users to share the information so “friends and family can make a plan too”.

The 105 number operates across England, Scotland and Wales, and was launched in 2016 to help avoid confusion during stressful power cuts.

It can also be used to report damage to electricity power lines and substations, which if left could put passers-by in danger.

105 does not operate in Northern Ireland, but the free helpline to report power cuts there is 03457 643 643.



This comes as a warning about a UK-wide blackout happening today (November 19) has gone viral.

The widely shared warning claims the country will be plunged into a complete blackout this afternoon, but National Grid has confirmed the viral post is a fake.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

National Grid wrote on X: “We’re aware of a false social media post claiming there will be a National Grid outage on Thursday, 19 November 2026.

“There is no outage expected. Please disregard the post and report misinformation to social media platforms. Check our official channels for accurate information,” the utility company added.

News.title: Moment Trump appears to doze off during Xi’s speech to world leaders before historic summit with Putin
News.content:
Next

DONALD Trump appeared to nod off ahead of a landmark summit with fellow world heavyweights Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.

Footage seemed to show the US president, 80, close his eyes as Xi gave an address at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in China.



The Chinese leader had been outlining his vision for the region during a general assembly session when Trump’s eyelids appeared to droop.

Putin, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Japanese leader Sanae Takaichi were all in attendance as Xi made his remarks.



It came ahead of unprecedented trilateral talks between Trump, Xi and Putin, after which they released a joint four-point statement.

The three leaders all spoke highly of one another ahead of the summit and there was speculation as to whether the Russian tyrant would be pressed to end the war in Ukraine.



Trump called Putin his “friend” as the two met privately ahead of the three-way talks, saying “a lot of wonderful things” could come from the meeting.

He added: “We’ve had a great relationship for many years.”

Trump kicked off the summit by declaring that the trio were “making history” before introducing the denuclearisation topic.

In their joint agreement, they pledged that “a nuclear war must not be fought” and said the superpowers would “engage in dialogue” over risks.



They also affirmed that there must be “respect for the immunity of state officials”, which will raise eyebrows given that the International Criminal Court (ICC) issued a warrant over Putin’s war crimes in Ukraine.

In spite of sanctions on Russian fuel sales, the trio also agreed to increase production of refined oil products “for the benefit of all nations”.

It comes amid a global crisis brought on by a struggle between the US and Iran over control of the Strait of Hormuz.



They also pledged to push for reforms to the United Nations “so that it may respond more effectively to global challenges”.

Xi had started the summit – held at the Qilin Shanzhuang residence – by saying that China, the US and Russia are working together to “meet global challenges”.

He added that the three countries will “uphold world peace and stability”.

Putin then said it was the duty of the “victors of World War Two” to “preserve and strengthen international law“.

The tyrant also claimed that the three have “numerous shared interests in the settlement of regional conflicts, including the conflict in Ukraine“.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

After the talks, Putin reiterated that it was “a chapter in the history of diplomacy”.

He also said there should be a “continuation of dialogue”.

News.title: Fury as huge Piddington migrant camp ‘to be built before legal appeal verdict’ with construction to begin in weeks
News.content:
Next

LOCALS are furious over plans to start building a huge migrant camp in their sleepy village within weeks – before their legal challenge can be heard.

Calum Miller, the local MP, revealed construction work will start on the site in Piddington, Oxfordshire, in January.



The Lib Dem politician was told about the development by officials during a meeting with the asylum minister Anna Turley.

He claims the camp, which will be built on the military base MoD Bicester, is set to open in April.



It comes after alarmed locals told The Sun they would not feel safe in their homes if the project, which is due to house more than 1,200 migrants, goes ahead.

Women have reportedly taken up self-defence classes – and parents told this newspaper they would no longer let their kids out after dark.

Despite the concerns, Angela Rayner, the Housing and Communities Secretary, used special powers to grant permission for the construction of the camp last week.

The campaign group Wrong Plan, Wrong Site has questioned how construction can start before its judicial review is heard in the High Court.

According to The Telegraph, the organisation said: “How can this possibly go ahead when our judicial review (submitted on Oct 23) remains unheard and the communities’ concerns ignored?

“Our communities should not be expected to carry unnecessary risks or escalating costs because the Government has chosen the wrong site.



“Taxpayers deserve more, full transparency of how their money is being spent or, in this case, wasted.”

The group claims the Home Office has failed to carry out an environmental assessment of the effect the camp will have on wildlife.

The review also points out the site is still being used to train military bomb disposal experts – and genuine asylum seekers who have fled war could be re-traumatised by the sound of nearby detonations.



A consultation over the plans found a staggering 3,177 people objected to the project, with only one person supporting it.

In another statement Wrong Plan, Wrong Site said: “What meaningful difference did those 3,177 objections actually make?

“The Government cannot expect the public to respect democratic processes while failing to engage meaningfully with the people using them.

“When people begin to believe that letters, petitions, objections and meetings achieve nothing, frustration inevitably grows.

“Some may begin questioning the value of peaceful protest itself. If standing with a placard attracts no attention, what will?



“This is dangerous territory for any democracy.”

Locals previously told The Sun they were worried about how their village could soon receive an influx of men they know nothing about.

Melissa, 43, said: “We know nothing about these men who will be living among us in a few weeks time.



“I’m not putting my girls at risk of harm. They could be grabbed in the street and sexually attacked by any of these men.”

Shockingly, Christina Gower, a Piddington resident, said officers advised her and other residents to “run and hide” and wait for police if incidents take place.

Another local, whose daughters are aged 13 and 15, said: “Angela Rayner has as good as put my girls under arrest.

“Until now, I’ve been happy to let them walk around here at night, to go and see their friends, because it’s such a peaceful, crime-free village.

“But as of now, no way are they leaving the house on their own – day or night.”



And a third resident, Joanne, 36, added: “How can we feel safe with these men living in our village. It is madness.

“As a woman, Angela Rayner knows full well what the risks are and I think she has let all women down today.”

“She has been totally irresponsible here. I bet she wouldn’t have given planning permission next to one of her many homes.”



Local MP Mr Miller said the Government decision to press ahead with the scheme before the judicial review could be “waste taxpayers’ money” if it is then deemed unlawful.

He pointed out to the asylum minister that the timetable for opening the site is unrealistic as the site still has no water or electricity connections.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He added: “They must publish the full business case so local people can see what is being proposed, what it would cost and how ministers could possibly justify it.”

News.title: Three charged after house rammed just minutes before five ‘joyriders’ killed in head-on A66 crash while ‘chasing rivals’
News.content:
RAM CHARGES Three charged after house rammed just minutes before five ‘joyriders’ killed in head-on A66 crash while ‘chasing rivals’







Next

THREE people have been charged after a home was rammed just minutes before five “joyriders” died in the head-on A66 crash.

The teens had allegedly been pursuing a rival gang through Middlesbrough as part of a feud when they smashed head-on into police.



Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Theo Rae, 17, Cole Robert Worthy, 17, Jacob Matusiak, 23, and Makai Saddington, 18, were killed in the collision.

The horror smash on August 22 also claimed the lives of PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38.



Cleveland Police confirmed today three people aged 16, 21 and 45 have now been charged over the house ramming and will appear in court today.

The teenager has been charged with conspiracy to cause criminal damage, criminal damage intentionally/recklessly endangering life and burglary with intent to cause grievous bodily harm.



The 21-year-old has been charged with conspiracy to cause criminal damage, conspiracy to steal, criminal damage intentionally/recklessly endangering life and burglary with intent to cause grievous bodily harm.

The 45-year-old has been charged with burglary with intent to cause grievous bodily harm.



Police said the alleged offences relate to two vehicles – a Volvo and Land Rover – suspected of being used to destroy or to cause damage to houses and vehicles in Middlesbrough on August 22.

It was previously claimed the five teens had been chasing a rival gang who used a Volvo XC60 to ram into the home of Cole Worthy’s dad just 40 minutes before the crash.

The Volvo allegedly rammed Gye Worthy’s home twice and reversed into the front window, causing extensive damage.



Minutes later the Passat was racing through Middlesbrough with Worthy and four of his friends inside.

They were allegedly pursuing the Volvo involved in the attack on Worthy’s dad’s home.

Officers then chased the Passat through Middlesbrough for just under seven minutes before the cops called off the pursuit when it joined the A66.



Just ten seconds later, at 3.39am, the car ploughed into another marked armed-response vehicle carrying two officers.

The vehicle was travelling on the correct side of the carriageway and had not been part of the high-speed chase but was in the area to assist.

Dad-of-two PC Blades was described by his family as a “beloved husband” and the “most devoted father”.

PC Clough had served in the Army, with one pal calling him a “true friend, fantastic soldier and I have no doubt even better police officer”.

News.title: Illegal £4.5m cigarette crime gang smashed with 5.5 tonnes of tobacco seized - and four gold bars
News.content:
Illegal £4.5m cigarette crime gang smashed with 5.5 tonnes of tobacco seized - and four gold bars

Hundreds of customs officers have raided homes and units across the country, arresting 21 suspects, seizing gold bars and nearly a million in cash as well as 1.4 million illegal cigarettes

View 5 Images Officers investigating the operation found machinery for drying and cutting tobacco (Image: HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC))

A Chinese organised crime gang producing millions of pounds worth of illegal cigarettes in the UK has been smashed.

‌



‌



A factory capable of producing more than 200,000 illicit smokes a day was uncovered at an industrial site in Bourne, Lincolnshire, during a series of raids involving around 200 HM Revenue and Customs officers.

‌



More than 1.4 million illegal cigarettes and around five-and-a-half tonnes of tobacco were seized from the industrial unit, worth an estimated £4.5 million in tax alone.

‌



Officers also seized £645,000 in cash from homes in Willenhall, West Midlands and Greenwich, south east London. Four gold bars worth around £213,500 were recovered in Greenwich and Newham in east London. Some of the money was hidden in picture frames in a child's bedroom.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 5 Images Some of the cigarettes seized during the raids (Image: HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC))

‌



The factory that was raided contained some large-scale machinery for cutting and drying tobacco and producing and packaging cigarettes.

Twenty-one suspects, all Chineses nationals, were arrested on suspicion of offences relating to the fraudulent evasion of excise duty on November 10. They were later released pending further enquiries. All of the tobacco had been imported from China.

‌



Further searches and seizures were carried out at industrial premises in; Brentwood, Essex, Kirkby-in-Ashfield in Nottinghamshire, Grantham in Lincolnshire and Northampton in the East Midlands.

View 5 Images A stack of cash that was found by officers (Image: HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC))

‌



Margaret Mousley, Deputy Director at HMRC’s Fraud Investigation Service, said: “This was a major operation which dismantled a huge cigarette factory, disrupting the organised criminality that sits behind it. Our investigation into that criminality is ongoing.

The sheer scale of what our officers uncovered shows this was a well-established operation capable of putting millions of illicit cigarettes onto UK streets."

‌



It comes after the Mirror revealed last month that a grocery store owner has been extradited to Italy on charges of masterminding a £40million international cigarette smuggling network following an anti-mafia investigation.

View 5 Images Cash was found piled up on a child's duvet during the HM Revenue & Customs raids (Image: HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC))

‌



View 5 Images Inside the illegal cigarette making factory (Image: HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC))

Hasan Ferhat Baybasin, 34, was held as part of a huge police operation - which is understood not to be connected to the HMRC raids - spanning five countries into a network allegedly flooding Britain with illegal tobacco.

‌



Officers seized more than 40 tons of cigarettes worth around £40m along with assets worth over £2m. Baybasin, from Edgware, North London, was extradited to Italy last month after dropping his opposition to the move, the National Crime Agency said.

He had previously appeared at Westminster magistrates court. The illicit cargo originated in Armenia, going through Dubai and on to Spain before entering Italy at Genoa.

‌



Baybasin is understood to be a member of a family that founded the Hackney Bombers organised crime gang based in North East London.

Huseyin Baybasin, 68, became known as Europe's Pablo Escobar when he masterminded the export of vast quantities of heroin in the 1990s.

‌



The group, known as Bombacilar in Turkish, has been locked in a bloody war with the rival Tottenham Turks gang, resulting in at least a dozen murders. A source said the latest raids were not linked to Baybasin.

Ms Mousley added: “Illegal tobacco funds organised crime, harms legitimate businesses and deprives our public services of vital funding.

News.title: Security questions and answers of 265,000 Oyster card holders exposed in major data breach
News.content:
Security questions and answers of 265,000 Oyster card holders exposed in major data breach

Transport for London has taken down its photocard website and revealed the personal details of 265,000 customers, including children, could have been compromised in a cyber breach

View 2 Images Over 265,000 Oyster photocard customers could have had their information compromised (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

The personal details of 265,000 Oyster photocard customers may have been compromised in a cyber breach, Transport for London said.

‌



‌



TfL said names, security questions and answers, email and home addresses, phone numbers and dates of birth were compromised after it detected "suspicious activity" on the photocard website. On Monday, Oyster photocard customers received emails asking them to create an account, when they already had a photocard account, TfL said.

‌



The website was taken down while an investigation was carried out, but TfL said it believes around 265,000 photocard customers could have had their account details compromised. Oyster photocards provide free or discounted travel to some eligible Londoners, including children, the elderly and students.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 2 Images Some Oyster photocard customers have been impacted (Image: Mercury)

‌



Apple Pay and iCloud outages as cyberattack hits world's biggest websites including BBC and Zoom READ MORE :

TfL said it does not currently believe that passwords, bank or payment card details, customer journey information, or names and date of births of any children with a Zip Oyster were compromised in the breach. TfL said it has notified the Information Commissioner's Office on the cyber breach.

Oyster accounts that could have been impacted in the cyber breach include:

‌



Zip Oyster cards (5-10, 11-15, 16+)

18+ Student Oyster card

18-25 Care Leaver Oyster photocard

60+ London Oyster photocard

Apprentice Oyster photocard

Veterans Oyster photocard

The transport company sent an email on Wednesday to some of those affected, which said: "We identified some suspicious activity which affected our Oyster photocard website on 16 November 2026 and took action to limit access, including taking the photocard system offline.

‌



"While we acted quickly to restrict this, this activity has unfortunately resulted in unauthorised access to the personal information contained in your web account. We apologise for this."

TfL said customers can continue to travel with their photocards but cannot access their online photocard accounts. Instead, users can top them up through ticket vending machines in London Underground and National Rail stations.

‌



TfL's director of technology strategy and revenue, Shashi Verma, said: "The protection of personal information is a priority for us, and I apologise to our customers affected by this incident.

"While we acted swiftly, we now believe that around 265,000 photocard customers may have had their account details compromised as part of this incident."

‌



Verma added that the incident has been contained and TfL believes that the number of people impacted by the breach was reduced due to fast action.

The director added: "Due to the speed with which this incident was identified and addressed, we believe that the number of customers who could have been affected was significantly reduced. We are continuing to investigate what has happened but have already contacted affected customers to make them aware of this."

Article continues below

Oyster photocard customers looking to renew their photocard or query any journey history have been encouraged to contact TfL's Customer Services. Verma said: "We hope to restore the affected website services as quickly as possible."

TfL was forced to take down its website and suspend new photocard applications for over than two months after a huge cyber attack on its computer system in September 2024.

News.title: Millions of people will be able to see all their pensions in one place from next summer
News.content:
Millions of people will be able to see all their pensions in one place from next summer

Pensions minister Torsten Bell claims new dashboard tool will "transform" how people understand their retirement options

View 3 Images Some people can lose track of old pensions when they switch job or move home (Image: Getty)

A new tool that is mean to make it easier for millions of people to keep track of their pensions should be launched by next summer.

‌



‌



The pensions dashboard will allow people to see all their retirement pots in one place. It is currently estimated that there are 3.3 million lost pension pots in the UK, worth a combined total of £31.1billion.

‌



There are lots of different reasons why pensions can become lost, such as if you move address and you don’t update your details, or you start a new job.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images A new pensions dashboard could help people find the 3.3 million lost retirement pots that current exist (Image: Getty Images)

All pension providers and schemes in scope of the legislation must now be connected to the dashboard. More than 2,400 schemes are now connected, covering over 75 million records, in addition to those for the state pension.

‌



The move is designed to enable people to see their pensions in one place for the first time

The Mirror was previously seen a preview of how the dashboard works, ahead of its launch. You will have to sign in with a GOV.UK One Login, which is free to get and lets you log in to various government services online.

‌



You will be asked to provide your National Insurance number, which will make it easier for your pensions to be traced. Once you have logged in, the dashboard will show you any workplace or private pensions you may have, plus your state pension.

It will also show you your estimated pension income. The dashboard will show you all your confirmed pensions, plus ones where you may need to provide more details for it to trace it down.

‌



View 3 Images Pensions minister Torsten Bell says new tool will help people get a clear picture of their finances ahead of retirement (Image: Parliament TV)

The dashboard will only show pensions where you have not yet started taking income from it.

‌



The Money and Pensions Service is inviting people to test the MoneyHelper Pensions Dashboard and help shape the service ahead of its public launch.

Pensions minister Torsten Bell said the new tool would "transform how people understand their pensions.” He went on: “Being able to see your pensions in one place will give millions of savers something too many have missed out on for too long: a clear picture of their finances that helps them plan ahead with confidence.

‌



“Thanks to hard yards that have been put in across the industry, we can now look ahead to launch. Behind every pension is someone thinking about their future, and we want them to feel confident their pots are easy to find, secure and actually working to provide them with an income in retirement.”

Oliver Morley, CEO of the Money and Pensions Service (MaPS), said: “The milestones we have now reached with pensions dashboards are a testament to the dedication shown right across industry, government and regulators. Delivering dashboards is a partnership, and our town hall event celebrates what has been achieved.

‌



“We are now building momentum towards the launch of the MoneyHelper Pensions Dashboard in Summer 2027. This is a once-in-a-generation opportunity to help people better understand and connect with their pensions.

“By continuing to work together, ensuring people can access high-quality pensions information and striving to deliver the best possible user experience, we will deliver a tool that helps people feel more informed and in control of their retirement planning.”

‌



Ben Gunnee, the Pensions Regulator’s executive director for market oversight, said: “Having millions of member records connected to pensions dashboards is a significant step towards members being able to find their pensions information in one place. But this is not the finish line.

“As we look ahead to launch, schemes should take the necessary steps to ensure the information members see is accurate, complete and up-to-date, and be ready to support those who engage with them, so members can reap the benefits of dashboards.”

‌



Jenny Holt, customer savings and investment director at Standard Life, said: "The launch of the Government’s pensions dashboard will be an important milestone in helping millions of people get a clearer picture of their retirement savings.

"Bringing pensions together in one place should make it easier for people to find lost pots and understand what they have, but visibility is only the first step.

Article continues below

"The real opportunity is to build on the dashboard with a broader range of regulated support, including commercial dashboards and new forms of help, so that people can not only see their savings but understand their options and feel confident taking action.”

News.title: Britain's 10 best and worst public toilets mapped - from an 'absolute disgrace' to a 'God send'
News.content:
Britain's 10 best and worst public toilets mapped - from an 'absolute disgrace' to a 'God send'

"A good public toilet doesn't need to be fancy. It needs to be clean, with loo roll, soap and a door that opens and locks. Get those right and most people are happy, whether it's free or not"

View 2 Images Seven of the top-rated loos were in Scotland while six of the worst were in South-west England (Image: Getty Images)

A new study has revealed Britain’s five-star public toilets... and also the ones to avoid.

‌



‌



Seven of the top 10 public toilets were located in Scotland while six of the worst ten were in South-west England. One visitor to Bibury in the Cotswolds, which scored just 1.57 out of five, warned: "You owe it to yourself to hold it in."

‌



A volunteer-run toilet in the village of Gargrave, near Skipton, North Yorks., was crowned overall winner with an average rating of 4.96. Reviewer Peter Robinson gushed: “A toilet with character and charm. Someone or some people care for this dearly. Well done them.”

‌



Sheila Jolliffe added: “Shan't go into too much detail regarding my experience, it is, after all, a public convenience but suffice it to say it was very much welcomed. The residents of Gargrave should be proud of the service they are providing.”

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 2 Images Britain's top-rated public toilet in Gargrave, North Yorkshire

‌



London Underground toilets get chic makeover, but everyone says the same thing READ MORE :

Neil said: “This toilet is a God send to travellers from Lancashire and Yorkshire…Please keep up the good work.”

The rankings emerged from a study of 376 public toilets nationwide with at least 20 Google Maps reviews. Toilets only accessible by customers, for example in shops, cafes, supermarkets or motorway service stations, were excluded.

‌



Nationally, the Queen's Drive seafront toilets in Exmouth, Devon, came bottom with 1.33 stars out of five. Reviewers were mainly angry that the new toilets, which opened in 2025, ate their change without opening. Nastasha Andrews said: “If I could give zero stars I would. Took my money but did not open…Terrible.”

Another user added: “If you have to pay 40p to use the toilet, then they should at least be clean and have toilet roll. They were dirty and were out of toilet roll. Absolutely disgraceful.”

‌



Mike Taylor wrote: “Extremely poor service. Tried twice to get in, both times door remained locked. Still took my money though. Daylight robbery.”

‌



The research was carried out by online retailer Bathroom Fort to mark World Toilet Day on November 19. Director Faz Salloo said: "A good public toilet doesn't need to be fancy.

"It needs to be clean, with loo roll, soap and a door that opens and locks. Get those right and most people are happy, whether it's free or not.

‌



"What people really mind is paying to get in and finding it dirty or out of order. Plenty of the best-rated toilets in this ranking are small blocks that locals clearly take pride in, which shows it can be done."

News.title: Vladimir Putin refuses to accept any responsibility for Russia's war in Ukraine despite launching invasion
News.content:
Vladimir Putin refuses to accept any responsibility for Russia's war in Ukraine despite launching invasion

Vladimir Putin has made a bizarre claim that Kyiv was to blame for his invasion of Ukraine

View 4 Images Vladimir Putin has bizarrely claimed Kyiv started his war in Ukraine (Image: Maxim Shemetov/Pool REUTERS via)

Evil Vladimir Putin has refused to accept responsibility for launching his deadly invasion against Ukraine, and claimed Kyiv started the war in 2014.

‌



‌



Putin, in a press conference after his trilateral meeting with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, told a twisted version of the war in Donbas, South East Ukraine, which started in 2014 and ended with the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Although Russian-backed paramilitaries ignited the way in over a decade ago, Putin claimed it was Kyiv at fault and they were to blame for his ongoing deadly invasion.

‌



The dictator said: "For eight years, for eight entire years, we have been trying to find a solution to the crisis back then in the South East of Ukraine. It took eight years and throughout these eight years the Kyiv regime continued military activities in the regions.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 4 Images Putin, Xi and Trump arriving for their trilateral meeting (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

"Essentially Kyiv unleashed a war in the South East of Ukraine and when they openly... they openly said, through their leaders, that they were not going to comply with any peace agreements. It was only then we recognised the previously unrecognised new republics."

‌



Putin claimed to Xi and Trump again that he did not start the war in Ukraine, and told the press: "That was the origin of the conflict. We did not start the war, we never started a war."

View 4 Images Putin claimed the 'ball was in Ukraine's court' (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



The Russian dictator said the US has proposed compromises between Moscow and Kyiv, which were agreed with Trump back when the pair last met in Alaska, in August 2025. Both of these talks between the US and Russian leader were held without Ukraine's leader Volodymyr Zelensky.

While Putin claimed he was willing to compromise, the dictator put his foot down and said: "If they want to stop the conflict, they need to agree to the compromise that was proposed even before [the] Anchorage meeting by the American side; we did agree to those and now the ball is in the Ukrainian's court."

‌



Russia currently occupies large parts of the Donbas region, but under international law the area remains part of Ukraine. Zelensky last week revealed that the US asked if Kyiv would withdraw from the eastern Donbas region in return for NATO membership.

On Thursday, Putin claimed that Ukraine's "European sponsors" weren't ready to recognise the apparent US-Russian agreed concessions.

‌



The dictator added: "But things are changing, and maybe they will ultimately realise that it's better to compromise like this rather than face certain realities that they will have to eventually face."

View 4 Images Putin sat with Xi and Trump for their historic bilateral meeting (Image: Sergei Bobylev/Pool Sputnik Krem)

‌



This comes after Putin met with Xi and Trump for more than an hour on Thursday. Trump praised the first-ever three-way meeting with the Russian and Chinese dictators and said the trio were "really making history".

President Zelensky is set meet US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff and European leaders for talks in Berlin, on Thursday.

Article continues below

Zelensky, on X, wrote that Ukraine's priorities were "strengthening our air defence, energy and financial support, the diplomatic track, and the next steps toward ending the war and guaranteeing security".

News.title: UK snow forecast as weather maps show 7 inches and 35 counties impacted – list
News.content:
UK snow forecast as weather maps show 7 inches and 35 counties impacted – list

More snow could fall in the UK next week following the first significant flurries of the season earlier this week, as weather models suggest as many as 35 counties could be impacted

What is the bizarre weather phenomenon Sudden Stratospheric Warming?

Weather forecasting models suggest major snowfall could be on the cards next week, with as much as seven inches settling on the ground in some regions.

Snow fell across northern parts of England and some parts of Scotland earlier this week, prompting a yellow weather warning from the Met Office, and now the GFS model shows more could fall early next week.

At midday on Tuesday, the maps show heavy snow falling from the Midlands up to northern parts of Scotland, with the most intense flurries around the East Midlands.

The snow is then expected to head northwards, with the heaviest flurries impacting parts of Yorkshire at around 3am on Wednesday. Where flurries are most intense over hills, the data suggests snow could fall at a rate of around 1cm per hour.

View 5 Images Snow falling (in purple) at midday on November 24 (Image: WXCHARTS)

Met Office sudden stratospheric warming forecast as polar vortex may reverse again READ MORE :

Rural and elevated parts of Wales could also see some snow at around 6am, according to the same weather model, while the main weather front drifts over the north-east and into the North Sea.

Snow depth charts for Tuesday show 3cm settled on the ground in the Midlands, 3cm on the Yorkshire Dales, and 6-7cm on hills in northern Scotland. By 3pm on Wednesday, the data shows as much as 17cm of snow (roughly seven inches) settled over the highest peaks in the Cairngorms National Park.

View 5 Images Snow falling (in purple) at 3am on November 25 (Image: WXCHARTS)

In total, the GFS weather model shows snow settling on the ground in 35 counties across Tuesday and Wednesday. They are all in England or Scotland.

View 5 Images Snow depth (cm) at 9pm on November 24 (Image: WXCHARTS)

Polar vortex disruption could impact UK weather

There was a weakening and a reversal of the winds in the polar vortex at the start of this month, forecasters say, which could have an impact on our weather over the coming weeks.

This is caused by a process called sudden stratospheric warming (SSW). When temperatures in the stratosphere rise, cold air rushes downwards and can impact the jet stream, potentially creating a blocking effect and keeping cold conditions locked in place over the UK.

View 5 Images Snow depth (cm) at 3pm on November 25 (Image: WXCHARTS)

‌



SSW led to the infamous Beast from the East in 2018 - during which 22 inches of snow settled in some areas - but that doesn’t mean the same thing will happen this time around.

The Met Office said: “While the SSW could influence UK weather in the coming weeks, this is only a shift in chances rather than a guaranteed cold spell. In any case, cold weather also doesn't mean snow is inevitable, as a number of factors need to align for snow.

“For now, the polar vortex is beginning to recover, with its westerly winds strengthening again. Some longer-range model members suggest those winds could weaken again later in December, potentially raising the possibility of further disruption, but this remains a significant uncertainty.”

News.title: Salon boss fumes after dog wees on £2k Christmas display – but complaint sparks backlash
News.content:
Salon boss fumes after dog wees on £2k Christmas display – but complaint sparks backlash

Kellie Hughes, who has run Kellie Hughes Hair Nails and Beauty Emporium for 28 years, claims she spent almost £2k on her Christmas display – but was left furious after a dog urinated on her plant pot

View 5 Images Kellie Hughes was left fuming by the situation

Christmas spirit appears to be in short supply as a salon owner fumed when a dog urinated on her festive decorations. Kellie Hughes thought she was justified in posting her frustration online, but she found herself facing an unexpected backlash from people who challenged her response.

‌



‌



Kellie, 53, who has operated Kellie Hughes Hair Nails and Beauty Emporium in Whalley, Lancashire, for 28 years, invested nearly £2,000 transforming the exterior of her salon for Christmas.

‌



The mum-of-one had dedicated weeks to assembling everything, including a £180 plant pot housing a seven-foot Christmas tree adorned with baubles and artificial snow.

‌



But after stepping outside on November 9, Kellie was shocked to discover that a dog had urinated on the display.

She later posted footage of the incident online, with the video racking up more than 1.5 million views. Yet, rather than receiving widespread support, she found herself being criticised by some viewers, reports Lancs Live.

View 5 Images She subsequently shared footage of the incident online (Image: Kennedy)

‌



Kellie said: "I've had the salon for 28 years and I always decorate outside for all the seasons. Over the last three weeks I've been up every morning at 5am. I do it all myself, decorating, putting the trees in the pot.

"The pot that the dog weed on has a full 7ft decorated Christmas tree in it and has been sprayed with snow.

‌



"You can clearly see it's not a public plant pot, it's a plant pot that belongs to the salon."

She explained that she had popped inside to attend to a customer before heading back out to discover what had occurred.

‌



View 5 Images Kellie was surprised by the online backlash

"I went in the salon, did a client, I went back outside and I couldn't believe it. Somebody had let their dog wee up the plant pot, and it's my plant pot," she said.

‌



Kellie, who owns four dogs herself, insisted she would never permit her own pets to behave in such a manner outside someone else's business.

She added: "The tree was £250 and I had to get an electrician for the electric outside. It's not a dog wee station."

‌



The hairdresser subsequently cleaned the affected area but claimed the urine had caused the container to deteriorate, leaving it cracked at the base and forcing her to buy a replacement.

View 5 Images Kellie hit out at 'keyboard warriors'

‌



She was particularly taken aback by the reaction to her video, with some viewers suggesting she was blowing the situation out of proportion.

"If you look at the comments, people are asking if I'm alright," she said.

‌



"All these keyboard warriors jumped on board telling me I am not alright and that this is everything I have to worry about.

"It's not all I've got to worry about but I was astounded and shocked." Among the responses, one person wrote: "How do they stop the dog p***ing lol."

‌



View 5 Images A dog urinated on the display

Another suggested: "Just tip some water on it. It's nothing. Rain will soon wash it off. Not a lot you can do because dogs mark everything."

‌



A third commented: "Are you okay? The rain will wash it down, how do you stop a dog from weeing?" Others, however, rallied behind Kellie, with one supporter writing: "Some people just don't care, do they Kellie."

Another chimed in: "So disrespectful, hope you have a camera to see who the culprit was." While a further commenter added: "That's disgusting."

Article continues below

Despite facing criticism, Kellie maintained that her sole aim had been to make the village feel more inviting, particularly in the wake of the devastating flooding it endured in 2015.

She added: "I just wanted to decorate the village to bring it back to life after flooding in 2015. I have a passion for keeping the village looking beautiful. I wanted to bring some cheer."

News.title: Putin humiliated by Ukrainian attack on vital Russian bridge as he meets Trump and Xi
News.content:
Putin humiliated by Ukrainian attack on vital Russian bridge as he meets Trump and Xi

A third Ukrainian aerial attack in four days on the key Kerch Bridge linking Russia and illegally annexed Crimea has halted rail traffic

View 3 Images The Kerch bridge has been struck again by Ukraine (Image: EyePress News/Shutterstock)

Ukraine has struck a vital Russian bridge for the third time in four days, halting rail traffic in a move that seems calculated to embarrass Vladimir Putin as he meets Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China.

‌



‌



The latest attack on the key Kerch Bridge linking Russian and illegally annexed Crimea comes after earlier strikes shut down the road section of the landmark.

‌



The Kerch Bridge is a key route for military and civilian supplies to Crimea, which Moscow seized in defiance of international law in 2014 and uses to support frontline troops. It is a potent symbol of Russia’s illegal annexation and has been a prime target for Ukraine.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

The assault also came hours before the start of talks in Berlin on Thursday between US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky alongside European leaders.

Train traffic across the bridge stopped after the overnight strike while authorities assessed the damage but it was due to be restored starting from around 4pm local time on Thursday, the Moscow-appointed head of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, said.

‌



View 3 Images Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met today (Image: Getty Images)

Trump appears to fall asleep in front of Xi Jinping at historic summit with Putin READ MORE :

A large section of the road deck and an arch collapsed in this week’s attack that was the culmination of weeks of preparatory strikes over seven stages of the operation, according to Mr Zelensky.

‌



The Russian defence ministry said on Thursday that its air defences intercepted 53 Ukrainian drones over 10 Russian regions during the night.

Ukrainian authorities said that Russia launched anti-ship missiles and 98 drones at Ukraine, with hits recorded at 18 locations, according to the statement.

‌



At least 10 people were reported wounded as Russian strikes caused damage in 12 regions, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said.

Russia’s bigger army hopes to exhaust Ukraine on the front line through sheer weight of numbers in terms of soldiers, armour and weapons. But Kyiv’s defences are largely holding the Russians back, sapping Russian momentum with the help of drones that quickly choke off troop advances.

‌



Russia has resorted to strategic bombing to wear down Ukraine’s resistance, placing special emphasis on knocking out power ahead of winter, while Kyiv’s domestically developed long-range drones and missiles have struck deep inside Russia, often targeting its oil refineries.

View 3 Images Ukraine's attack on the Kerch Bridge seems aimed at embarrassing Putin (Image: Getty Images)

‌



In China, Mr Trump called Mr Putin “my friend”. The American president’s relationship with Mr Zelensky, meanwhile, has soured.

European leaders have tried to isolate Mr Putin diplomatically and have heavily sanctioned the Russian economy.

‌



Ukrainian officials fear their country’s fate could be determined by agreements between Mr Trump and Mr Putin, while European governments alarmed by Moscow’s aggression are trying to avoid being side-lined by Washington and Moscow.

The question of US support for Ukraine, severely curtailed under Mr Trump, could be raised by Democrats in Congress after their wins in midterm elections.

‌



Mr Kushner and Mr Witkoff have led efforts to end nearly five years of war following Russia’s all-out invasion of its neighbour and recently have mediated new discussions, though the talks have yielded no major breakthrough.

Mr Kushner said on X that Washington’s priority at Thursday’s meeting in Berlin is to “further strengthen our close co-ordination with Ukraine and Europe, work toward a unified position on the key elements of a lasting peace, and to jointly prepare the agenda and proposed format for the next round of multilateral negotiations”.

Article continues below

The meeting will also explore how Ukraine’s European backers can fit into post-war security arrangements.

Kyiv wants to ensure that Russia does not invade again, while Moscow wants to keep the Nato military alliance away from its borders.
