Since then, the prospects for expectant mothers in the West African nation have improved dramatically.

Sullaymata Saffa with her one-day-old baby girl, after travelling across Sierra Leone to use the new maternal facility Credit : Simon Townsley

According to official figures from its Ministry of Health released last month, there are now only 354 maternal deaths per 100,000 live births, a 74 per cent reduction.

While any progress is welcome, the latest data show that globally 260,000 women died during pregnancy and childbirth in 2023. The vast majority of deaths in low and middle income countries are due to infection, haemorrhage and hypertensive disorders such as pre-eclampsia – and they are entirely preventable.

Reducing these risks does not require expensive or hi-tech kit – instead access to antenatal care, emergency obstetric care and postnatal follow up could all help save women’s lives. When a mother survives childbirth, her child is significantly more likely to live, receive an education, and break out of generational poverty, strengthening the community around him or her.

An expectant mother receives an ultrasound scan at an MSF hospital Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

Sierra Leone’s success is largely due to the roll-out of free healthcare to pregnant women and children in 2010, and a more recent push to reach zero preventable maternal deaths. The 300 days of Activism for Triple Zero campaign – which also aims to tackle preventable child deaths and unvaccinated children – began in March.

According to the government, maternal deaths have dropped by 31.4 per cent since last year. There remains, however, deep inequality for pregnant women, mostly because of geographical inequity.

The United States charity Partners in Health, the lead funder for the Maternal Center of Excellence, points out that women in Sierra Leone have a one in 74 chance of dying in pregnancy or childbirth in their reproductive years. By comparison, the risk for UK women is around one in 7,500.

Despite the unparalleled progress of recent years, the happy ending which Adama and her baby have experienced is by no means universal across Sierra Leone.

A mother and her newborn recover from birth at the Maternal Center of Excellence at the Koidu Government Hospital Credit : Simon Townsley

Accounts of pregnant women dying before reaching hospital are commonplace, with deplorable road conditions and poor facilities in rural clinics often to blame.

Last month, a woman in the remote Falaba district in the far north of the country died while being taken to the local state hospital.

The first ambulance dispatched to transport her became stuck on the road, forcing health authorities to send a second ambulance. Sadly, the woman died while being transported in the replacement vehicle.

During visits to villages in the diamond-producing Kono district, the Telegraph observed how the positive official statistics do not always reflect the reality on the ground.

The busy waiting room at Koidu Government Hospital, in the east of Sierra Leone Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

The contrast between the gleaming new hospital in the regional capital Koidu and the primitive clinic in the village of Ponduru is jarring.

Our journey provides a snapshot of how arduous it can be for expectant mothers living in distant communities to reach a decent maternity unit.

For the first hour, the spine-shaking terrain prompts me to contemplate how much more painful the same trip would be for a heavily pregnant woman.

Women wait for ante-natal examinations Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

Afterwards, the churned-up mud track is so bad that we have to abandon the vehicle and walk the final mile.

Motorcycles skid and swerve through the sticky clay, but are the only form of transport for people living several hours further down the treacherous route, including pregnant women.

An ambulance that was due to visit the village during our visit never arrives because the driver is afraid it will get stuck.

It is evident that a woman needing a team of midwives and expensive monitoring equipment to assist with a complicated birth can be totally cut off during the rainy season.

On our hike, we pass women washing clothes in a flooded river while, further along, a group of men escapes the full blast of the sweltering heat in the shade of a mango tree.

Betty Abu prepares for the birth of her third child; Only two of Isha Sheriff’s four children survived Credit : Simon Townsley

Nine-months pregnant Betty Abu, 26, is sheltering inside the village clinic, preparing to give birth for the third time.

“I walked here from my own village because the road is so bad,” Betty tells me. “It took me three hours. I’ve been doing the same thing regularly for appointments because I’ve had a lot of pain.

“Even though it’s not great here it’s better than where I come from. Many women there have had miscarriages and stillbirths.”

Beside her, 29-year-old Isha Sheriff echoes this view, testifying that only two of her four children were born alive. Isha, like others, bears her tragedy with stoicism, recognising her own survival is entirely thanks to modern medicine.

Sebatu Kamara with baby Moses Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

“I had a blockage in my stomach, which caused the baby to die inside me. I also had sepsis,” explains Isha, a teacher in the village school. “They had to operate on me.

“My whole body was swollen. I could barely walk because I was so weak. But I know that I definitely would have lost my life without the treatment I was given in hospital.”

As we leave the village, I meet 23-year-old Sebatu Kamara carrying her eight-month-old baby Moses in a sling on her back.

Heavily pregnant Betty Gbortu faces the prospect of motorcycle transport Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

“I feel very lucky to have got through my pregnancy,” admits Sebatu. “There are no guarantees in a place like this. Now I can focus on my child.”

Heavily pregnant Betty Gbortu, 19, is less settled, desperately hoping that she can avoid an excruciating motorcycle trip to Koidu. She counts down the days to her admission into Ponduru’s delivery room.

If she does stay, the facilities in the clinic will be minimal. The village has a pump from a borehole, but no running water.

Community midwife Margaret Messie Seppeh admits the power supply is so unstable that she regularly depends on mobile phone torches to see during a nocturnal delivery.

The Maternal Center of Excellence is now the country’s main referral centre for high-risk pregnancies and obstetric emergencies Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

For those with the means to get there, the Maternal Center of Excellence, which is five and a half hours from the capital and biggest city Freetown, offers exemplary care.

Attached to the existing Government Hospital, it is now the main referral centre for high-risk pregnancies and obstetric emergencies for the whole country.

From the six-bed delivery ward to the intensive care unit, every part of the hospital boasts the latest foetal and maternal monitoring technology.

The facilities are so much better than other regional delivery wards that some patients travel for days on the back of a motorbike taxi to use it, including some from neighbouring Guinea. Admission is free of charge, mostly thanks to financial support from Partners in Health.

The centre boasts state-of-the-art hospital facilities Credit : Simon Townsley

Nearly half of the 2,375 women to give birth in the Maternal Center of Excellence since it opened have had emergency caesarean sections, for which a blood transfusion is routinely required.

The reason for this is that many patients – often still teenagers – have had no check-ups, so potential complications are only identified as they go into labour.

Nurse Kamara says another significant challenge is that the majority of expectant mothers have been subjected to female genital mutilation, making a natural birth more problematic.

Midwife Fatu Josephine Musa with foetal heart-rate monitors in the centre’s delivery suite Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

“Most mothers who come here have undergone this procedure,” she explains. “We can have up to 14 c-section operations a day, not including emergencies.

“Many of them had no antenatal appointments so when they arrive it is already too late for a natural birth.

“The young mothers often just don’t know what they are doing. They arrive here with a variety of obstetric problems. They are usually exhausted from the long journey too.”

A mother watches over her newborn in Sierra Leone’s first-ever neonatal intensive care unit Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

Another issue which affects maternal health is the nutritionally limited diet of mothers who depend on staples like cassava and plantain. A lack of vitamins and minerals can increase the risk of anaemia, pre-eclampsia and complications after delivery.

Lack of income prevents many from making the long journey to Koidu. For them, motorcycle taxi fares are unaffordable.

But for now, the successful results of the facility mean pregnant women are gravitating there. With no equivalent anywhere nearby, it could soon be over-capacity.

In the antenatal ward, Kadiatu Jawara, 26, says it has taken her two days to reach the sanctuary of the region’s outstanding maternity hospital from her village in Guinea.

After suffering a miscarriage in her first pregnancy, she was desperate for the reassurance it provides.

“The pregnancy has been fine, but I know there is always risk,” admits Kadiatu. “I will need a caesarean, so I feel much more confident about it being here.”

Blood donors in Ponduru – including the village chief (centre) – play a crucial role in maternal healthcare Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

At the heart of the multi-pronged approach to tackling maternal deaths in Sierra Leone is blood donation.

A scheme called Gi4SaveLife is addressing postpartum haemorrhage – when a mother loses a large quantity of blood after delivery – one of the leading causes of maternal death.

Clinics previously relied on blood donated by family members for transfusions.

Community blood donors in Ponduru Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

This precarious dependence was further complicated by cultural suspicion around blood donation in the rural areas where it is most needed.

Now, instead of desperately finding relatives willing to accompany a patient to give blood during an emergency, villages are building up their own supply.

Isatu Jimmysam, 27, discloses that she is alive only because she received two pints of blood from stocks donated by her neighbours when she delivered her baby boy Hassan earlier this year.

At a blood drive in another village outside Koidu, backed by the local Lifeline organisation, 28-year-old Kadaitu Balgale tells me she feels obliged to donate following her own experience during childbirth.

“I was given a transfusion because of complications when I had my baby,” she reveals. “My pressure went right up during labour and I collapsed. The nurses had to perform a C-section.

Moses Kpovuwa, 45, is one of the most vocal advocates for blood donation in his village after losing his sister to childbirth Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

“Now my baby is three and we are both healthy. I was lucky. I’m very happy to give blood to make sure there is enough stock for other women who have the same problem.”

“I’m doing this to help save pregnant women and their children,” affirms Osman Kamara, 32. “I have been several times after the daughter of our village chief became very ill and needed blood during labour.”

In Sierra Leone’s most isolated places, however, keeping a stock of blood is simply not feasible.

Maya died aged 25, along with her infant, after losing too much blood to be resuscitated Credit : Collect

Refrigerated storage requires stable electrical power but 95 per cent of rural areas remain off grid. Solar panels are used but are not always reliable, especially during the rainy months.

Moses Kpovuwa, 45, is one of the most vocal advocates for blood donation in his village.

His sister Maya died aged 25 after losing too much blood to be resuscitated. She had been pregnant with her third child.

“Both her and the baby died,” states Moses. “She was very strong and healthy but developed serious complications which led to her bleeding profusely. There was nothing that could be done in time.”

The introduction of portable monitoring systems which enable rural midwives to assess maternal and foetal heart rates has also brought positive results. A trial of a device called the Cradle-5, backed by King’s College London and local NGO Wellbodi Partnership, improved detection of complications such as haemorrhage, sepsis and pre-eclampsia.

In the fishing village of Tombo, a complementary endeavour linked to the blood drives has led to a steep drop in maternal and perinatal deaths.

A pregnant teenager in the isolated Ponduru village, Kono district Credit : Simon Townsley

2YoungLives is a nationwide mentoring scheme for pregnant teenagers which recruits respected older women to mentor pregnant adolescents from pregnancy until a year after birth.

Mother mentors take girls to antenatal appointments, negotiate with families, recognise danger signs, accompany them during labour and help them return to education.

Before it started, many young women were ejected from their family homes after becoming pregnant.

Ostracised from the traditional support network, they were less likely to seek medical attention until too late.

Mother mentors with their charges and the babies in Tombo Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

A 2015 survey showed one in ten pregnant teenagers had died during pregnancy or during delivery.

According to a paper published in The Lancet, 2YoungLives has reduced the number of maternal deaths, stillbirths and neonatal deaths in some areas since its creation in 2017. More than 900 pregnant young women have been mentored.

Dr Mangenda Kamara, who founded the project with Lucy November, a midwife research fellow at King’s College London, said it started because so many of Sierra Leone’s maternal deaths were among those aged under 20. Many were also victims of sexual assault, she explains.

Dr Mangenda Kamara, one of the project’s founders Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

Having become pregnant at 16 herself but then encouraged to continue school by her supportive father, Dr Kamara, now 45, is familiar with the predicament others fall prey to.

“Those who were dying were frequently from rural areas,” Dr Kamara explains. “They were often girls who were forced into sex. For example, it might be that a man would tell a girl he could help her avoid the long queue for water in return for sex.

“There are also stories of teachers and motorbike taxi riders abusing their positions in this way too. When they become pregnant, these teenagers become stigmatised and avoid seeking help.

“I took in a girl who became pregnant after being raped by her stepfather. She stayed with me until she gave birth so I could ensure there were no problems. That’s how this started.”

“Pregnant girls here are very vulnerable,” says mother-of-four Margaret Mansaray, 65, who has been part of the mentoring scheme since it started. “Their boyfriends abandon them and their families drive them out.

Margaret Mansaray, 65, has been part of the mentoring scheme since it began Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

“Most of these pregnant girls don’t want to go to clinic appointments because they are embarrassed, so one of our main jobs is to ensure that they do.

“We make sure they are tested for conditions like malaria and hepatitis, as well any issues with the pregnancy.”

Margaret has been mentoring around 10 girls every year, significantly diminishing the skyrocketing maternal death rate in Tombo.

Pregnant Saodatu Fofana, 17, with her mother-mentor Margaret Mansaray in Tombo Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

“There were so many girls dying in the past,” she continues. “My own niece died from bleeding because she was not taken to hospital in time.

“Because of that, I was very happy to do this. I knew there was a desperate need. We used to go into the communities to search for abandoned pregnant girls but now people are aware of us. They see us as role models. Some of the girls even name their children after me.”

Gathered around Margaret are the local teenagers whose lives she has protected. Mums Adama Sesay, 17, and Rahmatalai Bah, 16, sit on a stone wall holding their babies.

Although abandoned by the men who got them pregnant, they can at least look forward to watching their children grow up.

Additional reporting by Saidu Bah

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Testosterone ads banned over low sex drive claims
News.content:
Five adverts that claimed symptoms such as low energy and lack of sex drive were linked to low testosterone levels have been banned by the UK’s advertising watchdog.

An investigation by the Advertising Standards Authority (ASA), published on Wednesday, found that the adverts exaggerated the link between low testosterone and several common symptoms, including loss of motivation and changes in mood, which could have many possible causes.

The adverts, which included three posters and two paid-for Facebook ads, were created by Voy, an online health platform and prominent seller of weight loss jabs like Mounjaro and Wegovy.

The ASA said: “While some symptoms may be more closely associated with the condition, others were much less specific and shouldn’t have been presented as strong indicators of low testosterone in isolation”.

It also ruled that one Facebook ad, claiming that low testosterone affects one in four men over 30, was “misleading and not supported by the evidence Voy provided”. Voy disputed this.

“We’ve banned the ads and have told Voy to ensure that future ads don’t mislead people about the symptoms or prevalence of low testosterone,” added the ASA, who launched its investigation after receiving multiple public complaints.

Catherine Drewett, investigations manager at the ASA, said: “People should be able to trust the health claims they see in ads. This ruling makes clear the standards we expect from advertisers promoting health tests and services and the importance of ensuring their claims are supported by strong evidence”.

In response, Voy said the language in the ads was “deliberately conditional”, arguing it “did not state or imply that the advertised symptoms were definitively caused by low testosterone”.

Voy said the ads were retracted while the investigation was underway, adding that they will not run them again.

Dr Earim Chaudry, Chief Medical Officer at Voy, said: “Every patient decision at Voy is clinician-led and these campaigns were developed to align with UK advertising standards. We keep all our advertising under continual review to ensure it meets any updated guidance”.

News.title: Saucepan racks, fitted sheets and dehumidifiers: Your tricks for drying laundry in winter
News.content:
As temperatures drop and laundry piles up, drying clothes indoors can become a headache. But when Laura de Barra gave her verdict on the best heated clothes airers, Telegraph readers had a lot to say. So, we asked you what works in your homes.

While some of you have relied on heated airers for years, others have found a standard clothes horse or an overhead airer paired with a dehumidifier preferable. Several of you argue that you can’t beat the efficiency of a tumble dryer.

Here are your tried and tested tips...

Heated airers

These readers explain why they’ve relied on their heated airers for years, offer advice on what makes a good model and how to avoid damp and mould problems.



After seeing a review for the Lakeland heated airer printed in The Telegraph in 2008, Clive Ruffle, 67, from Surrey, felt enticed to buy one. “It had a price offer and a coupon to send to the newspaper,” he recalls.

“It’s still going strong and has been very useful to us,” he says. “I was quite surprised to see the dryer we bought those years back still available.”

The options to fold the airer away flat and use only half of it, where one side is folded down, are the two major features that attracted Clive to the product.

“The drying speed is good, and we’ve never felt frustrated by it,” he says. “The heated bars are very effective and if we choose to heat, clothes are usually done in the day. They take a bit longer without the heater.”

To avoid damp or mould problems, Clive keeps his upstairs windows open, “even on the coldest days,” he adds.

For a more affordable option, Caroline Morrell, 65, from Greater Manchester, recommends buying a tiered Minky heated clothes airer, which she uses with a Beldray cover.

News.title: ‘I lost my family when I contracted HIV’: why virus is still taboo in Iraq
News.content:
Hassan Mehdi never imagined that telling his family he had contracted HIV would cost him his home and his family.

The initial symptoms of the virus weren’t too worrying: a skin allergy, a rash, and swollen lymph nodes in his neck. The dermatologist told Mehdi, not his real name, that he was probably suffering from a seasonal allergy. But he then began to think about his dating and sexual history and did an HIV test at home. A faint line appeared, indicating it was positive. “I tested once again at home and got the same result,” he said.

His worst fears were then confirmed by doctors at a public HIV centre.

“Mentally and psychologically, I collapsed,” Mehdi told The Telegraph, his voice thick with pain. “I decided to take a break and leave my job as a graphic designer, and I shut myself in my room.”

The doctor urged Mehdi to tell his family about the diagnosis. He also asked him to sign a paper promising to disclose his status if he married, not to stop treatment and not get a tattoo. It also warned that he could face legal consequences if someone accused him of spreading the virus.

When he finally broke the news to his mother, he hoped she would support him. But instead, he was met with hostility.

He said: “After informing my mum, she started to spread the news with my relatives, and they warned her that if I stayed at home and mixed with them, I would infect them all. Additionally, my elder brother heard and told me: ‘If I see you in the street or anywhere else, I will kill you.’ That was the last sentence I heard from him before I packed my bag to leave home forever,” he said.

“I lost my family when I told them I had HIV,” he adds. “To a religiously extreme family, HIV/Aids is taboo,” he added.

To fight the virus and adjust to a new life away from the town where he grew up, he immersed himself in gym workouts, a strict diet, and his treatment regimen. Close friends, social gatherings, and special cultural events became his sanctuary.

Sports.title: Pochettino tells Man Utd stars ‘not to think about sleep’… in boost to Mbeumo after midnight GTA VI gaming session
Sports.content:
Next

NEW Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino has told his players “not to think about sleep” ahead of their huge Premier League clash with Liverpool on Sunday.

The 54-year-old landed in Manchester on Wednesday to begin his new job as head coach.



And in his first interview, he outlined what he expects from his men as they look to climb out of the relegation zone.

He told the official club media channel: “It’s a privilege to be head coach of Manchester United and I think we cannot be wasting time.



“We need to be ready to compete Sunday. Now it’s not thinking about rest, it’s not thinking to sleep.

“It’s to be ready and to prepare everything to be sure that we are going to compete in the best condition at Anfield.”



Some United stars may already have sleep low on their priority list – especially following the release of Grand Theft Auto VI today.

Several players have already spoken about how excited they are for the new game.

Patrick Dorgu shared on TikTok that he had downloaded it early.

Meanwhile, Bryan Mbeumo said: “The game will make myself stay at home every single day… after training!”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The United forward shared a photo of himself loading up the game late on Wednesday night.

Fans were quick to react, with one person commenting: “I’m losing sleep over Sunday. Mbeumo is just chilling playing GTA VI. This club will finish me.”

Upon his arrival at United, Pochettino said: “The best request that we can have, the players that we have, and we need to love the players that we have.

“We need to support the players, we need to provide all the tools for their performance.



“It’s only an act of responsibility now to start to work and provide them the possibility to translate all their talent on the field.”

He also insisted he is backed by the United hierarchy, adding: “I feel all the support. We feel all the support from the director and the owner.

“And of course, now it’s up to us to provide what they expect from us.

“We have a clear idea of what the club expects from us, and we want to be at the level of the demand of this football club.”

Sports.title: Glam ex-international footballer, 32, arrested after ‘laundering drug money for notorious gang with 10 relatives’
Sports.content:
DRUG BUST Glam ex-international footballer, 32, arrested after ‘laundering drug money for notorious gang with 10 relatives’







Next

A GLAMOROUS ex-international footballer has been arrested on suspicion of laundering dirty cash for a notorious narco cartel.

Francisca Gabriela Morais de Rocha, 32, known as Gabi Morais, was detained during a massive police operation targeting ruthless Brazilian drug gang Comando Vermelho.



Cops suspect the former Brazil midfielder – once nicknamed “Gabi Neymar” for her silky skills on the pitch – helped clean dirty money through a string of business fronts in her hometown of Fortaleza.

Her brother, João Paulo Carneiro de Morais, was also cuffed in dawn raids on November 17.



The siblings are the children of João Presinha, identified in local reports as a leading figure for Comando Vermelho in the north-eastern city’s Lagamar neighbourhood.

More than 10 members of the family are among dozens of suspects accused of running a sprawling criminal network in the area.



Detective Rene Mesquita, director of Ceara’s Department for Combating Money Laundering, explained: “More than 10 of the 40 people under investigation are related to each other, and they have been in the Lagamar area and surrounding neighbourhoods for a long time, I believe more than 20 years.”

Investigators are probing allegations of drug trafficking, money laundering, murder and participation in organised crime.



Cops believe gang members set up businesses selling goods and providing services to disguise profits generated by rampant drug trafficking.

They suspect Gabi laundered money through businesses and negotiated new acquisitions for the criminal gang.

Detective Mesquita said: “We identified the core of this criminal organisation, responsible for opening service companies and businesses selling products, which were used as fronts to conceal the real financial transactions, which came from drug trafficking.”



He added: “It is difficult to identify individual conduct because this is a criminal organisation, so the activities overlap.

“One person does one part, another does something else, so I cannot say exactly what any specific person did, particularly at this stage of an investigation that is still ongoing.”

The two-year probe was led by homicide detectives before financial investigators combed through bank records, tax filings and phone data.

Cops said they had identified at least 41 suspects during the investigation.

Gabi was arrested during Operation Liquidação – one of three coordinated swoops that saw cops execute 49 arrest warrants and freeze around £19.4 million in suspected cartel assets and bank accounts.



Following a custody hearing on Wednesday, a judge ordered the former Corinthians and Internacional midfielder to remain behind bars while the investigation continues.

Born in Fortaleza, Gabi played indoor football before becoming one of Brazil’s top women’s players, starring for several domestic clubs as well as enjoying spells in Portugal, with Braga and Famalicão.

She also enjoyed a stint in the US with Sky Blue.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

During a trophy-laden stint at Corinthians, she lifted back-to-back Brazilian league titles in 2022 and 2023, alongside the Copa Libertadores and Super Cup.

She represented Brazil at the 2014 Under-20 Women’s World Cup and earned senior national team call-ups before hanging up her boots in February this year.

Sports.title: Man City miss out on £1.5BILLION as major finance organisation scrap loan after guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Next

A MAJOR finance organisation has scrapped a planned £1.52BILLION loan to Manchester City.

In what appears the first repercussion of the guilty verdict from the independent commission which found the club had committed more than 100 breaches of Prem rules, US-based Apollo Global Management walked away from the deal.



Apollo, which has more than £800 billion assets under management, had been prepared to loan the cash to City’s parent company, City Football Group.

It was planned that the loan would have provided the group, which owns 12 clubs across Europe, North and South America, Australia and Asia, with extra liquidity as well as being used to refinance existing credit facilities.



CFG is understood to have significant debts in excess of £1bn and it seems likely that the plan would have been to use the Apollo loan to consolidate all of these in one package.

Some of the cash might also have gone towards the £590m cost of New York City’s new stadium in Queens, close to Flushing Meadow and immediately adjacent to the Citi Field home of the New York Mets baseball side.



But the agreement was junked in the aftermath of the commission finding that City’s commercial sponsorships were “sham” deals adding up to nearly £1bn over nine years.

City, who appealed against the commission verdict, have vehemently denied all the allegations, insisting their “comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence” would prevail and branding the ruling as “an opinion” by a panel that had bought the “Premier League’s conspiracy theories”.

That appeal – in front of a separate three-member commission – will be heard next month.

But Apollo’s decision to back out of the major financing deal seems a signal that fears over City’s risk in the wake of the commission findings have become significant.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Carrying significant debt is a common situation for football clubs and other institutions.

Indeed, the recent State of the Game report by the Independent Football Regulator found that four Prem clubs are “technically insolvent”, with the League-wide net debt estimated at more than £6bn.

Long-term, though, those debts have to be repaid and an inability to raise external funding could mean owner Sheikh Mansour having to dig further into his own reserves to meet due repayments.

Last month, following the initial 40-page outline summary of the verdict, Sheikh Mansour injected £100mn of equity into City Football Group via his Newton Investment and Development vehicle.

Should City’s eventual punishment – if their appeals fail – result in the club being relegated, financial experts believe it would put the onus on the Sheikh to make further injections.



The Apollo decision comes despite the New York-based company agreeing to take a minority stake in Mubadala Capital, the asset management arm of the Abu Dhabi sovereign fund chaired by Sheikh Mansour and run by CFC chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

Apollo have also taken a minority stake in Atletico Madrid, loaned Nottingham Forest £80m and agreed a loan of £2bn to the holding company of the New York Yankees baseball franchise.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino allowed to break little-known Premier League rule just days before Man Utd’s trip to Liverpool
Sports.content:
Next

MAURICIO POCHETTINO has been given the green light to break a Premier League rule following his arrival at Manchester United.

The Argentine, 54, was appointed as the Red Devils’ new chief following Michael Carrick’s sacking last week.



And Pochettino jetted in from the USA as he officially started his new job at Carrington on Wednesday.

Premier League bigwigs have now given the former Tottenham supremo permission to go against regulations.



Managers usually have a 1.30pm deadline on Fridays to hold their pre-match press conference.

But United came to an agreement with the Premier League to allow Pochettino to face the media at the slightly later time of 2pm instead.

It comes after the new Old Trafford supremo has had an action-packed week as he prepares to make his debut in the Red Devils’ dugout.

Pochettino guided the USA to a 2-0 win over Haiti in the Concacaf Nations League on Tuesday night.

Former Chelsea playmaker Christian Pulisic and Julian Hall found the net in Cincinnati.

And, after holding a viral post-match interview, Pochettino jumped on a flight to Manchester.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The ex-Chelsea and Southampton boss has vowed to get the United squad fighting as he prepares for a trip to arch-rivals Liverpool on Sunday.

In his first message to United fans, Pochettino said: “I am looking forward to meeting you guys. I hear so many good things about you.

“I hope we bring all the happiness, working together and connecting together.

“This is going to be a special season to support and to make our players fight on the field and to get the results we deserve.”



United went into the international break sitting in the Premier League’s relegation zone following a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

And the Red Devils could find themselves at the foot of the table by the time their clash gets underway against Liverpool.

Sports.title: Luxury two-bed apartment inside former Premier League stadium goes on the market – but do you recognise it?
Sports.content:
PITCH PERFECT Luxury two-bed apartment inside former Premier League stadium goes on the market – but do you recognise it?







Next

THIS luxury two-bedroom apartment sits atop a former Premier League stadium – but do you recognise where it is?

The impressive £1million penthouse is spread across two floors and includes a private terrace, two double bedrooms and two bathrooms.



The second floor of the jaw-dropping home boasts an open-plan kitchen, dining and reception area, complete with high-end appliances and a wine cooler.

The property is based in a luxury gated community which features underground parking, concierge facilities, an on-site gym, a swimming pool and landscaped communal gardens.



It is a home fit for footballing royalty, which makes sense given its iconic location.

The property is based in the former ground of one of England’s top teams – founded way back in 1886.



It is of course Arsenal’s former Highbury ground, where the Gunners played between 1913 and 2006.

The chain-free home, which is now on the market, is in Highbury’s original West Stand, where generations of fans stood to watch their heroes play.

The flat overlooks communal gardens on the site of the stadium’s old football pitch.

It is the same hallowed ground that Arsenal’s “Invincibles” squad played on without losing a single game during the 2003-04 season.



In a nod to Arsenal’s modern history, the property’s second balcony looks towards the team’s current Emirates Stadium.



But it is the West Stand history that will appeal most to Arsenal supporters.

Originally designed by Claude Waterlow Ferrier, it opened in 1932.

Arsenal said it cost £50,000 and was the country’s most advanced grandstand at the time, with seats for 4,000 spectators and room for another 17,000 standing.

The Gunners final game at the ground took place on 7 May 2006, when they beat Wigan Athletic 4-2 with Thierry Henry scoring a hat-trick.

The stadium was subsequently turned into more than 650 homes.



The west and east stand were part of the development, while the north and south stands were replaced with new apartment blocks.

Lastra Property Group is accepting offers of more than £1million for the 1,248 sq ft home.

There are around 234 years left on the lease, which also comes with an annual service charge of £5,450 and ground rent of £500.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino vows to lift pressure off struggling Man Utd players and build new philosophy ‘starting from zero’
Sports.content:
Next

MAURICIO POCHETTINO has vowed to lift the pressure off Manchester United’s players and build a new culture by “starting from zero”.

The new Old Trafford head coach took training for the first time at Carrington on Thursday with United rotting inside the relegation zone.



He landed in the UK on Wednesday morning after boarding an overnight private jet from Cincinnati immediately after overseeing the national team’s 2-0 victory over Haiti.

Pochettino, who signed until 2029, headed straight to Carrington where he was greeted by CEO Omar Berrada and given a tour before sitting down for his first club interview.



The Argentine has three sessions to work with his new squad, who sit 18th in the Premier League table with one win in 10 league games, before their daunting trip to Anfield on Sunday.

The 54-year-old said: “The culture is the most important. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform.



“That is the most important thing, and our priority now is to work with them and try to take [off] the pressure.

“Pressure needs to bring energy. Responsibility needs to bring energy, because if not, it’s too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back

“Culture is the most important thing and the need to create the platform for the players to feel free to express their talent.”

An advanced party of Pochettino’s coaching staff – assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeping coach Toni Jimenez and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino – travelled to Manchester last Sunday to lay the groundwork for his arrival.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

United’s players reported back to Carrington on Wednesday morning, and training was overseen by Pochettino’s staff, but he took charge of Thursday’s session and cast his eye over the squad.

On the challenge of fierce rivals Liverpool on Sunday, Pochettino said: “We need to be ready to compete Sunday and now is not the time to rest.

“It’s not to sleep, it’s not to think, it’s to be ready and to prepare everything to be sure that we are going to compete in the best condition on Anfield.”

Pochettino has faced Liverpool 19 times in his managerial career, losing 11 games, drawing five and winning three.

He added: “We need to create our own philosophy and be guide for a genuine and a very natural leadership. You start from there.



“We still need to adapt to the to the culture of the club. We need to know the identity of the club the culture the philosophy.

“And then with this sense of knowing the history of the club is to try to create all together because we are all different.

“You know a culture a philosophy that can you know respect that identity of the history of the club but at the same time if we don’t perform the responsibility is mine.

“We need to see the potential of this club and of course the circumstances and we need to be responsible for the circumstance.”

United faces deep-rooted cultural and playing-style issues that have persisted across multiple managerial regimes.



Pochettino had been considered for the United job on four occasions over the last decade and he admitted he could not turn it down when Michael Carrick was sacked, despite having been employed by the USA.

He said: “I feel really excited and so good. I think to be in place, waiting, you know, this time being in America, and I think now to be here is amazing.

“”The possibility to be a head coach of Manchester United, you cannot turn it down and I know that it’s a massive responsibility but, at the same time, that responsibility is energy, it’s excitement, it’s about giving your best and to challenge yourself

“It’s a privilege to be the head coach of Manchester United, and we cannot waste time. We need to be ready to compete Sunday.”



“Step by step. Now I am focusing to adapt here as soon as possible, very quick. Thank you to all the staff and the people and the director that make easier that adaptation in the first few hours.”

Pochettino’s determination is in large part due to one of his strong memories of the club back in 1999 when he was a player at Espanyol.

Alongside his now trusted goalkeeper coach Jimenez, Pochettino was at the Nou Camp to see United clinch the Treble against Bayern Munich.

He said: “In 1999, I was in Barcelona for that final. That was an iconic final.

“Toni Jimenez [was there] too. We were shouting for Manchester United from there. I was so excited to see Manchester United.



“This [is the] type of game that you stay sitting in your place [for] and you’re so excited because you are watching the game. That was an amazing game.

“And then what happened in the end… it’s like it’s impossible not to empathise with that team, no?

“That was an amazing memory that made me pay more attention to United, to [Sir Alex] Ferguson and the players that were there, that are all legends.”

Sports.title: Man Utd fans blast Mbeumo as he stays up late playing GTA VI hours before first training session with Pochettino
Sports.content:
Next

BRYAN MBEUMO has been brutally blasted by Manchester United fans after revealing he was playing Grand Theft Auto VI past midnight.

The winger, 27, prioritised binging the new video game just hours on from new Old Trafford supremo Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival.



Mbeumo, who is pushing to be at the forefront of the Argentine’s plans following Michael Carrick’s sacking, posted a snap on Instagram Stories.

The photo, which was shared in the early hours of Thursday, showed the Grand Theft Auto VI title screen.



And United fans were fuming when they spotted Mbeumo’s social media post a matter of days before a crunch clash with arch-rivals Liverpool.

One said: “This is why we are in the relegation zone, unserious players.”

Another added: “I’m losing sleep over Sunday. Mbeumo is just chilling playing GTA VI. This club will finish me.”

A third chimed in: “No wonder we’re s***. Players not getting enough sleep when they’re supposed to be pro athletes.”

A fourth bluntly noted: “Look at what my players are doing.”

And a fifth vented: “We are 18th in the Premier League. Not saying players can’t have a life but our players need to focus.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But Pochettino, 54, has told his squad now is not the time to be worried about sleeping patterns.

The new United supremo said: “I think it’s an opportunity. It’s a privilege to be head coach of Manchester United and I think we cannot waste time.

“We need to be ready to compete on Sunday. Now it’s not the time to think about rest. It’s not the time to think about sleep.

“We need to be ready and prepare everything to be sure that we are going to compete in the best condition at Anfield.”

Mbeumo had already warned the release of Grand Theft Auto VI would lead to him being cooped up at home.



In a viral interview, where the Cameroonian showed he had pre-ordered the video game, he admitted: “I think [my favourite] would be GTA.

“I’m just waiting now. The game will make me stay at home every single day – after training.”

Mbeumo’s United team-mate Patrick Dorgu also logged onto TikTok to show he had Grand Theft Auto VI downloading onto his Playstation 5.



And Liverpool striker Alexander Isak previously revealed he was looking forward to the video game’s release.

The former Newcastle marksman said: “I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from November 19, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the plan.”

But Old Trafford legend Gary Neville is baffled by Grand Theft Auto VI and hated pals pulling all-nighters.

He told Stick to United: “I’ve never played a computer game. Do you know what I used to play when I was younger?

“You know when the shapes come down and you try and fit them in – Tetris. That’s the only game I’ve played.

“I hated football players playing computer games. They stay up until two or three in the morning playing them.

“And that’s just not good for you. I hated the idea of getting into something and you’re addicted to it.”

Sports.title: Mykhailo Mudryk points finger of blame over failed drugs test that led to Chelsea ban
Sports.content:
Mykhailo Mudryk points finger of blame over failed drugs test that led to Chelsea ban

Mykhailo Mudryk has opened up on the challenges he faced during his suspension for a failed doping test after finally getting the green light to return to football in the summer

View 2 Images Mykhailo Mudryk has spoken about his failed drugs test (Image: Ed Sykes/Allstar)

Mykhailo Mudryk has blamed the Ukrainian national federation for the failed drugs test which cost him more than a year-and-a-half of his career.

‌



‌



The Chelsea winger, currently on loan at Tottenham, was suspended in November 2024 after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium. He was initially handed a four-year ban by the Football Association before a successful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport. Mudryk's suspension was lifted in July 2026 after accepting he had breached anti-doping rules and agreeing to a suspension which was equivalent to the time he had already been out of action.

‌



Mudryk, 25, has been speaking about his 20-month ban on the Ukrainian YouTube channel, Guest of Gordon. In a wide-ranging interview, Mudryk, who believes the banned substance entered his system while on international duty, made it clear that he held the national team responsible for the ban when asked.

‌



“The environment, the situation in the Ukrainian national team,” he replied. “It should never have existed. I probably haven't said it publicly yet, but I'm saying it now.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



“I had never heard of a drug like meldonium. It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England.”

Mudryk continued to say he had only been in Ukraine with the national team, which “points to the fact it was in a national team camp”. When he was then pressed on if he blamed the national team, Mudryk replied: “Yes, exactly.”

‌



Mudryk went on to reveal that he spent millions of pounds on legal fees in a bid to clear his name. He said that he cried and turned to alcohol when he learned of the initial suspension.

View 2 Images Mudryk joined Tottenham on loan in the summer following his suspension (Image: Maynard Manyowa/News Images)

‌



He added: “It was a bolt from the blue. I couldn't believe it [the positive test] was true.

“It was like falling off a skyscraper. In a dream you would hit the ground. In life, I just kept on falling. It hit me very hard, mentally.”

‌



After being given the green light to return to football, Mudryk joined on Tottenham on loan for the season after being urged to go and play by Chelsea's head coach, Xabi Alonso, who also offered him a lifeline with the Blues.

“[Alonso] told me straight up to my face: ‘You had better go and play and get some minutes then come back. I am counting on you.’”

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino immediately confirms his top priority in first words as Man Utd boss
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino says only instilling the right type of culture will enable Manchester United to become successful again after officially taking charge at Old Trafford.

The Argentine has become the eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013, with the club at their lowest ebb since the legendary Scot's appointment 40 years ago. The Red Devils find themselves in the Premier League relegation zone having picked up just one win from their opening 10 Premier League matches. That form was enough to see Michael Carrick's time in the Old Trafford dugout ended, less than six months after his permanent appointment.

Pochettino faces a daunting start to his tenure, as he takes his new players to Anfield to face their old rivals Liverpool on Sunday. And preparations for the trip to Merseyside have also been impacted by the 54-year-old opting to stay in his post as USA national team manager for both of their fixtures during the current international break.

His final game charge didn't finish until the early hours of Wednesday morning, with Pochettino flying to Manchester immediately after and touching down in Carrington by Wednesday afternoon.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Speaking to Manutd.com, Pochettino immediately pinpointed culture, saying it is “the most important thing” before addressing the club's perilous position in the Premier League. “It's a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club,” Pochettino said.

“Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it's a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free.

‌



View 3 Images Pochettino arrived at Manchester United on Wednesday (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

“The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now – it’s to work with them and try to take the pressure.

“Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it's too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back. When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your team-mates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

“That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff - we were talking a lot today. Then to settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero.

‌



“I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.”

View 3 Images Pochettino replaces Michael Carrick at Old Trafford (Image: Manchester United)

Pochettino added: “We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us to be close to winning every single game.”

Reports have indicated that Pochettino will be back in the winter transfer window with United's beleaguered squad failing to live up to expectations this season. But the former Chelsea and Tottenham manager has already talked up his newly inherited players.

‌



“The best squad that we can have are the players that we have and we need to love the players that we have. We need to support the players,” Pochettino added.

“We need to provide all the tools for them to perform. We cannot blame no-one. It's only to an act of responsibility now to start to work and provide them the facility to translate all their talent on the field.”

Sports.content:
Premier League agree to relax rule ahead of Mauricio Pochettino's first Man Utd match

Mauricio Pochettino will lead Manchester United for the first time at Anfield on Sunday, following a whirlwind week which saw him fly through the night into the United Kingdom

View 2 Images New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United FC)

Premier League bosses have reached an agreement with Manchester United, allowing Mauricio Pochettino to conduct his first press conference beyond the established deadline.

‌



‌



The Argentine was officially named as United's new manager last Friday, replacing Michael Carrick who was sacked after just one win from 10 top-flight matches this season. But due to his commitments with the USA national team, Pochettino didn't arrive in Manchester until Wednesday afternoon.

‌



He flew from America to the United Kingdom in the early hours of Wednesday morning, following the USA's win over Haiti in his final match in charge of the country. After landing in Manchester, he immediately reported to Carrington, where he met a small number of players, along with the United powerbrokers.

‌



He then completed in-house media commitments for an interview which will go live across the club's official channels on Thursday. He will then meet the assembled press on Friday, as he previews the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday.

As per Premier League rules, those press conferences must take place by 1.30pm on a Friday at the latest. However, after discussions it has been agreed he may start his at 2pm due to the unusual circumstances surrounding his arrival, reports the Manchester Evening News.

“I'm very excited to be there, it's an honour, it's a privilege to be in this amazing club. Yes, I'm looking forward to start to work," Pochettino told United's club media yesterday.

They have taken training in the early part of the week, with the manager himself overseeing things for the first time on Thursday.

Sports scientist Sebastiano Pochettino began working on his father's backroom staff during his time in charge of Tottenham. He has also joined United and is expected to work alongside strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya.

Former USMNT analyst Alec Scott has also followed Pochettino to Manchester after working with him in the US.

Sports.title: Barcelona chief officially gives green light for Liverpool to complete £47m transfer
Sports.content:
Barcelona chief officially gives green light for Liverpool to complete £47m transfer

Barcelona sporting director Deco has opened the door for Liverpool to complete a permanent move for Ronald Araujo next summer

View 3 Images Ronald Araujo and Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola (Image: Liverpool FC, Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Barcelona sporting director Deco has revealed the club are completely open to discussing a permanent move for Ronald Araujo following his loan spell at Liverpool.

‌



‌



And the Barca chief has praised on-loan Reds defender Araujo for adapting "seamlessly" to life on Merseyside since his August arrival.

‌



Araujo has impressed since his summer switch from Barcelona, predominantly featuring at right-back under Andoni Iraola's guidance, with the club currently sitting fourth in the Premier League.

‌



Since the Uruguay international has been used on the right side of defence, Liverpool have conceded just six goals across eight Premier League matches. Half of which came in the 3-0 defeat to Manchester City after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off.

‌



Liverpool have the option to sign Araujo permanently at the end of the season for £47m, and Deco, the former Chelsea and Portugal playmaker, confirmed the La Liga giants are willing to complete a permanent sale, reports the Liverpool Echo.

"I think, first of all, I think [with] Ronald, both (assistant) Bojan and I have been through quite a lot with him over the last few years," Deco told 3cat radio station. "Personally, I'm happy for him.

‌



"Aside from football, we work at Barca - we want the best for the club, we have to win, we want the best squad - but at the end of the day we stay up to date and we also want to build relationships.

"Ronald has been a captain in recent years. He's had difficult moments at the club, but also happy moments. In recent years he has been one of the leaders and idols at Barca.

‌



Black Friday special! Click here to sign up to Mirror+ for just £1 a month!

View 3 Images Iraola has seen his defence improve since using Araujo on the right side (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images)

‌



"That's why we go back a bit to the dynamic - the playing dynamic wasn't the best for him. He makes his own decision, we respect it, and the manager does too.

"And for us, the most important thing, above all else, is to see a player who has recovered, who is happy, and who is in a positive dynamic in his sporting career.

‌



"If later on he decides to stay there, there is a buy option on Liverpool's part, since they know perfectly well what they have to do or not, and I believe they will make the decision at the right time."

Araujo accepted a wage cut in a bid to revive his career by moving to Liverpool in August, and Deco suggested that discussions between the Reds and the 27-year-old defender would still be required if they opt to make the move permanent.

‌



The Barcelona chief continued: "If everything goes down that path, Ronald is doing well, he's happy, and he decides to stay there, because they also have to negotiate with him. It's no longer just a matter of paying the clause and it works out well for us.

View 3 Images Deco has opened the door for Araujo to join Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"We'll be happy for several reasons: because things worked out, because Ronald is happy, because it went well for us - he helped us during his time at Barca.

"And on top of that he continued his sporting career seamlessly. Seamlessly and happily, because football is a bit like that.

‌



"Sometimes the dynamic isn't the best, yet we still want someone to succeed when the time comes - and of course, if the money comes in, that wouldn't be bad either, so we'll see.

"He has a date to execute the option, as we have had when we bring in loaned players. Then you can try to negotiate, you can work, it will depend on our moment, on the player, some things now."

Sports.title: 'These are the best 25 players I've ever seen live' - join the debate
Sports.content:
JOHN CROSS: It is a fiendishly difficult, horribly biased, and incredibly skewed task - but I've chosen the players that have thrilled me and enhanced my deep love of football

'These are the best 25 players I've ever seen live' - join the debate

I've been reporting on football for more than 25 years - but in the last few months I've written about England's best ever away performance with the 3-2 World Cup win over Mexico; the greatest individual major tournament from an Englishman since 1966 in Jude Bellingham; and the first English Ballon d'Or winner for a quarter of a century in Harry Kane.

So it was time for me to rank the greatest players I've ever seen live.

Read my list, watch their iconic goals and moments, and get involved in the conversation in the comments.

Sports.title: Arsene Wenger left red-faced as 'daylight' offside proposal set to be axed
Sports.content:
Arsene Wenger left red-faced as 'daylight' offside proposal set to be axed

A new offside proposal from the legendary former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger is now unlikely to be given the green light after an underwhelming trial in Canada

View 2 Images Arsene Wenger's daylight offside rule has not impressed (Image: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images)

The proposed new 'daylight' offside rule proposed by Arsene Wenger is set to be scrapped - with even the legendary former Arsenal manager not impressed after it was implemented in a trial.

‌



The Canadian Premier League was chosen as the testing ground for the proposal, which works on the basis that there must be clear daylight between an attacker and a defender for the former to be declared offside.

Although Wenger's proposal had the potential to wipe out tight offside calls in the future, The Times report that it will not be recommended for use by the International FA Board.

Results from the trial, which spanned 108 games, were presented to the game's law-makers, who discovered that the altered rule only 'made things worse', with most teams adopting deeper defensive lines to combat the proposal.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

While the number of offside decisions fell by more than half, there was no significant increase in goals scored. Only 13 goals were scored by players who would have been deemed offside outside of the daylight trial.

As well as confirming even Wenger failed to be impressed by the results of the trial, a source told the outlet: “The consensus was that the daylight offside doesn’t work. The defences dropped much deeper and there were not many more goals scored - and some of those that were scored looked weird.

“It was frustrating for the players too. This is not the way forward.”

View 2 Images Wenger has been tipped to rival Gianni Infantino for the Fifa presidency in recent weeks (Image: ANP/Shutterstock)

Wenger, who won three Premier League titles during his historic Arsenal tenure, became Fifa's head of global football development back in 2019.

He had recently been touted as a potential rival to Gianni Infantino for the top job at Fifa following a chastening year for the incumbent president. However, it emerged earlier this week that Wenger has opted against rivalling Infantino in his bid to be re-elected.

Wenger would have received the backing of Uefa had he decided to run for the presidency after they called on Infantino to resign earlier this year. Instead, Philippe Diallo, the president of the French football federation, will be Uefa's preferred candidate.

Sports.title: The cost of Arsenal's great player retention drive - and what comes after
Sports.content:
Regardless of what transpires between now and May, nobody can accuse Arsenal of standing still in the wake of their Premier League success last year.

The Gunners have followed up on their first domestic title in more than two decades by positioning themselves even further ahead of their elite rivals. Already, they are the overwhelming favourites to lift English football's most coveted prize aloft at the end of the season. And they once again look a real force on the continent after the most heartbreaking of conclusions to their bid to seize a maiden European crown last time out.

A major factor of Arsenal's current rude health is the shrewd work they have undertaken in terms of managing their contract churn. A flurry of renewals has strengthened Mikel Arteta's hand no end as the Gunners chase greatness.

Bukayo Saka is the poster boy for the movement: a top-class, homegrown player committing his prime years to the club in exchange for handsome renumerations in the region of £300,000-a-week. But Arsenal's operation preceded him; Gabriel and William Saliba, the cornerstone of Arsenal's imperious defence, signed on again last year. Myles Lewis-Skelly has also re-signed. And it emerged this week that Declan Rice will also enter the upper echelons of the club's pay bracket after agreeing a new deal. which brings him almost in line with Saka. David Raya, Jurrien Timber and Piero Hincapie are also poised to follow suit. Others are likely to follow, if you don't get the picture by now.

‌



That leaves Arteta very much looking like the cat who got the cream. The nucleus of a title-winning team all locked down as they approach their prime? We're approaching Football Manager territory.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

The caveat to this impressive operation of player retention - which will at some point bite - is the cost associated with such a strategy. Even a goliath of the game such as Arsenal cannot ignore the numbers and enhanced contracts for so many key figures, not to mention a meaty new reported £20million salary for their title-winning manager, too, is quite the significant outlay. And that's without taking into account the natural side-effects of a team growing older together.

‌



Player trading may seem like the obvious answer to offsetting the cost of these significant contracts. But that is not without risks. It will undoubtedly lead to difficult decisions in terms of personnel - and potentially sooner rather than later given the ages of some of the key players Arsenal have yet to lock down to fresh terms.

View 3 Images Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka have both agreed lucrative new contracts with Arsenal (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Captain Martin Odegaard is a prime example. Turning 28 next month and with 18 months remaining on his deal, it is effectively stick or twist time for the Norway international. If Arsenal decide Odegaard will not be joining his peers in having his terms extended, then selling your captain in his prime - and just as he appears to have rediscovered top form - is a hard sell. But it's a scenario they may have to play ball with if they are to remain in a position of power long-term. Particularly as they will need to rebalance their squad in future transfer windows with new heroes as father time joins the Premier League elite in chasing their current stars.

Another element is Arsenal's track record in sales. It is, perhaps, the one area the club have failed to substantially improve upon in the years where they have re-established themselves as a leading force in the game.

‌



Arsenal have simply generated nowhere near enough from selling players in the past, particularly when you compare their activity to their elite rivals in the Premier League. That Gabriel Martinelli became the club's record sale at £55.7million when he departed for Al-Hilal in the final hours of the summer window is telling. The fact that prior to his move Arsenal's sale high was £35m is an even more damning reflection on their previous body of work in the market. If it continues, Arsenal will have no wriggle room in those challenging decisions.

View 3 Images David Raya is among a group of Arsenal players who are expected to follow Rice and Saka in signing new deals (Image: Julian Finney/Getty Images)

Andrea Berta will be the man primarily responsible for transforming the club on that front. Their recent success should naturally translate itself to more lucrative sales, with successful players more likely to prove far more desirable to potential suitors. But it would be naive just to expect the issue to simply solve itself based off the team's continued success alone. Arsenal will need to be more savvy in the market in the future to sustain their recaptured influence and power. And once a club has a reputation in the market, be it cheap sellers or over-payers, it can be hard to shift, as other English clubs have discovered.

Arsenal felt like a club operating in the here and now in the summer; the failure to land the world-class attacker Arteta craved may have stung, deals but for Ezri Konsa and Bruno Guimaraes were not done to lay foundations for the future. Not with the next five years in mind, rather the upcoming 18 months.

‌



There is nothing wrong with that approach. And given the current status of Arsenal's elite rivals in the Premier League, it may even be very likely to yield further titles and accolades. And for Arteta to create the dynasty he craves.

But the picture for the future will have to come into sharper focus soon - and one that is considered carefully given the vast sums of money tied up in this team.

Arsenal may very well be approaching a new golden era; one that maybe even lives up to the glorious Arsene Wenger days of old. What comes after won't be straightforward or cheap.

Sports.title: Harmer stars as South Africa beat Bangladesh
Sports.content:
Simon Harmer ran through Bangladesh's tail and South Africa knocked off the 12 runs required to win the first Test by nine wickets on Thursday, taking a 1-0 lead in the teams' two-match series.

The win sees the Proteas edge closer to securing a spot at the World Test Championship final at The Kia Oval in 2027, with the defending champions having dethroned Australia to go top of the ICC rankings following their series win last month.

Resuming on 100-5 at the Wanderers, Bangladesh's lower-order batters couldn't handle the off-spin of Harmer, who took four of the remaining five wickets to help dismiss the tourists for 168 and return figures of 6-51.

Image: South Africa bowled Bangladesh out for 168

It revived memories of Harmer taking 6-16 on day five of the series-clinching victory over Australia last month.

"I don't think I bowled my best this match," Harmer told SuperSport.

"But I'm very aware of the way cricket works; you're going to have days where you bowl well and don't necessarily get rewards.

"Sometimes you don't bowl as well as you should, but you end up getting wickets.

"It would have been tricky if we were chasing 150 or 170. To be able to restrict them and get wickets in the third innings is enjoyable and it's always nice to contribute."

Image: Harmer returned fourth-innings figures of 6-51 but felt he had not bowled at his best

There is bad news for South Africa, though, who are likely to be without their captain Temba Bavuma for the second Test, live on Sky Sports, with the skipper still struggling to overcome a fitness issue.

The Proteas lost first-innings century-maker Marques Ackerman - for a second-ball duck - on the way to reaching their target before lunch at 12-1. Soon after getting bowled off a no-ball, Aiden Markram (8 not out) scored the winning run.

In Harmer, South Africa have a 37-year-old player enjoying a renaissance in a Test career that was drifting until a year ago, when he returned after a two-and-a-half-year absence. He is now a reliable match-winner.

Having already removed Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mahfijul Islam late on day four, Harmer took the final four wickets of the match in his brilliant four-over burst that came after overnight batter Litton Das got an inside edge and played onto his own stumps off Kagiso Rabada (3-46).

Mushfiqur Rahim added 34 runs to his overnight five before gloving Harmer to a close fielder, for a dismissal that was only given after the Proteas reviewed a not-out call.

Image: Mehidy Hasan Miraz was stumped by South Africa's Ryan Rickelton

In his next over, Harmer had Mehidy Hasan Miraz stumped for four before removing Hasan Mahmud (4) and Ebadot Hossain (0) in consecutive balls to wrap up the innings.

Despite making 400 in the first innings after winning the toss, Bangladesh barely avoided an innings defeat.

Sports.title: Consistently inconsistent? Ten things we've learnt about Alonso's Chelsea so far
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso's Chelsea project is 10 Premier League games in. Here's what we've learnt so far...

1 - Could Mike Penders become the preferred option to No 1 Emi Martinez?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders shows off quick reflexes to deny Leeds with a brilliant double save

Goalkeeper has been a long-standing problem position at Chelsea. Xabi Alonso spoke positively about his keeping options after taking charge but a night to forget for Robert Sanchez at Fulham in the Spaniard's first game in charge pushed the club into action. The 2022 World Cup winner Emiliano Martinez seemed like a no-brainer. However, the 34-year-old let three goals in on his debut against Brighton and hasn't looked totally assured.

An injury to the Argentine has created an opportunity for the highly rated Mike Penders. A calamitous own goal for the 21-year-old against Spurs was a terrible way to mark his first Premier League start but his response has been impressive. It is food for thought that Penders has a positive Expected Goals Against vs Actual Goals Conceded ratio (4.49 vs only three let in). Martinez's return is negative - 11 goals conceded from shots worth 9.17.
