Get all 6 right and the jackpot is yours! Make your weeks predictions and beat our pundits.

Ji-sung Park is the definition of underrated

Max then picked the player he thinks is the 'definition of underrated' and a trailblazer for Asian players in England.

"From 2005 to 2012, Park won 11 major trophies with Man United, which included four Premier League titles and a Champions League.

"Possibly the most versatile and trusted player to ever play under Alex Ferguson, and that's a big claim. Fergie absolutely loved him.

"He only scored 28 goals and provided 24 assists in his career, but it's the energy, the work rate, the professionalism, work off the ball and ability to play everywhere.

"Of course, there are some players like that nowadays, but if you think of players who play for the elite clubs, clubs that are challenging for titles, I struggle to think of a player who can play as many positions as Ji-sung Park.

"He was an icon. Not just at Man United, but in South Korean football, he's a real statesman-like figure there and he deserves it."

6 Park was never a goalscoring player, but he played a crucial role for Man United under Sir Alex, winning all sorts of titles Credit: AFP

6 Muller is one of the greatest goalscorers of his generation and could have received more credit if it wasn't for Messi and Ronaldo Credit: Getty

Overshadowed by Messi and Ronaldo

Of course, as it's Mount Rushmore Or Less, so Max wanted to make space for another in a big list of underrated stars.

He opted against forcing in someone from his beloved Nottingham Forest, while he also considered Gilberto Silva, Mousa Dembele and Michael Carrick - but Thomas Muller gets the nod.

"I don't even know where his best position is given he plays everywhere across that front line," Max said of Muller.

"His stats are absolutely unbelievable, not only has he won 13 Bundesliga titles, two Champions Leagues... he's won the World Cup with Germany in 2014 and scored 250 goals for Bayern Munich.

"He's an absolute legend. And the brilliant thing about Muller is he doesn't look like a footballer. He's a bit lanky, doesn't look particularly strong, look particularly mobile or rapid.

"But the longevity, the output, the class and the brilliance... I've loved watching him play, and he's such an amazing character.

"He's hugely underrated, maybe that's just because he existed in that Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo era where we were obsessed debating who is the best out of them two, when actually, you had world class players like Muller."

Sports.title: Mark Cuban makes decision on buying MLS franchise with $6.8bn fortune as relegation debate rages
Sports.content:
Mark Cuban makes decision on buying MLS franchise with $6.8bn fortune as relegation debate rages

Mark Cuban inserted himself into a debate about the pros and cons of relegation.

But the NBA Finals-winning owner also stumbled into several excellent points about why inserting relegation into United States sports isn't as easy as it sounds.

5 Mark Cuban had a different opinion than Mauricio Pochettino Credit: AFP

Will NBA Finals-winning owner buy MLS team?

Cuban also gave a one-word answer about his desire to purchase a Major League Soccer team.

"Thinking about buying an MLS team?" a fan asked Cuban, whose net worth is estimated at $6.8 billion.

"No," posted Cuban, who won the NBA Finals with the Dallas Mavericks in 2011.

But it was another series of questions that drew even more interest from fans, especially after Cuban ended up in a back-and-forth about relegation tied to Mauricio Pochettino's recent comments.

Pochettino, who recently left USMNT for Manchester United, blasted the lack of relegation and promotion in US soccer.

"If you start in MLS and you haven’t won a game in three months and you’re at the bottom, what’s the consequence if there’s no promotion or relegation, no international competition?" Pochettino said.

That drew Cuban's attention on social media.

"One key reason why relegation doesn't work in American sports is because of the draft," Cuban posted.

"In Europe they develop players in academies. Sign them younger and younger. Pay transfer fees to try to get better."

The 68-year-old Shark Tank star then asked Grok a series of questions on X.

5 Pochettino thinks that MLS needs relegation to improve Credit: Getty

5 Cuban has also made a decision about buying an MLS team Credit: Getty

"What are the 5 least valuable teams in the MLS vs the 5 least valuable teams in the Premier League, and the 5 least valuable teams in La Liga?" Cuban wrote.

"And what is the typical change in valuation when a team is relegated?"

Grok replied with financial information that might upset Burnley fans and diehard supporters of inserting relegation into US sports.

"MLS (Forbes 2026): CF Montréal $440m, Vancouver Whitecaps $445m, Colorado Rapids $450m, Orlando City $475m, Real Salt Lake $510m," Grok replied on X.

"PL (2025-26 estimates): Burnley ~$280m, Bournemouth ~$385m, Wolves ~$400m, Sunderland ~$450m, then Forest/Brentford ~$500m.

5 Lionel Messi joined MLS but the league can't compete with the Premier League financially Credit: AFP

"La Liga bottom clubs (limited full valuations) typically sit $150-350m range (Alavés, Getafe, Osasuna etc.); only Atleti cracks top global lists at $2.95B.

"Relegation typically cuts club value 20-40% short-term (revenue drop ~$90-100m net in PL after parachutes; squad value often -30%). Cumulative multi-year hit $200m+."

The NBA could eventually consider adding relegation and promotion after NBA Europe is unveiled.

But The Association is almost guaranteed to never create a ladder system with college basketball and the NCAA.

The same for the NFL, which makes $23 billion in annual revenue and is the richest sports league in the world, but doesn't relegate or promote any of the league's 32 teams.

Another Grok response also appeared to back Cuban's point that relegation wouldn't work in MLS.

5 LeBron James has never had to worry about relegation or promotion in the NBA Credit: Getty

Burnley is worth $160m less than Montreal, according to the 2025-26 estimates, but the current Championship club almost quadrupled Montreal's revenue and had significantly better fan attendance.

"MLS (Forbes 2025 rev / 2026 att): Montréal $48m/14.7k, Whitecaps $46m/25.2k, Rapids $50m/19.2k, Orlando $50m/20.1k, RSL $54m/20.7k," Grok posted.

"PL lower (est full rev / 25-26 att): Burnley ~$190m/21k, Bournemouth ~$240m/11k, Wolves ~$230m/30k, Sunderland ~$220m/47k, Forest ~$200m/30k."



Will Gavin, Brian T. Smith, former NFL star Efe Obada and a collection of special guests debate the biggest talking points across the NFL, soccer, NBA and more.

Sports.title: BBC and Sky Sports female rugby pundit is cleared of sexually assaulting woman by putting hand up her skirt in cricket club toilet
Sports.content:
A former England rugby player and pundit has been cleared of sexually assaulting a woman.

Danika Priim, 42, was accused of putting her hand up the skirt of a woman in a cricket club bathroom.

Today, the BBC and Sky Sports pundit has been found not guilty following a trial at Leeds Crown Court.

During the trial, the woman claimed that Priim had twice reached up her dress and grabbed her underwear at Horsforth Cricket Club in the city on July 22 2022.

Two of the complainant's friends also claimed to have witnessed the incident with one saying Priim laughed and said 'wahey' before walking out of the toilet.

On Thursday a jury of seven women and five men cleared her of sexual assault after deliberating for just more than two hours.

Priim, and her family and friends in the public gallery, sobbed as the verdict was announced.

During a three-day trial at Leeds Crown Court, the complainant told the jury she had washed her hands, put on some lipstick and was talking to two of her friends when Priim 'walked straight up to me and put her hand up my skirt and grabbed hold of my pants and my private parts'.

Danika Priim (pictured), 42, was accused of putting her hand up the skirt of a woman in a cricket club bathroom

The woman said: 'I said: 'What the f*** are you doing?'

'Then she did it again, grinning at me, and walked off.'

Two of the complainant's friends told the jury they saw Priim put her hand up the woman's skirt.

One of them said she exchanged text messages with her friend the following day in which she encouraged the woman to report what had happened, saying she would support her.

Priim told the jury she was never in the toilets with the three women and the sexual assault 'categorically did not happen'.

Asked why she thought three women would have 'got together to make completely false allegations', Priim said: 'It's the biggest question I have – it's the why.'

She told the court: 'I'm also a very happy heterosexual woman. I'm with a man. I live with a man.'

Priim, 42, of Keighley, West Yorkshire, played for Bradford Bulls, Leeds Rhinos and represented England, including at the 2017 World Cup.

She retired from the game in 2021 and she told the jury she has appeared on BBC, Channel4 and Sky Sports as a pundit, reporter and commentator.

This is a breaking news story, more to follow.

Sports.title: Arsenal's dynasty drive behind their raft of new contracts: Why stars are desperate to play for Mikel Arteta, the ultimatum he gives each of them and the dilemma over whether to extend Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz
Sports.content:
Arsenal's dynasty drive behind their raft of new contracts: Why stars are desperate to play for Mikel Arteta, the ultimatum he gives each of them and the dilemma over whether to extend Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz

Secure the king, and the rest will follow.

Much of the attention surrounding Arsenal in recent months was on Mikel Arteta’s contract, which had been due to expire next summer. Behind the scenes, sporting director Andrea Berta lined up the Spaniard’s new four-year deal, which he signed in October, all the while keeping one eye on the players central to the club's long-term vision.

News of new contracts for Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber, David Raya and Piero Hincapie all broke in the past 72 hours. Extending players when they're approaching the final two years of their contract isn't revolutionary, but the spate of them in such quick succession drew the eye.

Most of the deals have been months in the making – talks over Rice’s new contract stretch back to at least March, for example. It also comes after Real Madrid having monitored Rice and Raya for the past year, and Barcelona trying to lure Hincapie away back in June.

But why now?

This push is central to Arsenal’s desire to forge a dynasty by securing the nucleus of this team for at least the next four years of Arteta's reign, following Gabriel, William Saliba and Bukayo Saka all signing long-term contracts last year.

Arsenal are closing in on new contracts for (L-R) David Raya, Declan Rice and Jurrien Timber, after also tying down Gabriel and William Saliba last year

Piero Hincapie (left) is also set to agree new terms, with the rush of extensions coming after manager Mikel Arteta (right) signed a four-year deal last month

An agent who has previously dealt with Arsenal revealed why the strategy is beneficial to multiple parties.

He told Daily Mail Sport: ‘They are maintaining the value of their players and ensuring squad continuity, to avoid the possibility of disruption. Now Mikel has got the right blend of players and got rid of the agitators (from earlier in his reign), he wants to keep the group solid.

‘Too many clubs leave it too late when it comes to contract extensions and sometimes agents are happy to let a contract run down so they can renew from a position of strength. Signing-on fees for both the agent and player, higher wages and commission can be boosted.

‘Though on the flipside, an agent can renegotiate a contract with two more years remaining and say: “If you want us to extend now, we want signing bonuses et cetera”. It also provides further long-term security for your client. It’s smart business all round. Arsenal are champions, the players are happy, why wouldn’t you extend?’

Rice benefits the most – his pay rise will take him very close to Saka, Arsenal’s top earner, with the winger on a deal worth £350,000 a week.

Now, though, comes the tricky part: who of the remaining first-team squad do they want to commit to? Extending every senior player’s contract in a Premier League world governed by Squad Cost Ratio rules is not particularly feasible. The plan to make up to 60 job cuts across the club, for instance, is a reminder of the general financial stakes at play.

The biggest decisions are on the futures of Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, both of whom have contracts expiring in 2028. One is the club’s captain, and the other is Arteta’s favourite son.

The injuries and dip in form of the two men last season could be why Arsenal may bide their time. Odegaard managed just 16 league starts with shoulder, knee and muscular problems disrupting his campaign, having also missed a large chunk of the season before with an ankle problem.

Kai Havertz (second left) and club captain Martin Odegaard (second right) are the next big decisions for Arteta. Both are key men but is the time right to capitalise on their sale value?

Havertz's season was even more frustrating, suffering a knee injury on the opening day which required surgery, before subsequent muscular setbacks. He played 90 minutes just once in the title-winning campaign.

Both remain important to Arteta, but their previous injuries and potentially strong sale value makes committing to improved long-term contracts a more difficult financial decision.

Mikel Merino’s deal expires in 2028, but he is not in the same financial or importance bracket as the above two stars. Ben White’s contract is also up in 2028, but there is an option to trigger a 12-month extension. This group are all in or approaching their peak years: Odegaard and Havertz are 27, White is 29 and Merino is 30.

Given most of the players who have agreed new long-term contracts will be past 30 by the time their deals expire, there has to be an awareness of not letting this squad get too old. The average age of Arsenal's starting XI in the Premier League this season is exactly 27 years old. Manchester United (27 years and 86 days) are the only Big Six side whose XIs have been older, while perennial rivals Manchester City are 480 days younger per player.

More broadly, sources say the rush of senior players committing their future to the champions is as much about the healthy culture at the club as it is about the team’s strong chance of scooping up silverware in the seasons ahead.

The environment is a positive one (winning a league title helps, of course) and the players are close with one another. They enjoy going into work, which can’t be said for stars at every club in the league.

There’s a recognition among players of Arteta’s ability to improve them, both individually and tactically. The Spaniard is a stickler for detail and doesn’t believe in the notion of a ‘finished product’.

When Rice arrived in July 2023 on the pre-season tour of the US as Arsenal's £105million club-record signing, Arteta described his new midfielder as a ‘lighthouse’. Yet last month after the club’s 2-1 victory over Leeds, the manager said: ‘I went to him (Rice) and said, “You are not the lighthouse anymore. You are something else”.’

Even Rice is not safe from Arteta's relentless demands for improvement

The collective trust built between Arteta and his players has created a setting where constant improvement is an expectation. And the players want to do that at Arsenal

This season, Rice has been challenged to impact play more in the final third. The collective trust built between Arteta and his squad has created a setting where constant improvement is an expectation, rather than a desire. And the players want to achieve that at Arsenal, rather than anywhere else.

Berta deserves a pat on the back, too. Ex-sporting director Edu, a shrewd people person and operator, did a fine job with the cards he was dealt; Saliba, Gabriel and Rice arrived on his watch. Berta has had a very different deck of cards to play with, but has also done well to turn this group into champions.

Much of Arsenal’s nucleus is now secured. But there are tricky decisions still to come for Arteta and Berta.

Sports.title: EDDIE JONES: I understand why Rassie Erasmus went public with his anger - but he overstepped the mark with 'match-fixing' comments
Sports.content:
World Rugby is just like international politics.

Look at global diplomacy right now. It’s the USA, Russia and China who hold all the power. Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping are the ones with the biggest influence. That’s because they lead the world’s biggest nations. It’s pretty simple, really.

The same is true in rugby. The countries who are right at the top of the rankings have the loudest voices – teams like Rassie Erasmus’ South Africa and England. There’s always a battle to be had on something and you’re either on the good end of the result, or the bad.

When you’re the coach of England, you have influence. When you coach Japan, you don’t. That’s the reality of how the game’s corridors of power work.

There is no doubt some countries get preferential treatment. World Rugby is based in Dublin, for example. You only have to put two and two together. As back-to-back world champions and world No 1, South Africa get their fair share of the rub of the green.

But this week, they’ve seen their coach banned for six matches for comments made in a press conference. I think Rassie had a point when he questioned some of the decisions made in his team’s defeat by France, and I sent Rassie a text to that effect - he didn't reply. But there are appropriate and inappropriate ways to make a point and Rassie’s was the latter, especially with his ‘match-fixing’ claim.

Rassie Erasmus had a point when he questioned some of the decisions made in his team’s defeat by France. But there are appropriate and inappropriate ways to point that out

South Africa have their backs to the wall after the loss at the Stade de France. A wounded animal is a dangerous animal – and that’s what they are now

Even with a ban, I think Rassie will still be busy! I’m looking forward to seeing how the livestreamed watch-along party he is hosting goes on Saturday. Maybe I’ll log on for some of it, once my Japan team have finished playing Scotland. It should make for an interesting watch.

Earlier this year, I was banned for six weeks for criticising a match official. So, I know what Rassie is going through.

When you’re a coach and you have a refereeing grievance, you’ve got a choice to make. You can keep quiet publicly and go through the proper channels with World Rugby. My experience tells me if you do that, you often don’t get much joy. The other option is to get into trouble!

Rassie would have known he was going to be in a bit of strife for his media comments, even if he might not have been expecting the consequences of a lengthy ban.

As coaches, we’re only human. We can all get emotional and tip over the edge. There’s a lot of pressure in Test rugby, especially if you’re coaching one of the big nations. But Rassie has definitely overstepped the mark this time. To use cricket parlance, he’s bowled a few no balls in his career. And this is the latest.

He won’t be at his team’s game with Ireland in Dublin, but I would imagine he’s still coaching and having a big influence on South Africa's preparation.

I wouldn’t put it past him for the Springboks to smuggle him into the ground, a la Jose Mourinho’s washing basket trick with Chelsea all those years ago!

Rassie is a very strong character. A deep thinker. Rugby needs that, but it needs respect too

I think there’s a pattern to Rassie’s behaviour in this area. After a loss, he tends to go down this route. It happened, controversially, on the 2021 Lions tour and the chickens have come home to roost again.

When I was England coach and we toured South Africa in 2018, Rassie was very generous with the red wine. I think he’ll be drinking most of it himself in a hotel in Dublin this weekend. Maybe I’ll send him a bottle or two!

One of Rassie’s frustrations after his team were beaten in Paris was around the refereeing of knee-drop and hip-drop tackles. It’s a contentious area. These are new rules. At the pre-Nations Championship meeting, us coaches were under the impression these incidents would be penalised with only a penalty. But now we’re seeing yellow cards too.

Rassie was obviously frustrated and I can understand why. He’s a very strong character. A deep thinker. Rugby needs that, but it needs respect too. I expect a strong response from South Africa, both to losing to France and to Erasmus’ ban. They’re a team who don’t need to have their backs to the wall to perform. But when they do, they have an extra edge.

A wounded animal is a dangerous animal. That’s what South Africa are now.

England look formidable... but expect All Blacks to fight back

My Japan side got physically and emotionally knocked out by England last weekend. After the game, I caught up with some of my old players – Jamie George, Luke Cowan-Dickie and Henry Slade. They were obviously on good form after a big win.

It’s funny, because two weeks ago, England were supposed to be in tatters. They were supposed to hate their coach and have factions. I haven’t seen that at all in the performances they’ve delivered against Australia and Japan. Both have been incredibly powerful. I’ve sensed a real togetherness in their team.

One of the keys to England’s good form this autumn is how they’ve regenerated their older players. Ellis Genge, for example, looks immeasurably fitter than he has done in the past. There was a period of about 18 months when he wasn’t really carrying the ball with any influence. Against Japan, he was back to his old self – aggressive, nasty, brutal. He looked like the Genge of old and that’s what England need.

Ellis Genge was back to his best against my Japan side – aggressive, nasty and brutal

I spoke to Maro Itoje after the game. He looks rejuvenated after his rest period

It’s the same with Maro Itoje. I had a quick chat to him too and he was in great spirits. Maro has obviously had a rest period where he’s been able to get into good physical shape. There’s no doubt he’s having a big impact on games this month.

England go into New Zealand in good form, with four straight wins. But they need to be wary of the All Blacks. If they’re not the second-best team in the world, they’re very close.

I wouldn’t look too much into their performance against Wales. It was a major upset and it would have been a huge disappointment to Dave Rennie, their coach.

But they didn’t play their best team and will be much improved for England. My memories of England-New Zealand games, especially at Twickenham, is that they’re always furious.

The All Blacks always want to open the game up. England have a power differential to their game, even if they are trying to play a bit more with Fin Smith at No 10. It will be cat and mouse – physically intense, especially around the breakdown.

I’ve noticed England are having success with three men in the tackle – two bringing the carrier down and a third trying to jackal for possession. It’s a rugby league model and can be very effective.

Not a lot of teams do it consistently. England aren’t doing it at every ruck because the risk with it is you can end up short in the defensive line. But if you get it right, you can win back possession quicker – especially if you’re very physical which is one of England’s strengths.

The breakdown will define the game. If New Zealand get quick ball, they can cause carnage. England will have to slow down their possession at the ruck. Someone like Ben Curry will be really key in that area.

New Zealand have great players to come back in – guys like Jordie Barrett, Damian McKenzie and Codie Taylor. Immanuel Feyi-Waboso is a big miss for England.

England are having success getting multiple players in the tackle – it's a rugby league model and can be very effective

New Zealand will be reeling from their shock loss to Wales and desperate to make amends at Twickenham on Saturday

I don’t know how many points playing at Twickenham is worth to England, but it’s a few and so it should be. It’s their home ground and when we talk about rub of the green in rugby, it’s normal for that to have an impact. I think it could be a deciding factor in the game.

My prediction? If England can get out to a fast start and build a lead in the first 20 minutes, they'll win. If New Zealand can stay in touch, they might have too much at the end.

My week north of the border

I’m in Edinburgh this week with Japan, and it's been typical Scottish weather here – low, grey skies. Drizzle.

Last Sunday, I went to Murrayfield to watch Scotland's game with Australia, which was a tough, old grind. I think it’ll be a different type of game this weekend. The weather forecast is pretty good.

When I was in London for our match with England, I loved having fish and chips. In Scotland, they don’t mind battering anything that moves. But I’ve kept away from all that – especially the deep-fried Mars bars!

Sports.title: DAN BIGGAR: England must brace for an All Blacks response, let's hope for a full house in Cardiff after Wales' magic moment... and the spicy match-up you cannot miss on Super Saturday
Sports.content:
What a weekend of rugby we had! Famous backs-to-the-wall victories for France and Wales over South Africa and New Zealand were games for the ages and showed once again that international rugby is in rude health.

They were a real shot in the arm for the Nations Championship too. Strong television audiences on ITV also showed the game can have a mass appeal.

I can’t wait for the six matches we’ve got lined up this ‘Super Saturday.’

They will decide who takes on who in the new competition’s ‘finals weekend’ and who will be in position to be crowned winner for the first time.

Here’s my guide to all the action…

The Nations Championship gave us another blockbuster few days of action last weekend

England vs New Zealand (2.10pm)

I still can’t quite believe Wales beat the All Blacks! Dave Rennie’s press conference pre-England was intriguing. He said New Zealand had ‘let their country down.’

As good as Wales’ defence was, I think the All Blacks will have been disappointed with their attack in the final quarter. They took contact every time, rather than looking to move the ball which is unlike them.

I think that will change for England and they’ve got so many good players to come back in – guys like Jordie Barrett, Damian McKenzie, Codie Taylor and Ethan de Groot.

I’ve no doubt New Zealand will be far better, but my experience tells me you have no idea what a shock defeat has done to you until you step onto the field for the next game.

When you suffer a loss you simply couldn’t have seen coming – like New Zealand did in Cardiff – it can either floor you or get you back firing. The All Blacks will hope it’ll be the latter. They’ll need to do so to beat England.

Barrett is the best centre in the world. He has it all – passing, kicking, size, work rate, communication, carrying.

With him back in the team, New Zealand’s attack should have a lot more deception about it. It’s such a tough game to call. I think it will be decided on one thing.

If England can shut down the New Zealand attack, they’ll win. If they can’t, I think we’ll see an All Blacks response.

I expect England to keep close to the same team that impressed against Australia, with Will Joseph staying on the wing after his five-try demolition of Japan.

I’ve been really impressed with England’s desire, tenacity and accuracy in their two games so far, but this will be their toughest test yet.

PREDICTION: England (just!)

New Zealand will be desperate to respond after their shock defeat against Wales in Cardiff

Will Joseph will hope to continue his good form from last week's thrashing of Japan

Scotland vs Japan (2.10pm)

Scotland were well beaten by New Zealand and their success over Australia was pretty gritty.

They’ve got a couple of injuries too, but they’ll still have far too much for Japan who have looked a poor side this autumn.

PREDICTION: Scotland

Ireland vs South Africa (4.40pm)

This is going to be spicy! The build-up has been centred on South Africa and their coach Rassie Erasmus, whose ‘match fixing’ press conference claims in the wake of his team’s defeat by France have earned him a six-game ban.

The suspension is with immediate effect, so he misses the Ireland game, the finals weekend, and South Africa’s build-up to the World Cup next year. It’s a significant ban.

Sam Prendergast, as Erasmus predicted in his press conference, is available to play No 10 for Ireland after he was cleared of a hip-drop tackle.

The combination of South Africa losing in France and Erasmsus’ ban means I think the Springboks will come out in in Dublin like a caged animal.

I do fear for Ireland in that regard, because an angry South Africa is not to be messed with, even if they will be without Erasmus.

I think the ingenuity Erasmus has shown, in terms of how he has redefined rugby with things like a 7:1 bench split, has been great for the game.

I think he’s entitled to air his views, so long as he does so respectfully. I don’t think anyone can say he did that in his press conference.

PREDICTION: South Africa

South Africa's game in Ireland will be spicy after Rassie Erasmus was handed a six-game ban

Italy vs Fiji (4.40pm)

Neither of these teams has won a game yet, which is disappointing for them.

Italy have been hit hard by injuries, but home advantage should be good enough for them to get on the board this weekend.

PREDICTION: Italy

Wales vs Australia (8.10pm)

Like England against New Zealand, this one is so hard to call! Both are flip-of-a-coin games.

In becoming the first Welsh team in 73 years to beat the All Blacks, Steve Tandy’s team produced one of the country’s greatest ever results and performances.

Their challenge is to back that up against Australia. The reality is doing that, both emotionally and physically, is so, so hard to do. That will be Wales’ big challenge.

In the 2015 Six Nations, the Wales team I played in pulled off a big result when we beat Ireland at home. It meant we stayed in the Championship hunt and ended Ireland’s Grand Slam dream.

It wasn’t quite like Wales’ victory over New Zealand in terms of it being a huge shock. But the parallels are relevant.

The next week, we played Italy in Rome and struggled to hit those heights again.

Although we eventually won 61-20, we were really poor in the first half. We couldn’t get anything going and got a right rollicking from Warren Gatland at half time. In the first 40, we just struggled emotionally and physically because of what we’d given the previous week.

The challenge for Wales now will be to back up last week's incredible New Zealand triumph

They are facing an Australia team who will be smarting after back-to-back defeats

To beat Australia, Wales can’t afford to do that. Only once the game starts will the Welsh players know how much New Zealand has taken out of them.

There is now significant expectation on Wales too. More people are expecting them to win this weekend.

If they do, they’ll be three from three this autumn which would be incredible given the struggles of the past three years!

I also hope there will be more supporters in Principality Stadium after there were 20,000 unsold seats for the historic New Zealand game. If Wales hit those heights again, I think they’ll win. But that’s a big if.

Don’t forget, Australia will be desperate too as they’ve had a poor autumn and haven’t won yet.

PREDICTION: Wales (just!)

France vs Argentina (8.10pm)

France were incredible against South Africa. To win with 25 players out and Maxime Lucu – as good as he is – playing as a makeshift No 10, was some feat.

I was so impressed by the way their forwards, without so many key men, stood up to the Springboks.

Yes, they were dominated at the scrum. But their physicality in all other areas of the field was impressive and when you’ve got Antoine Dupont in your team, he could play flanker and still go well. He’s that good! His performance last Friday night was just a joke!

France will ride that wave into Argentina, who are inconsistent but will still be able to cause some trouble at next year’s World Cup.

PREDICTION: France

France were incredible against South Africa and now must go again when they face Argentina

Watch Dan Biggar and Ronan O’Gara discuss all the big Nations Championship talking points on The Debrief, in association with Allianz, on Sunday at 9pm on ITV4 and 12.15am on ITV1

Sports.title: 'A lot of snooker players are a bit thick. I'd rather be thick and world No 5': 'Overthinker' Ronnie O'Sullivan opens up on his future - and finding his sport boring - as he invests in new T20-style event
Sports.content:
Seven-time world champion Ronnie O'Sullivan has suggested that many of his fellow players are 'a bit thick', but has claimed it's not necessarily a bad trait in the sport.

O'Sullivan, 50, now owns a 50 per cent stake in the new fast-paced 900 Global Championship snooker format, whose inaugural crown in May, and has opened up on how the event lets players act on 'instinct' rather than 'overthinking' every shot.

The 900 championship has been dubbed the T20 cricket equivalent for snooker, with frames timed to 900 seconds (15 minutes), while there is a 20-second shot clock. It makes for a much faster-paced and electric game.

And when heaping praise on the format as it continues with the Crucible Cup in Reading next week, 'The Rocket' spoke of how a lack of intelligence could aid players in the groundbreaking competition.

'There’s a lot of players on the tour who don’t think a lot – they’re just a bit thick,' he told The Telegraph. 'And you are better off being thick to play snooker. I’m not saying being thick will make you a great player because you have to have a certain amount of intelligence to become great at anything.

'The great players are thinkers, but I’d rather be a bit thick and maybe No 5 in the world and you don’t have maybe the inner dialogue of questioning yourself or over-analysing it. A lot of players, you know they are not thinking. As a snooker player, that’s probably not a bad place to be.

Ronnie O'Sullivan believes the 900 Championship is what snooker has needed to make it less boring

'That’s why I like the 900. It becomes about potting balls, playing off instinct. You’ve still got to think clever, play good snooker, play the right shot, play good shots. But it’s, ‘I’m going to have to play better than my opponent’ and not ‘I’m going to slow him down’. And I think that is a better way of playing.'

O'Sullivan has long spoken out about the 'boring' nature of the sport he has conquered repeatedly on the world stage and has stated that he finds it 'harder' to motivate himself to play these days.

He continued: 'I get a bit bored watching players walking around, looking at shots. You are thinking: "Oh God, come on". If it could take two, three, four, five hours, I’m like: "Well, there’s not much point. I might as well go out, get on with my day" and maybe watch the end of it on YouTube. But, if I know it’s going to be over in an hour, I’ll sit and watch.

'It’s not me that’s the problem, it’s the other players. They are very slow, methodical, take a long time on their shots, and overthink. It gets a bit boring to be honest with you. Just get on with it. With the 900, they have to. They don’t have a choice.'

O'Sullivan is considered one of the greats of the sport, if not the best the table has ever seen, winning 23 Triple Crown titles - including eight UK Championship titles and eight Masters titles - but has previously issued plenty of retirement threats.

When approached on the subject of when he will be putting away his cue once and for all he remained coy on the situation.

'I don’t know,' O'Sullivan added. 'It takes a lot more for me to want to move away from my home comforts. I play so little it tends to be two or three tournaments to get up to speed of where the other guys are.

'It’s hard to play when you are making elementary mistakes; not because you are not playing well enough, but you are just not sharp enough. If I was to play more I’d probably get to that point where I’m competing better.'

Sports.title: Most Australians now believe 'tainted' Pat Cummins is a liar. That could force stalling bosses to sack him - if captain doesn't quit first, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
Most Australians now believe 'tainted' Pat Cummins is a liar. That could force stalling bosses to sack him - if captain doesn't quit first, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH

As Pat Cummins was doorstepped at his Sydney home by reporters clamouring for reaction to Cameron Bancroft’s accusations the night before, it was clear Australia’s public mood had taken a turn for the febrile.

Six days earlier, Cummins appeared to have grabbed the momentum during a marathon press conference in which he called Usman Khawaja’s claim that the whole team knew about the 2018 sandpaper plot in South Africa ‘complete and utter nonsense’.

But his credibility took a hit, first when Chadd Sayers – 12th man in South Africa – backed Khawaja’s version of events on Sunday. Then, even more devastatingly, on Wednesday evening, when Bancroft planted his 4,497-word detonation in the West Australian, effectively branding Cummins a liar.

Code Sports, the Australian sports news website, has been running polls all week to determine whether the public are with Team Khawaja or Team Cummins. And until Bancroft’s revelations, the result was too close to call.

Now, though, the split has lurched to 80-20 in Khawaja’s favour. Four out of five Aussies, in other words, no longer believe Cummins has been truthful. It is an approval rating which might make even Donald Trump think twice.

One of the reporters pursuing Cummins to his car as he headed for training suggested the ‘English media’ thought he should be sacked, as if it were all a Pommie plot. But that downplays the extent to which the Australian press also believe his position is increasingly untenable.

Aussie skipper Pat Cummins appeared to have grabbed the momentum during a marathon press conference in which he denied Usman Khawaja’s Sandpapergate claims – but the mood has now changed

Cameron Bancroft's revelations in the Australian media effectively branded Cummins a liar

The golden boy who has captained his country to World Cup and World Test Championship success in 2023, and possesses a Test record – 328 wickets at 22 – to compare with anyone, is close to being hung, drawn and quartered in the court of public opinion.

And it is that court whose approval Cricket Australia have always craved. It was the Test team’s reputation-damaging five defeats in a row in 2016 that led to board officials laying down the law to the players, which in turn created the win-at-all-costs toxicity that spawned the use of sandpaper.

If CA now conclude that Cummins is damaged goods, that the job often described as the second-most important in Australia behind the prime minister has been sullied by association, they will have no choice but to sack him.

That assumes Cummins won’t jump before he is pushed, possibly on the pretext that he has become a ‘distraction’, since it is inconceivable that he will backtrack on the clear-eyed certainty of last week’s denial.

It emerged on Wednesday that Australia’s selectors had delayed naming their Test squad for December’s four-match series at home to New Zealand, ostensibly because they wanted to use the next round of first-class Sheffield Shield matches, starting on Sunday, to finalise their options.

But since none of Cummins, Josh Hazlewood or Mitchell Starc – the three frontline fast bowlers in South Africa eight years ago – is expected to turn out for New South Wales against Queensland at Sydney, it is hard to avoid the suspicion that CA are stalling, while they wait to see what other revelations crop up in the meantime.

CA chief executive, Todd Greenberg, looked impressively calm as he passed through Hobart Airport on Thursday morning, having announced during a bizarre press conference by a children’s playground that an ‘independent forum’ would be established to create a ‘safe space’ for the Class of 2018 to talk about Sandpapergate.

And while Greenberg is understood not to favour any action either immediate or drastic, neither can he afford to ignore the outside noise.

Cricket Australia chief executive, Todd Greenberg, is understood not to favour any action either immediate or drastic but he knows he cannot afford to ignore the outside noise

Australia have delayed naming their squad for December’s Test series with New Zealand so it remains to be seen if the famous bowling quartet of (from left) Josh Hazlewood, Nathan Lyon, Mitchell Starc and Cummins will be selected

It was instructive, for instance, that former Test wicketkeeper Ian Healy, whose niece Alyssa – herself an ex-international keeper – is married to Starc, said Bancroft’s testimony ‘taints the personal legacies’ of the bowlers.

Veteran journalist and broadcaster Robert Craddock was unequivocal, insisting: ‘It’s legacy-damaging. There’s no question about it.’

Part of CA’s problem is that they have invested heavily in the idea of Cummins as the figurehead of the Good Ship Australia, steering the boat away from the choppy waters created by the team coached by Darren Lehmann. Even Cummins himself called the atmosphere under Lehmann ‘ugly’.

Not only that, but he inherited the captaincy shortly before the 2021-22 Ashes, when Tim Paine was forced to step down because it turned out he had sent explicit messages to a Cricket Tasmania employee four years earlier.

Quite simply, Australian cricket needed Cummins – tall, handsome and articulate, a clean slate for a new era – to help win back the fans’ affection. When Greenberg argued on Wednesday that ‘the captain doesn’t need to be cleared’, it sounded like wishful thinking as much as anything, a plea for the sanity of the Australian game.

And yet the prevailing mood out here these past few days has been one of catharsis, with first Khawaja’s, then Bancroft’s claims, bringing to the surface all manner of emotions.

Bancroft himself, answering questions through his car window the morning after he burned the house down, said: ‘I didn’t want to point fingers or implicate the others. I just wanted for my own peace to tell the truth. I feel freed and happy.’

Bancroft tucks the sandpaper into his pocket during that infamous Cape Town Test in 2018. Having told his story he says he now feels 'freed and happy’

The Aussie coach during Sandpapergate, Darren Lehmann, cut a distressed figure in the Hobart press box when the Bancroft news broke

But Lehmann, who had been in Hobart to commentate on the barely noticed third ODI between Australia and England, cut a distressed figure in the press box when the Bancroft news broke.

And Peter Handscomb, the substitute who Bancroft claimed had been told by Lehmann at Cape Town to ‘get the f*****g sandpaper off Bangers now’ when the cameras exposed the skulduggery, was also on commentary duty – as if to emphasise the story’s continued resonance in every nook and cranny of the Australian game.

Very few figures have emerged from this episode with credit. In Bancroft’s telling, only CA’s media manager on the South Africa tour, Kate Hutchison, spoke out against the stupidity.

There are almost no heroes here, only cricketers and former coaches fighting for reputations, and reporters roaming the streets conducting vox pops. Everyone has an opinion. And it is turning against Australia’s Test captain.

Sports.title: Man United star Bryan Mbeumo stays up late to play GTA6 on morning of his new boss's first day at work: Athletes' performances to 'plummet' for weeks as Liverpool and Arsenal players reveal their video game all-nighters
Sports.content:
The world has been waiting 13 years for GTA6 and footballers are not immune from the lure and addictive nature of the game.

In fact, top flight players are notorious gamers given their amount of free time after training and Bryan Mbeumo was one of many to share his excitement at the midnight release.

No doubt new Man United boss Mauricio Pochettino would prefer his players to get a solid night's sleep ahead of taking his first training session on Thursday but Mbeumo couldn't resist a late-night session.

He shared the loading screen of the Rockstar game at midnight on his Instagram story with the word 'historic' as the clock ticked into Thursday morning.

It remains to be seen whether Mbeumo stayed up into the early hours playing but an estimated three million UK adults were expected to call in sick or take annual leave to play.

Sleep is vital for athletes to recover and perform at their best and one NBA star even predicted professionals across sports would see their output 'plummet' as a result of GTA's pull.

Bryan Mbeumo shared this picture on his Instagram story at midnight when GTA went live

Mauricio Pochettino's first morning of training coincides with the release of GTA, played by Mbeumo and plenty of other athletes who looked forward to the late-night release

In a previous video clip online, Mbeumo was being interviewed while on his console and showed he'd pre-ordered the game, saying: 'I'm just waiting now, the game will make me stay at home every single day... after training.'

Pochettino, who flew on a private jet to Manchester on Wednesday ahead of his first day in the job on Thursday, will no doubt have a keen eye on whether any of his stars are bleary-eyed in training.

The new boss has an incredibly tight turnaround to prepare for the huge clash with rivals Liverpool on Sunday at Anfield, but perhaps the Reds will also be dealing with GTA-mania.

Alexander Isak was asked about the game's release while on international duty with Sweden and admitted: 'Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the plan.'

A renowned sleep coach for top athletes, Nick Littlehales, has opined on the effects late-night gaming can have.

'They get lost in it, it’s an engaging distraction, and it satisfies their competitive edge, but just like mindlessly scrolling YouTube or social media, you need to put your own filters and blockers in place, otherwise you’ll find yourself doing something ridiculously stupid and playing for hours and hours, hurting your performance,' he told Ozoon.

'We know it’s unrealistic to expect a player to just stop after exactly two hours when they’re in the zone. You have to accept it and ask them: "Are you prepared to sacrifice your nocturnal sleep to be awake and stimulated? Is it worth it?" If they insist on it, we look at scheduling it. Maybe they game late on Tuesdays, Thursdays.

'You must have these open conversations instead of outright banning late-night gaming. If you just throw the book at them, they end up taking sleeping tablets, using snus, and taking unregulated supplements they don’t understand just so they can cope. When you help them manage their gaming, they usually start to self-regulate.'

It’s safe to say Bryan Mbeumo is ready for GTA 6. 🤣🤣 pic.twitter.com/skkPM2GYo9 — Kev 屮 (@UtdKev08) November 18, 2026

Conor McGregor announced that he would give employees at various businesses the day off

People cheer as Grand Theft Auto VI goes live at London gaming venue XP Tavern

Arsenal's Declan Rice could be another to be locked into the new GTA having previously spoken about how much gaming helps him switch off.

He told GQ: 'I can never sleep after night games. It’s impossible. I’ll be that wired. I'll play Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto, FIFA. Anything. Just play with a load of my friends. Adrenaline, everything. You don’t really settle down.

'I feel like when you’re playing at this level, your mind’s just constantly – it’s just going.'

Football clubs, businesses and even schools are braced for the effects of the new game, with one head teacher in Chelmsford, Essex, entering students into a raffle to win a £10 Amazon voucher in an attempt to stop them bunking off.

UFC star Conor McGregor announced that he was giving the day off to 400 employees at his various businesses so they could play the game.

And Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared an image of himself playing the game, flying a helicopter after it was launched.

The astonishing level of anticipation for GTA6 has banked more than £1.14bn in pre-orders alone and is set to become by far the highest grossing game ever made.

It debuted with a score of 99 on review aggregator website Metacritic – equalling 1998's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-rated video game ever.

Some 2.8million UK adults are set to play the game on launch day alone, according to a Uswitch poll commissioned earlier this month.

Over in the US, a number of athletes were frank in their honesty about how many of them would be addicted to the game.

Houston Rockets center Steven Adams previously said: 'You guys should anticipate November, the performance of the league, league-wide… GTA is dropping.

'So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet, mate. Just for the month of November, performance is going to go down. It should come back up, though.

'Most of the boys will get it done, hopefully they finish the game. Coaching as well, by the way. The coaching and scouts are going to be horrendous, mate. Just for November, but it should bounce back in December, hopefully. Should be good.'

🚨🇸🇪 Alexander Isak on the release of GTA 6:



“Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the plan.” 😂 pic.twitter.com/LEhQQRo8pQ — James Wathland (@JamesWathland) November 12, 2026

Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared this image from playing the game

'I told my mom she might not hear from me for a couple of days,' Los Angeles Rams receiver Tutu Atwell, a Miami native, said with a grin. 'We've been waiting for this one for a long, long time, You know it's going to be a big one.'

Plenty of other athletes share Atwell's excitement, but will prioritize their work on the field.

'I think a lot of athletes are responsible,' said Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Steve Avila. 'But if you could check guys' sleep scores … I think you'd see that some guys' hours are going to go way down, for sure.'

New York Jets running back Breece Hall concurs: 'Yeah, definitely getting the film done early, and then spending the extra hour or two on the game,' Hall said. 'But you've got to make sure you handle the main thing first before you have some fun.'

There were some technological concerns in the hours leading up to the game's release, with the official PlayStation Network status website yesterday acknowledging some players were unable to access online features.

A statement on the website read: 'You might have difficulty launching games, apps, or network features. We're working to resolve the issue as soon as possible. Thank you for your patience.'

Declan Rice is another star to stay up late gaming as it helps him switch off after big games

Those issues appeared to be cleared up by midnight, with PlayStation declaring all of its services were 'up and running' in the hours after the game went live.

BT and EE called the upcoming launch an 'unprecedented gaming download event' because of the size of the game and the number of people expected to play.

The pre-download drove the second-highest broadband traffic peak ever on BT's networks, only beaten by Arsenal v Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in May, and Virgin Media O2 saw its highest-ever daily data volume last Tuesday.

While the exact number of people who have pre-ordered GTA VI is not known, Sony said it is the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store.

Schools have urged pupils not to use the release of the game – which carries an age rating of 18 – as an excuse to skip lessons.

Sales of gaming consoles and accessories surged in the run-up to launch day.

A man walks past a Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) digital billboard advert in Milan - the game's release has become a global event

Department store chain John Lewis said it had seen a 62 per cent year-on-year increase in sales of gaming consoles and accessories, while retailer Currys reported a 149 per cent increase in PlayStation 5 consoles alone.

GTA VI returns to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City, Rockstar's fictional version of Miami, which has featured in previous instalments of the series.

The game follows two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, who find themselves caught up in a criminal conspiracy in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida.

The pair become embroiled in a Bonnie and Clyde-style crime story after 'an easy score goes wrong', leaving them 'forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive'.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino's culture reset: New Man United boss vows to shift losing mentality in his first interview - as he tells all on cheering them on at 1999 Champions League final
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino's culture reset: New Man United boss vows to shift losing mentality in his first interview - as he tells all on cheering them on at 1999 Champions League final

Mauricio Pochettino has vowed to reset the culture at Manchester United as he lifted the lid on being in the stands in 1999 to see the club's greatest triumph.

Pochettino was officially appointed as United's new head coach on Wednesday and he has since addressed the club's internal media team for the first time, outlining how he plans to drag this underperforming squad up the table.

'The culture is the most important,' Pochettino explained.

'Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create.

'We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us to be close to winning every single game.'

'The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now – it's to work with them and try to take the pressure.'

Mauricio Pochettino is determined to shift the culture at Manchester United back to winning

Pochettino's determination to be the man to bring winning football back to Old Trafford is in large part due to one of his founding memories of the club back in 1999 when he was a player at Espanyol.

Alongside his now trusted goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, Pochettino was at the Nou Camp to see United clinch the Champions League, thus sealing a famous Treble, against Bayern Munich.

'In 1999, I was in Barcelona for that final. That was an iconic final,' he added.

'Toni Jimenez [was there] too. We were shouting for Manchester United from there. I was so excited to see Manchester United.

'This [is the] type of game that you stay sitting in your place [for] and you're so excited because you are watching the game. That was an amazing game.

'And then what happened in the end... it's like it's impossible not to empathise with that team, no?

'That was an amazing memory that made me pay more attention to United, to [Sir Alex] Ferguson and the players that were there, that are all legends.'

That level of success feels a lifetime away from the current squad, which emerges from the international break for a trip to face bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield slumped 18th in the Premier League.

The Argentine head coach was in the stands in Barcelona cheering for United back in 1999

While there are those who may be daunted trying to turn around the ship which sunk so far it cost Michael Carrick his job, Pochettino wants to focus on potential, rather than the present.

'It's a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club,' a defiant Pochettino added.

'Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it's a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free.

'The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now – it's to work with them and try to take the pressure [off].

'Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it's too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back.

'When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent and when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your team-mates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

'That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff - we were talking a lot today. Then [we need to] settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero.

'I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.'

Pochettino took first team training for the first time on Thursday morning as he begins work

Pochettino poses at his unveiling with United director of football Jason Wilcox on Wednesday

Pochettino knows that time is not on his side ahead of an upcoming week that sees United travel to face Liverpool on Sunday, followed by a Champions League trip to face Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday. The week is rounded out by a home match a week on Saturday against Brentford.

The Argentine head coach touched down in Manchester on Wednesday morning, taking a private jet straight after the final whistle of United States versus Haiti in Cincinnati.

From there he immediately headed to their Carrington training base where he took a tour and met players and staff, including Tom Heaton, Luke Shaw, Mason Mount and Bruno Fernandes. It is understood he left a good first impression on the players.

And yet, in spite of such a packed schedule, which saw him leave Carrington very late at night on Wednesday and reappear bright and early on Thursday for training, Pochettino is raring to go and is eager for his players to head to Anfield on Sunday convinced they can win.

'I have plenty of energy. It's a privilege to be head coach of Manchester United,' he said.

'And we are not wasting time. We need to be ready to compete on Sunday.

'Now it's not time to think about rest, it's not time to think about sleep. It's about being ready and to prepare everything to be sure that we are going to compete in the best condition at Anfield.'

Sports.title: Cheltenham Gold Cup winner misses Betfair Chase because 'not enough water put on'
Sports.content:
Cheltenham Gold Cup winner misses Betfair Chase because 'not enough water put on'

Inothewayurthinkin was the ante-post second favourite for the £200,000 prize at Haydock on Saturday but was not among the seven declarations

View 2 Images Inothwayurthinkin: missing from Betfair Chase (Image: Getty Images)

Cheltenham Gold Cup winner Inothewayurthinkin has not been declared for Saturday’s Betfair Chase.

‌



‌



The horse who denied Galopin Des Champs a famous Gold Cup hat-trick at Cheltenham in 2025 had been second favourite for the £200,000 prize at Haydock. But the JP McManus-owned star was not among the seven names declared on Thursday after training Gavin Cromwell had a change of heart.

‌



Last season the eight-year-old largely struggled to rediscover the form that saw him run out a brilliant winner of steeplechasing’s blue riband event last year, but he was the subject of strong market support this week which led William Hill to slash his odds for the first Grade 1 jumps race of the season in Britain to 9-2 from 12-1.

‌



Leading conditional jockey banned for 17 days after exceeding whip limit in ITV race READ MORE :

However Cromwell said ground conditions were to blame for his star’s absence from Haydock where the official going is good (good to soft in the back straight).

“It’s just the ground – it’s only good ground in the straight and I was hoping they would have put more water on it,” he said. "He’s in very good form. I suppose we’ll just have to wait until Christmas, I don’t think there’s a whole pile more that he could run in unfortunately.

‌



“There’s Leopardstown at Christmas or possibly the Cotswold Chase (at Cheltenham in January) I suppose, but I don’t know at the moment. I would have liked to start him on Saturday, but that’s the way it is.”

View 2 Images Gavin Cromwell: unhappy with the going (Image: Daily Mirror..)

‌



Later, speaking to William Hill , Cromwell was more forthright. “Our reason for not declaring Inothewayurthinkin at Haydock is the ground,” he said. “It’s going to be good ground because they haven’t put enough water on, and they weren’t intending to.”

In Inothewayurthinkin’s absence a field of seven have been declared for the Betfair Chase, headed by Dan Skelton’s defending champion Grey Dawning.

Article continues below

Irish hopes are carried by Noel Meade’s Affordale Fury and the Henry de Bromhead-trained Gorgeous Tom, while the McManus silks will be sported by Jagwar from Oliver Greenall and Josh Guerriero’s yard. Jamie and Josh Moore’s Salver, Ben Pauling’s Handstands and Joel Parkinson and Sue Smith’s outsider Konfusion complete the septet.

Watering is being carried out at Haydock where 10mm was due to be appoied on Thursday.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney made Man Utd keep Kai promise that could see him released before senior debut
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney made Man Utd keep Kai promise that could see him released before senior debut

Wayne Rooney has been in close contact with Manchester United youth coaches as Kai continues to earn his stripes in the academy.

View 2 Images Wayne Rooney has discussed Kai playing for Manchester United. (Image: JMEnternational/Getty Images)

Wayne Rooney has instructed youth coaches at Manchester United not to afford his son, Kai, any special treatment. The former England international and the club's record goalscorer wanted his now-17-year-old to prove his worth at the club and demonstrate that he merits taking match time away from other exciting young players.

‌



‌



Speaking to Gabby Logan on the Life At The Midpoint podcast, Rooney claimed that he wanted Kai to be handled fairly, just like every other prospect in the academy, and assessed on ability rather than family name. So much so that the 41-year-old took the coaching staff aside and made himself crystal clear.

‌



Rooney said: "Firstly, going up through the academy, I didn't want the parents or anyone to think that he was there because of me. I actually spoke to the coaches and said, 'If he's not good enough, release him'.

‌



"I don't want him there because it's not fair on him if he's there and he's not good enough and the club are keeping him on because of me.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"And thankfully he has turned out to be good enough; he has been good enough."

‌



Kai, who was photographed in 2020 putting pen to paper on a contract with United and posing in a shirt bearing the number 10, is following in his father's footsteps, working his way up through the academy.

The teenager has earned his place at Carrington and, in July, he committed his future to the club by signing a scholarship. Rooney's son has since made his debut for the under-21s, coming on as a substitute in a 3-2 loss to Nottingham Forest in Premier League 2 last month.

‌



View 2 Images Kai Rooney signed a scholarship with Manchester United in July.

He's also made a couple of brief appearances in the UEFA Youth League, playing in a 3-0 loss to Atletico Madrid and a 1-1 draw with Roma.

‌



Kai has been handed opportunities at the under-21 level in recognition of his outstanding performances with the under-18s, where, so far this season, he's notched six goals in four league outings.

Rooney then explained why he didn't want United to one day question whether they should cut short his son's time at the club and potentially deny him a senior debut.

Article continues below

He added: "What I don't want is to always be there– he has to go through these moments in life because all of a sudden he is going to have a wife, he is going to have his own kids, etc., and we can't always be there for him."

Sports.title: Behind the scenes of Mauricio Pochettino's first day at Man Utd and message to players
Sports.content:
A shade over 10 hours after the final whistle had blown on his 37th and final game in charge of the US Men's National Team, Mauricio Pochettino walked into Manchester United's Carrington training ground, wearing a fresh, black club tracksuit and with a slightly jet-lagged appearance amid the excitement of the biggest challenge of his professional life.

At some point between the TQL Stadium in Cincinnati and his arrival at Carrington, Pochettino had swapped the Nike-branded US Soccer gilet for United's Adidas hoodie and joggers. While some elite-level coaches like a bit of time out between jobs, Pochettino had to make do with a sleep on a private jet and some new gear.

In what has been a chaotic season at Old Trafford, the fact that United's new head coach began work just hours after finishing his last job feels like it fits the theme, but the 54-year-old deserves credit for wanting to get his feet under the table as quickly as possible.

His No. 2, Jesus Perez, goalkeeping coach Toni Jimenez, and fitness coach and son Sebastiano Pochettino arrived in Manchester on Sunday. Pochettino has been in regular contact with them over the last few days, but still wanted to visit the training ground and start putting his own stamp on things.

Mauricio Pochettino's January transfer shortlist revealed as Man Utd target three signings READ MORE :

Man Utd boss Mauricio Pochettino issues defiant message after meeting stars for first time READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

He was greeted at Carrington by chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, spent time with United's key decision-makers, and was then given a tour of the facility by Berrada. He also briefly met some of the players who had been in for training that morning, in a session run by Perez, as well as meeting more staff members.

While any big team meeting will take place later in the week, the players he spoke to were left with the impression that Pochettino will be demanding to play for, but left with a sense of excitement and positivity from speaking to the new head coach.

Pochettino conducted some club media with in-house TV station MUTV late on Wednesday, although most of that footage is due to be released only on Thursday, and finalised plans for the remainder of the week.

He will speak to external media for the first time on Friday, while training sessions are set to take place every day before travelling to Merseyside on Saturday afternoon, ahead of the fixture with Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday afternoon.

View 3 Images Pochettino arrived at Carrington, hours after finishing his final game as USA boss

Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jr have made a positive impression on staff since their arrival at Carrington and caught up with the boss during his time on site on Wednesday. Pochettino didn't leave Carrington until late in the evening, capping off a working day that had lasted close to 24 hours.

He has kept a family home in London while working for US Soccer, but will stay at a Cheshire hotel provided by United as he looks for a more permanent place in the North West with his wife, Karina. The couple's two sons are now grown up, with Sebastiano, 31, and Maurizio, 25, a winger for Andorran side Inter Club d'Escaldes.

As his head hit the pillow in the leafy suburbs, it was a far cry from where his day had started in the United States' Midwest, watching his players cruise to a 2-0 win against Haiti.

Pochettino conducted a final round of media engagements at TQL Stadium, including an appearance on TNT Sports USA that produced some gentle ribbing from former Manchester City winger DaMarcus Beasley, before saying a final farewell to his players.

There had been plenty of time during the week for goodbyes, and the commanding lead the USA held from the first leg fostered a more relaxed vibe in Cincinnati, but the finality of Pochettino's exit still stirred emotions among him and his players. Tears were shed in the dressing room.

View 3 Images Mauricio Pochettino signed off as USA boss with a 2-0 win over Haiti (Image: Omar Vega/USSF/Getty Images)

He made the 15-minute journey from the stadium to Northern Kentucky International Airport, where he boarded a private jet laid on by United. He departed US soil at 4.39am UK time (11.39pm ET), ready to catch some sleep before beginning his new job. He was joined on the journey by long-time assistant coach Miki D’Agostino and performance analyst Alec Scott, both of who will join the staff at United alongside Pochettino.

Pochettino was awake in time to take a picture of the Manchester suburbs as the Gulfstream G700 jet came in to land, touching down in Manchester at 11.32am. He was greeted by United security staff at the airport's private terminal and driven straight to Carrington in a Mercedes-Benz van, arriving at the club's training ground within an hour of the flight landing.

He knows he has the challenge of a lifetime on his hands in Manchester, and there was no time to waste.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua names exact round he will knock out Tyson Fury
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua names exact round he will knock out Tyson Fury

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury will settle their differences in the ring in Cardiff on December 11, a decade after their heavyweight rivalry began

View Image Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua face off (Image: getty images)

Anthony Joshua plans to knock out Tyson Fury in the eighth round of their mega-fight.

‌



‌



Joshua and Fury will settle their differences in the ring in Cardiff on December 11, a decade after their heavyweight rivalry began. Fury will start as the favourite and has already predicted an early finish. But Joshua is also confident he can stop his rival - but is willing to wait until the second half of the bout.

‌



“I’m a knockout specialist,” he told The Sun. “I’ll knock him out in round eight. If I don’t do it in the first 30 seconds, that is. With us, it’s pure competition, pure pitbull competitor wanting to win. That’s the type of energy that we’re bringing to the table.

‌



“I’ve been in big fights, and I don’t need to disrespect my opponent. So long as you respect me, it’s going to be respectful until that first bell. But I have bad intentions. I’ve been thinking about what I want to do and I just want to punch with bad intentions."

Anthony Joshua becomes dad to baby girl weeks before Tyson Fury fight READ MORE :

Anthony Joshua opens up on cheating death in car crash which killed pals READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

‌



Fury, meanwhile, is hoping for an early night in the Welsh capital. “It's all right Joshua, I know you're afraid," he said recently. But I won't hurt you, I'll make it quick, I'll make it a quick KO, so you can get back to your business work being a landlord and stuff. I'll make it very fast, and I'll make it pain-free for you and your team."

Fury and Joshua initially looked set to clash in New York before the Olympic champion, along with promoter Eddie Hearn, dug their heels in and insisted their contract was honoured and the fight was staged in the UK. Cardiff's Principality Stadium was chosen but a final decision has yet to be made over the start time.

Several residents have complained about the 1am ringwalks and Cardiff Council's Licensing Sub-Committee will meet on November 25 - just over two weeks before the first bell - to decide whether to grant or reject the stadium's request for an extension to it's current arrangements.

Sports.title: Man Utd boss Mauricio Pochettino issues defiant message after meeting stars for first time
Sports.content:
Man Utd boss Mauricio Pochettino issues defiant message after meeting stars for first time

Mauricio Pochettino met some of his new Manchester United players on Wednesday as he officially started work at the club's Carrington training base

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino started work at Manchester United on Wednesday (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United FC)

Mauricio Pochettino is “not wasting time” after he began work as Manchester United head coach on Wednesday following an overnight flight from the United States.

‌



‌



The Argentinian officially took charge after completing his final duties as United States coach in Cincinnati on Tuesday.

‌



Pochettino, who is understood to have signed a deal until the summer of 2029, flew straight to Manchester and was whisked to the club’s training ground at Carrington to meet United staff and start preparations for Sunday’s Premier League match against Liverpool.

‌



“I have plenty of energy,” Pochettino told United’s website after his whirlwind few days. “It’s a privilege to be head coach of Manchester United. And we are not wasting time. We need to be ready to compete on Sunday.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



“Now it’s not time to think about rest, it’s not time to think about sleep. It’s about being ready and to prepare everything to be sure that we are going to compete in the best condition at Anfield.”

His appointment was announced last Friday, just over 24 hours after United had confirmed the sacking of Michael Carrick following the Red Devils’ worst start to a campaign since 1986.

‌



On Tuesday night, Pochettino asked fans to “give him time” to make United the city’s dominant club again after his last match in charge of the United States. Told by former Manchester City loanee DaMarcus Beasley that “Manchester is blue, it will always be blue” in the TNT Sports US studio after the second leg of the Nations League tie against Haiti, Pochettino responded: “You will see. Give me time.

View 2 Images Pochettino beat Haiti 2-0 in his final game with the USMNT (Image: Omar Vega/USSF/Getty Images)

‌



“The new challenge is a big challenge, but at the same time it’s adrenaline you want to feel.

“We need to add our common sense… we know the situation is not a situation that deserves to be a club like Manchester United, the fan base is amazing.”

‌



Pochettino then gave a very short interview to United club staff after arriving at Carrington. “Very excited to be here,” he said.

“It’s an honour. It’s a privilege to be in this amazing club. Yes, looking forward to start to work.”

‌



He added in a later club video directed at fans: “I am looking forward to meeting you guys. I hear so many good things about you. I hope we bring all the happiness working together and connecting together.

“This is going to be a special season to support and to make our players fight on the field and to get the results that we deserve.”

Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua becomes dad to baby girl weeks before Tyson Fury fight

Joshua, already a dad to 11-year-old JJ, was not present at the birth last weekend as he continues his training camp in Marbella ahead of his clash with Fury

View 2 Images Anthony Joshua and son JJ (Image: INSTAGRAM)

Anthony Joshua has welcomed a baby daughter into the world just three weeks before he takes on Tyson Fury.

‌



‌



Joshua, already a dad to 11-year-old son JJ, was not present at the birth last weekend as he continues his training camp in Marbella ahead of his clash with Fury in Cardiff on December 11. Joshua and the baby's mum, Nicole Osbourne, have not named their daughter who weighed 5.5lb.

‌



“It’s been amazing, a big blessing, and I can’t believe I’m a girl dad. I didn’t want to find the sex out during the pregnancy," he told The Sun. “I love boys but as soon as I found out we had a little girl I said, ‘No more Fifa, no more motorbiking, no more PlayStation!’. Nicole said it was an amazing experience. She said it was easier than JJ and she’s much prettier than JJ. So she’s happy. She’s already deeply in love with her. She’s an amazing mum.

‌

I will change nappies, I’ve gotta go through all that stinky bum time again! Now I’ve got a daughter, I will get an insight and a bit more understanding of what it means to be a woman, and how I can be supportive.

“My daughter will give me a first-hand experience of the power of a woman — I’ve spoken to all the women in my family, and it’s amazing the amount of support that women give each other. We haven’t given her a name yet, but she’s my Princess.”

Anthony Joshua has made a bombshell announcement that he has had a secret child
