Sports.title: Chris Eubank Jr in talks to fight Kell Brook in first bout since Conor Benn loss - with 'Special K' to come out of retirement
Sports.content:
Chris Eubank Jr is in talks to fight Kell Brook in his return to the ring.

Brook, 40, has not fought since beating Amir Khan in 2022, but has emerged as a potential option to fight Eubank in his first fight since losing to Conor Benn late last year.

According to Elliott Amoakoh, the executive director of Eubank Jr's management team, Nova Sport LLC, any agreement is still a way away.

He told Sky Sports: 'Talks are ongoing but the date, purse and location are yet to be confirmed.'

Ben Shalom, however, who has represented both fighters in the past, told talkSPORT: 'It's a fight that we have been trying to make for a couple of months.

'They have pretty much agreed terms on both sides, there is just some final bits to go. It is one of the biggest fights in British boxing. I think you are right on February and in Manchester.'

Chris Eubank Jr (pictured) is in talks with Kell Brook to face off in his return to the ring

Brook (pictured) hasn't fought since 2022 and retired after beating long-term rival Amir Khan

Brook retired after beating long-time rival Khan in Manchester, having been linked with a fight with Eubank in the aftermath.

Brook has seemed almost certain to return to the ring, having revealed his return fight would be 'announced soon'.

He retired with 40 wins from 43 fights, and is a former International Boxing Federation welterweight champion.

Having debuted as a professional in 2004, he didn't lose until September 2016, when he was stopped in the fifth round by Gennady Golovkin.

Eubank Jr, meanwhile, had faced questions over retirement following his defeat by Benn but has refused to call it quits on his 15-year career.

He had claimed to have major fights scheduled for 2026, but has taken a whole year out of action.

Sports.title: English boxer, 18, banned from World Championships after extraordinary sex test mix-up: 'Broken' teenager reveals how his dream was shattered after team forgot to prove he was a man
Sports.content:
English boxer, 18, banned from World Championships after extraordinary sex test mix-up: 'Broken' teenager reveals how his dream was shattered after team forgot to prove he was a man

A teenage English boxer has said they have been left 'broken' after being denied the chance to compete at the World Championships due to officials failing to organise a sex verification test to prove he is male.

George Francis, 18, had been due to represent England at the Under-19 World Championships in Budva, Montenegro last month.

Francis was withdrawn from competition on the eve of the event after an administration error by England Boxing, with the governing body having failed to arrange the necessary sex verification test.

'They got me in a room and told me that I couldn't box because they didn't know if I was a boy or a girl, basically,' Francis told the BBC.

'The explanation was that they couldn't provide a blood sample for me in time. Everyone else was able to provide a blood sample, but they just forgot me.

'Somehow I wasn't on the system.

George Francis, 18, missed out on competing at the Under-19 World Championships after England Boxing failed to arrange a necessary sex verification test. Source: Instagram/georgefrancis_07

'It was the worst news I've ever had in my life.

'I wouldn't wish it on anyone, to be honest. I was just broken. They were speaking to me and I couldn't even really hear. I was devastated.

'I couldn't really talk. I literally couldn't feel anything. There was a hole left there.'

Francis's situation, first reported by The Times, followed the mandatory introduction of sex verification tests by the sport's governing body World Boxing.

World Boxing announced the move last year, with genetic sex testing initially introduced for female competitors aged 18 and above. The governing body stated the move was due to a 'duty of care to deliver safety and competitiveness fairness'.

It followed controversy at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games, where boxers Imane Khelif and Lin Yu-ting won gold.

Khelif and Lin had been disqualified from the previous year's World Championships, with boxing's former governing body – the International Boxing Association – claiming the pair had failed sex eligibility tests.

Earlier this year, Lin was cleared to compete in women's events following a review of her sex eligibility.

World Boxing's mandatory tests were extended to include male boxers earlier this year.

Francis had been required to undergo a test due to turning 18 four days before travelling to the World Championships.

Francis, a multiple national champion, had been required to undergo a mandatory test after turning 18 days before the World Championships. Source: Instagram/georgefrancis_07

World Boxing introduced sex testing last year amid the controversy surrounding Algerian boxer Imane Khelif's participation at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games

The multiple national and GB champion has claimed he is considering turning professional following the mix-up.

England Boxing reportedly contacted Francis's father to apologise for the 'administrative oversight', with the governing body stressing it will 'strengthen processes' to avoid a repeat incident.

'We maintained open communication with George and his family throughout, despite this, a resolution was not possible,' an England Boxing statement read.

'George remained a valued member of the England team, including representing the squad as flag bearer.

'England Boxing has no greater priority than the health and wellbeing of athletes on its performance pathway and are committed to learning from this experience and strengthening our processes to prevent a recurrence.'

World Boxing's policy requires boxers to undergo a once-in-a-lifetime PCR (polymerase chain reaction) test to determine their sex and their eligibility to compete in either the male or female category.

The PCR test is a laboratory technique used to detect specific genetic material, in this case the SRY gene, which reveals the presence of the Y chromosome that is an indicator of male biological sex.

A dozen boxers, representing five nations, were last year blocked from competing at the World Championships in Liverpool because deadlines for their sex tests were missed.

Under World Boxing rules, national federations are responsible for testing and will be required to confirm the sex of their athletes when entering them into World Boxing competitions

Sports.title: Viddal Riley opens up on why he stuck with his dad instead of moving to Las Vegas to train with a Mayweather as he eyes fighting Oleksandr Usyk
Sports.content:
Derrick Riley almost never speaks publicly. Ahead of his son's European title defence against Seydi Coupe at Wembley on Saturday, father and son sat down together to talk about trust, tough love, Joe and Enzo Calzaghe, and why Oleksandr Usyk returning to cruiserweight is 'a little bit greedy'.

But to understand where Viddal is going, you first have to understand the man in his corner.

Derrick Riley has been watching his son get punched since he was a little boy. He still can't put into words what it does to him.

'It's strange,' he exclusively tells Daily Mail Sport. 'I've been doing it for a long time. But you have to try and separate it. You have to shut off the emotion and the sentiment. If you let that sentiment in, I think that's a bad thing. That's your boy in there. He's getting hit and he's getting hurt. I would say it's not easy, and some people can't separate it.'

It's rare to hear Derrick say anything at all. He stays out of the spotlight, and he leaves the talking to his son. Sitting beside Viddal days before the biggest night of his career, when the unbeaten Londoner headlines OVO Arena Wembley against Frenchman Coupe, you quickly see how their relationship works.

'Only my dad would be able to speak to me the way he does,' Viddal says. 'But it comes from a place of genuine care. It's not a job. Someone can only care so much when it's a job. It's like being an employee at a company and having your own business. It's a completely different mentality. This is my business, so he cares and I care.'

WATCH THE EXCLUSIVE INTERVIEW ON THE DAILY MAIL BOXING YOUTUBE CHANNEL

Derrick Riley (R), the father and trainer of son Viddal Riley (L), almost never speaks publicly

Viddal is set to take on Seydi Coupe at Wembley on Saturday evening, headlining the event

Derrick added: 'Part of caring too is the fact it's the same brain you've got now that you're going to need after boxing. You can't go to the shop and buy a new one, so you need to protect it. That's why it's difficult to separate the two.'

Viddal grins and says: 'It's the same brain I need for the grandkids.'

The partnership was not always a given. At 21, Viddal went looking for something of his own.

'I was at a stage where I was trying to find some independence. That's the truth,' he says. 'I was presented with the opportunity to go to Vegas, train with a Mayweather and work with Jeff Mayweather. I was thinking, "Yeah, I'm doing this my way. I'm doing things differently."

'But the truth is, I knew my ceiling was getting lower. And I knew the only person who could push that ceiling higher, and continue to do so, was my dad.

'So when I came back to the UK, I said, "Dad, can you train me?" He was like, "Nah, I'm alright. I'm not doing it." And I was like, "Nah, I need you to do it, because that's the only way this dream we've been talking about is going to be fulfilled."

Derrick's refusal was not stubbornness. It was self-preservation.

When asked why he initially said no, Derrick admitted: 'I know what the game is about. I know what boxing involves, and I thought to myself, do I want that in my life? It's a good question when you're in your 50s. I've lived life. There are no rose-coloured glasses. I know what boxing is. But I had to think about it.'

Derrick Riley has been watching his son get punched since Viddal was a little boy

The irony was that he was already qualified for the job. 'By this point I already had a British Boxing Board of Control licence, because I was in the corner with Viddal in Dubai,' he laughs. 'So, funnily enough, I already had the licence.

'He looked at me with those puppy-dog eyes, and I thought, you know what? We've got to do this. But I did say to him, "It's not going to be easy, son. We're going to have to do this properly. You're going to get no ranking belts, no intercontinental belt, nothing like that. You're going to have to do it the old-school way, with the British, Commonwealth, European, and it's going to be hard." And we've done it, man.'

The record backs him up. Viddal is 14-0 with seven knockouts. He won the European title in April with a wide points win over the vastly experienced Pole Mateusz Masternak at The O2, a fight that also served as an IBF world title eliminator. Saturday is his first defence, and it's a mandatory one against a challenger who is also unbeaten in 14.

For a template of what father and son can achieve together, Derrick points to Wales.

'I appreciate Enzo [Calzaghe] more now than I did before,' he says. 'I've always appreciated him, but I appreciate him even more now because I'm doing it myself. People have no idea what it takes, and for him to do what he did with Joe was absolutely amazing. I take my hat off to him.

'Don't get me wrong, I had a boxing background. I wasn't great, I wasn't pulling up trees, but I had a boxing background. Enzo had no boxing background whatsoever, yet he managed to do what he did with Joe. That is amazing.

'It's funny. During the fight with Bernard Hopkins, I think Enzo was saying something to Joe, and Joe gave Enzo a look. I know that look. I give Viddal that same look.'

Viddal and his father have become a force to be reckoned with but they've faced criticism

Joe Calzaghe has described his own brief split from his father, and how he came back because he realised he wanted those highs to be shared with Enzo. Viddal sees the same story in his own.

'We relate to that story because we were severely doubted,' he says. 'It wasn't celebrated. The partnership is only now starting to get some recognition, with people acknowledging that it works. It wasn't like that at the beginning.

'It's been suggested to me that my dad shouldn't train me and that there are people better suited to the job. That's what we walked into. It wasn't accepted as, "Oh yeah, this is a nice family dynamic, let's get it going." It was challenged. The aim was to separate us.

'When we're up against it, we just keep proving ourselves, time and time again. That's what I take from Enzo and Joe. It wasn't celebrated either. They had to keep doing what they were doing, and he turned his son into a 46-0 fighter and one of the best to have ever done it.'

Fathers who train their sons are often accused of living through them. John Fury, so often more visible than Tyson, is the obvious example. Derrick, a former boxer himself, rejects the comparison.

'I don't live vicariously through Viddal. I don't want that,' he says. 'I'm not hogging the camera. It's not about me. It's about Viddal. He asked me to help him, and I'll help him.'

Viddal is just as clear about who he fights for. 'I do it primarily, first and foremost, for me,' he says. 'And very quickly after that, it's for everyone around me that's put work into me achieving it, because it couldn't be done by myself.

Derrick has said he resonates with Enzo (pictured right) and Joe Calzaghe (pictured left)

'When I became British champion, it made me give my dad the belt. We sat down at home for years watching people pick up the Lonsdale belt and hold the Lonsdale belt. So I heard the announcement, "British champion", and I'm like, "Dad, hold this." That's something he's always deserved.'

By rights, Viddal should already have fought for a world title. When Jai Opetaia was stripped of the IBF belt after signing with Zuffa Boxing, the Masternak win put Viddal in line for a shot at the vacant title against New Zealand's David Nyika. Then Opetaia sued the IBF, the governing body held off sanctioning the fight, and Viddal was left waiting.

At the same time, the division has been turned upside down. Opetaia is moving up to heavyweight to face Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua card in Cardiff on December 11. David Benavidez holds the WBA and WBO belts and faces WBC champion Michal Cieslak next month. And now Oleksandr Usyk wants to come back down.

'As I have been saying, it's messy, but I'm trying to get in the mess,' Viddal says. 'I don't want to be on the outskirts of that mess. I'm trying to be in it.

'Right now, I'm just on the outside of the door. I can hear the music in the club, I can hear the bassline. I know there's a vibe in there. I've been seeing the people getting in the door, walking past me. I want to get in there. And Coupe this weekend is another step towards that.'

The most famous person trying to get through that door is Usyk. The Ukrainian became undisputed at cruiserweight, moved up to become undisputed twice at heavyweight, and his team says he now plans to return to 200lbs to chase Benavidez and become undisputed at cruiserweight again. He hasn't fought at the weight since knocking out Tony Bellew in November 2018, and he turns 40 in January.

Viddal admires him. But he isn't convinced.

'It's a bit greedy. It's a little bit greedy,' he says. 'He's completed the level here. He's gone up, he's completed it there, and I think he's just needing that challenge. He's a guy you can tell lives for challenge. All he does is take challenges. "If I'm fighting for a world title, I'm going to go to your country and I'll beat you there." He's that character. That's what makes him a GOAT. That's what makes him a legend.

Viddal has said Oleksandr Usyk is 'greedy' for returning to the cruiserweight division

'But it's dangerous too. Forty years old, dropping all that weight. He hasn't been a cruiserweight since 2018. If I'm in his circle, I'm saying, "Bro, you ain't got to do this. Why? There's no need to." It's not going to be financial. It's just that craving for a challenge.'

Regardless, Viddal is happy with where he is at.

'What I like is that if I'd done this interview four or five years ago, everyone would have asked me, "Do you want to fight Tommy Fury or Jake Paul?" he says. 'Now people ask me, "Would I fight Usyk?"

'Clearly, I'm doing something right.'

Sports.title: What REALLY triggered HSTikkyTokky's boxing night riot between Tommy Robinson and Mo Deen, as Muslim influencer breaks cover to claim 'set up'
Sports.content:
The Muslim influencer at the heart of HSTikkyTokky's shut-down influencer boxing night claims he was 'told to' attack Tommy Robinson in a 'scripted' moment that sparked a riot which saw a man stabbed and two arrests made.

The 'Unhinged' event, held in Kilkenny, Ireland, and streamed to millions online was held 'without any authorisation from anybody', sources say, and promised to be a 'proper scrap between the most chaotic names in the internet scene' – with Muslim influencer Mo Deen and a rival calling himself MrTikTokUK on the undercard.

But the night, with a capacity of up to 2,000 young fans, had to be cancelled three fights before its conclusion when venue owners refused to let it continue.

HSTikkyTokky, the controversial British 'manosphere' influencer whose real name is Harrison Sullivan, is behind the Unhinged event company. He now claims it has been banned 'worldwide' in the wake of the carnage, while simultaneously talking up a fight card for next month – with hopes that far-Right activist Robinson will fight on it.

At the point of cancellation, Mo Deen had jumped from the ring to attack Robinson, metal chairs were being hurled across the crowd by fighting fans, Sullivan had been hit in the head by a glass bottle and racist and sexist comments were being broadcast on commentary online. Later, one man was stabbed and two people were arrested. One teenager has been charged.

Sullivan suggested the event had run 'absolutely brilliantly' because it was trending online. His claims of his company being cancelled appear to have little substance, sources close to boxing authorities say.

Mo Deen now says he has received death threats from Robinson's supporters and, in one video, suggested he feared a 'hit' would be put out on him.

For all those people who claim Tommy Robinson was simply the victim in what became a mini-riot in Dublin, watch this video.



TR might have well been kicked by MoDeen earlier )or attempted flying kick but debatable if there was actual contact), but it was after that incident had… — Nick Lowles (@lowles_nick) November 8, 2026

A mass brawl erupts at HSTikkyTokky's Unhinged 003 boxing event in Kilkenny on Saturday

Far-right activist Tommy Robinson sparked the violent riot with an altercation inside the ring

Muslim influencer Mo Deen has claimed he was 'told to' attack Robinson in a 'scripted' moment

At the Hub in Kilkenny, a 1,900-capacity community venue which hosted The Boomtown Rats at the start of the year and is welcoming Irish singer Gavin James next month, an already violent event broke out into a brawl after an altercation between Robinson and Deen – whose real name is Mohammad Kubba.

Robinson, currently on bail after being found guilty in October of harassing two Daily Mail journalists in a campaign that caused them to fear for their safety, arrived in Kilkenny as a ringside guest, accompanied by a large contingent of his supporters. He is due back in court on December 16 for sentencing, with the hearing potentially to result in a custodial sentence.

The chaotic scenes in Kilkenny were preceded by an equally unruly press conference on Friday evening, where multiple fighters launched themselves at one another in a series of violent clashes involving streamers, rappers, OnlyFans models and convicted sex offender-turned-YouTuber Paul Flaherty.

Flaherty, who was jailed for five years in 2018 after being convicted of sexually assaulting a woman he met on Tinder, had already been embroiled in a chaotic brawl at a Unhinged promotional event in September, with footage of the confrontation quickly going viral online.

Tensions rose on Saturday night when Sullivan and his influencer friend Ed Matthews, who starred alongside HSTikkyTokky in Louis Theroux's documentary Inside The Manosphere, invited Robinson to join them at the commentators' desk before Deen's fight.

Holding a copy of his book, The Grooming Gang Cover-Up, the 43-year-old activist made a series of inflammatory remarks about Islam, claiming that 'Muslims have been raping our country for 100 years' and citing false statistics about Muslim men and sexual offences.

After defeating MrTikTokUK, Deen – whose real name is Mohammad Kubba – climbed out of the ring and launched himself at Robinson with a flying kick, in a moment he has since claimed was staged and designed to raise tensions ahead of a potential future bout between the two.

Deen took to social media to claim his attack was staged as he sought refuge in a utility room

The initial brawl spilled into the crowd but was largely contained by security, who managed to defuse the situation. Deen, 41, subsequently left the venue as the remaining bouts got underway, only to be escorted back inside by event security after it was claimed Sullivan called for him to return and face Robinson in the ring.

Sullivan has denied the claim as well as the claim by Deen that he was following a script.

With tensions through the roof, and many racially diverse spectators left furious at Robinson's previous remarks, the far-Right activist launched his book towards Deen, sparking a physical brawl that violently went out of control.

Robinson was grabbed as punches were thrown, while people from both entourages were caught up in the melee.

Violence quickly spread through the crowd, with chairs and metal barriers hurled across the venue, spectators exchanging blows and others scrambling to escape the commotion as security desperately attempted to intervene.

A string of videos showing people screaming, pushing and throwing punches were published to social media in real time as the chaos continued for approximately 20 minutes. Shouts of 'Oh Tommy Robinson' bellowed out from the riot before the livestream, which was broadcast on platform Kick to approximately 1.8million viewers, eventually cut to black.

Police, who had been alerted to disturbances at the venue before the mass brawl broke out, arrested and detained a man in his 20s after another man was stabbed and rushed to hospital earlier in the evening.

A teenager was also arrested by the Gardai and charged with violent disorder.

‘Gardai attended the scene of a number of incidents on the night of Saturday 7th November, 2026 at approximately 9pm at a premises on the Dublin Road, Kilkenny,’ a police statement read.

’One male, aged in his 30s was assaulted and removed from the scene to St. Luke’s Hospital. A man, aged in his 20s was arrested and is currently detained under Section 4 at a Garda station in the South East.

‘A second male was arrested, an adult in his teens, for violent disorder and has since been charged. He is due to appear in court later today, no court sitting has been set at this time. Investigations ongoing.’

Despite the arrests and widespread violence, Sullivan attempted to restart the remaining bouts without spectators, solely for the event's livestream, before a visibly upset venue representative intervened to stop him.

Robinson brawled with Deen and his entourage after being invited into the ring by Sullivan

Robinson greets the event's organiser HSTikkyTokky, whose real name is Harrison Sullivan

HSTikkyTokky CRASHED OUT after someone in the crowd THREW a GLASS BOTTLE at him while he was interviewing a fighter 😳 pic.twitter.com/Uq8uSghkXC — clipmate (@clipmxte) November 7, 2026

A spokesman for the Hub has since said in a statement to Kilkenny Live: 'Following an incident the decision was made by the management of the venue to step in and stop the promotions company from continuing with their event.

'The Hub has a zero-tolerance policy towards violence, aggression or disorderly behaviour.'

As the violence unfolded, Deen took to social media claiming his initial confrontation with Robinson had been staged for entertainment but spiralled out of control.

As he and his entourage sought refuge in a small utility room, Deen urged that his post-fight fly kick was scripted as he hurriedly told his crew to 'lock the doors'.

'The whole place is surrounded,' a concerned Deen said as wild shouting could be heard in the background.

'There's fights everywhere, we're locked in a room right now. Listen I'll make this clear to every single person in the UK. I'm not trying to cause problems. This is like WWE, they said this is what the situation is. I followed the script.

'I'm getting death threats, people trying to kill me. I don't know about this, I just know this is what we had to do. Why is everyone trying to kill me right now?

'This is a message to all supporters of Tommy, supporters, gangs, whatever you are. I just followed the script they told me to agree with. Tommy's agreed to it, they've agreed to it, I followed it.'

'Look at my hands bro,' he added looking visibly shaken. 'My guys are getting rushed, look at my friend's face bro. This whole thing is crazy.'

Deen went on to plead with Elon Musk, whom he described as one of Robinson's 'friends', and the activist's wider network of supporters not to 'put a hit out' on him.

'A fight is a fight, hopefully anyone who is with Tommy and is friends and that, Elon Musk or whatever, don't put hits out on me,' he added, holding his hand to his heart.

Sullivan, who initially stated that the event went 'absolutely brilliantly' because it was trending globally, has refuted Deen's claims that the fight and aftermath was staged.

In a video on his YouTube channel, Sullivan said: 'I was sat next to Tommy. Do you think that I wanted to get f***ing fly-kicked and f***ing some fat belly over me? My watch nearly got popped off. Do you think that that was a plan? No. The plan was for them to face off in the ring.'

The 25-year-old manosphere influencer also dismissed claims that he intentionally attempted to stage an impromptu bare-knuckle fight between Robinson and Deen when the Muslim fighter was escorted back into the venue.

According to The Guardian, Sullivan repeatedly shouted 'let Tommy fight him' while Robinson's entourage – referred to by the YouTuber as 'Tommy's boys' – were permitted to enter the ring to face off with Deen and Co.

He added: 'What is that nonsense? You think I would want them to have a bare-knuckle fight for free, not to just face off and hype up the next event?'

🚨MUST SEE: Hstikkytokky has OFFICIALLY SOLD AWAY his UNHINGED PROMOTIONS COMPANY…



He goes on to apologise to all fans and every supporter 😳



HS: “I’ve had message from police and the boxing commission, I am no longer able to host @UnhingedEvents pic.twitter.com/6EopqIhyMr — KickClipz (@Kickclipzfeed) November 8, 2026

Chairs were hurled and punches were thrown as the event descended into absolute chaos

HSTikkyTokky appeared on Louis Theroux's Inside the Manosphere documentary this year

Sources have told Daily Mail Sport influencer events such as Saturday's Unhinged 003 tend to take place without authorisation from any official boxing body.

HSTikkyTokky had promoted the event as a 'proper scrap between two of the most chaotic names in the internet scene', with British rappers Russ Millions and Kirky set to headline a card that was ultimately abandoned before their bout could take place.

After initially hinting that a potential bout between Robinson and Deen had been in the works for next month, Sullivan appeared crestfallen on a later video as he called an end to Unhinged Promotions, claiming they had been shut down from operating 'worldwide'.

'I've had a lot of messages from police around the world, message from the boxing commission... I am not allowed to put an Unhinged event on anymore after Tommy Robinson riots at Kilkenny last night,' he said on his channel.

'Obviously it's massively disappointing, I wanted to grow the company Unhinged Promotions, I wanted to make it massive and huge and take over the world but the risks that have come in play from the decisions some of my staff have made has now led to us having to cancel any future event. We won't be back, but I will sure be supporting some of the other promotions around the world.

'I just want to apologise to the internet. I didn't want to ever have to put on events that risked the safety of people that came to support. I'm super sorry and I won't be doing an event again. I wish I could, but I'm not allowed to now.'

In case the message wasn't already clear, he stated again: 'There is no venue around the world that will take me, there is literally nothing I can do. I feel cornered, I feel lost, I feel gutted. I feel jobless, this was my passion, my desire, my life.

'Now it's been taken away from me over something that was meant to be a light-hearted promotion for the next event. I'm gutted and I want to say again, sorry to everyone.'

Sullivan's self-pitying demeanour offered a stark contrast to the buoyant figure he immediately cut after the chaotic event, which he claimed went 'absolutely brilliantly'. Footage from earlier in the night had shown him being hit by a glass bottle thrown from the crowd while he stood in the ring.

Thrilled that Unhinged's third event had trended globally on social media platforms as a result of the riots, he said: 'I think it went absolutely brilliantly. Listen it was controversial as f*** but please tell me other promotion on their third event is trending globally on Twitter like this, has generated over 200 million views across TikTok, Twitter and Instagram.

'So everyone who's hating, you're clearly still watching. The fights were absolutely brilliant up until the venue got closed down.

'I'm gutted that we didn't get to see the final three fights but s*** happens. I totally hold accountability for misjudging the amount of security that was needed and the types of people that were coming. I misjudged that.

'But what I won't listen to is that wasn't a f***ing great night of entertainment. It was huge. Every single person is watching what I do. Every single person likes to talk about what I do because I'm the number one at what I do.'

Robinson was holding a copy of his book, The Grooming Gang Cover-Up, as he entered the ring

Robinson, who is on bail before his sentencing in December, said 'Muslims have been raping our country for 100 years' as he riled up the crowd with inflammatory remarks about Islam

Irish mobster Paul Flaherty just KNOCKED OUT a boxer at HSTikkyTokky’s Unhinged boxing press conference 😳 pic.twitter.com/NHVJFG10Ij — vxdeo (@vxdeo) September 17, 2026

Sullivan has seen other boxing events shut down in the past. In January, he complained that 'hundreds' of complainants had called the local council and police to cancel a show in Basildon, saying that one of his fighters was a 'convicted child predator'.

The mayor of Kilkenny called the scenes this weekend 'absolutely disgraceful'. Andrew McGuinness said on local radio station KCLR: 'I am absolutely disgusted Kilkenny was used as a backdrop for such a horrendously managed event.

'They are grooming young people to behave in a way that's absolutely disgraceful. They have no respect for themselves, no respect for other people and particularly no respect for women.

'They groom thousands of people into going to these events. The fact there were minors and teenagers at the event is just absolutely appalling.'

Sports.title: Troubled ex-boxing world champion Adrien Broner wheeled out of concert and slumps over couch after falling unresponsive
Sports.content:
Troubled former boxer Adrien Broner has sparked major concern after viral footage showed him falling unresponsive at a concert on Saturday night.

Former four division boxing champion Broner, 37, was seen in the worrying state during a livestream while attending a 'Skilla Baby' concert in downtown Los Angeles.

In the viral footage, Broner could be seen looking dazed before slumping over on a couch. An EMS worker attended to him and helped carry him to a flight of stairs.

While taking Broner down the stairs, the ex-boxer appeared to fall in and out of consciousness before eventually regaining enough composure to walk down.

In the end, Broner was loaded into a wheelchair by friends and the EMS worker before being taken backstage and into a car outside the music venue.

It marks the latest concerning incident involving Broner, who recently had a run-in with police in Beverly Hills.

Troubled former boxer Adrien Broner has sparked major concern after viral footage showed him falling unresponsive at a concert

Broner had to be helped down a flight of stairs by an EMS worker while at the concert

At the end of October, Broner was among a group of men recording content on the streets of Beverly Hills for the social media platform, Kick, when local police arrived.

Viral footage from the incident shows the group recording what appears to be a music video involving both Broner and his fellow content creator, Deen The Great.

A separate clip showed Broner with his arms raised and walking backwards towards a pair of officers, who ultimately placed him in handcuffs.

Broner was seen trying to poke fun at the situation by doing a funny walk for the officers' benefit, but they did not seem amused.

'Broner was detained during a traffic stop as part of an investigation into a large street gathering in a residential area,' Beverly Hills police told TMZ in a statement. 'He was released from the scene and a citation was not issued.'

Broner is also currently among several defendants being sued in Los Angeles County over allegations of sexual battery, battery and assault.

'Plaintiff alleges that Broner repeatedly pressured Plaintiff for sexual activity after repeated refusals, attempted to isolate Plaintiff, repeatedly pressured Plaintiff while intoxicated, attempted unwanted physical contact, publicly humiliated Plaintiff, and made false sexual statements about Plaintiff to a livestream audience,' read the complaint, obtained by The Daily Mail.

Broner has denied any wrongdoing in the case.

Previously, in September of 2025, Broner was kicked off rapper Cam'ron's popular podcast after ignoring the host's warnings to stop flirting with his on-air co-host.

Sports.title: Hamilton insists there are no "trust" problems at Ferrari
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has insisted there are zero “trust” problems at Ferrari despite him overruling strategic calls becoming a repeated occurrence across recent Formula 1 grands prix.

The seven-time world champion has ignored calls to pit in two of the last four rounds - Singapore and Brazil - with both backfiring on the Scuderia driver.

In Singapore he elected to keep track position under a virtual safety car, but on worn tyres he dropped from podium contention to sixth late on - for which he apologised afterwards.

Then in Brazil last time out, Hamilton stayed on slicks despite the rain intensifying and this led to a late spin at the final corner before pitting the following lap to eventually finish ninth.

Those instances came amid talk of fractious relations down at Ferrari but ahead of this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix, Hamilton confirmed all is well - particularly with his new-for-2026 race engineer Carlo Santi.

“It’s definitely not a trust thing, we’re constantly working on our communication,” said the 41-year-old.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

"It's been a lot better this year. Carlo has done an amazing job and those particular two times, particularly the last time, was just I didn't have the information I needed.

“I got the call right at the last minute. We'll just continue to work on the processes. We're super united in what's working, in the right direction."

This year has been much improved for Hamilton, who is fourth in the standings with three rounds remaining, currently on 261 points compared to his total of 156 in 2025.

His first year in Ferrari colours was certainly underwhelming, but there have still been signs of improvement in 2026 despite it being a significant jump from last season.

Not only is that in reference to the strategic calls, but also his connection with team-mate Charles Leclerc, clashing on a few occasions and most notably in Mexico three weeks ago.

It cost Ferrari the win and Hamilton subsequently criticised Leclerc’s “do or die” attitude, before suggesting in Sao Paulo that the Monegasque races him harder than he does with other drivers.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Yuri Cortez / AFP via Getty Images

That led to an hour-long meeting between both Scuderia drivers plus team boss Fred Vasseur and Hamilton and Leclerc are now confident that the issue has been resolved.

“Charles is a great driver,” said Hamilton. “The detail we went into about stuff like that, in terms of when we close the visor, it's very clear, we understand each other, we understand each other's boundaries and the ultimate goal, which is to get the best result for the team.

“So I don't feel like that will be a problem moving forward. I have no concerns or worries about racing him, and I don't think he does for me either.”

The talk surrounding the Mexico clash was naturally high, but Leclerc reckons that is a consequence of driving for Ferrari and all focus is now on securing runner-up in the constructors’ standings.

“Everything has been taken out of proportion,” said Leclerc. “I'm kind of used to it now, driving for Ferrari for so many years. But things are very often taken out of proportion.

“The goal is not always to agree and that will never happen. We can have different opinions and that was the case, for example, in Mexico.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

“But just the fact of speaking eased all tensions and we were completely fine with it. It's not that we had to speak for an hour, even though it ended up lasting an hour, just because we had a good time.

“We started speaking about many other things in trying to bring the team and to help the team go forward.

“But the discussion about the tension was like maybe five or 10 minutes and then the air was clean and that's it.”

Ferrari heads into the Vegas race 95 points ahead of third-placed Red Bull and 142 behind Mercedes, who clinched its ninth title at Interlagos.

Sports.title: Who has the best F1 power unit: Red Bull or Mercedes? Russell shares interesting theory
Sports.content:
The Las Vegas Grand Prix promises to be an interesting challenge for Formula 1 teams in several respects, arguably even more so than in previous years. With the 2026 cars producing less downforce and relying on active aerodynamics, getting temperature into the Pirelli tyres – and, given the long straights, keeping it there – promises to be even more difficult than before.

According to newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli, this factor will determine who gets to lift the Las Vegas GP winners' trophy on Saturday night, although another aspect should not be underestimated either: energy management.

During a weekend in which much of the discussion has centred on the return of V8 engines, the reality remains that the 2026 power units have significant limitations, many of which will be exposed again in Las Vegas.

Verstappen described the simulator work as “painful”, a sentiment echoed by other drivers. Clipping is once again expected to play a major role on the long straight, with Antonelli also warning about the return of “yo-yo racing”.

Although that is hardly good news in itself, it does raise an interesting question: who currently has the best power unit at these energy-poor circuits?

At the beginning of this year, the answer was clearly Mercedes, while efficiency on the electrical side of the power unit was still a weakness for Red Bull. Although the newcomer from Milton Keynes has not received an ADUO token and has therefore been unable to make hardware changes, it has made significant progress in terms of efficiency and learning how to optimise its power unit for each circuit.

Nevertheless, Verstappen still points to Mercedes as the benchmark at an energy-poor track like Las Vegas.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

“In Baku, we were probably not the strongest in that regard. I hope that it will be a little bit better here, but I think Mercedes is normally the strongest on that side, with maximising that.”

When Autoport subsequently put those comments to Russell, the Mercedes driver offered a nuanced reply. According to him, it is not so easy to distinguish between the internal combustion engine and the electrical components, and the picture from the beginning of this year is not necessarily valid.

“I do think we've probably got the most efficient electrical management, but I think it's unfair sometimes to separate the two things,” Russell said. “You've got to develop a car and a power unit and a battery deployment setup that all contribute to one another.”

And it is precisely in this respect that different manufacturers and teams make different compromises, according to Russell.

“You can compromise the ICE to give you more, and vice versa. And you can compromise your aero package to give you more power. We could achieve more power from the engine, but we would have to take a sacrifice with the aerodynamics.”

When Russell takes all those factors into account, however, his conclusion is clear: “On the whole, I think Red Bull, on the power unit side, are the team to beat right now. So I just look at that as over the course of a lap and not distinguishing between ICE and battery.”

George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

An interesting point is that, according to Russell, the picture from the beginning of this year is no longer valid for two reasons. Firstly, the competition – particularly Red Bull – has made progress in extracting performance from its power unit, but secondly, Russell says the drag levels of the W17 have changed, particularly following the upgrade in Malaysia.

“I think earlier this year, we had an exceptionally efficient car. With our previous package, we were considerably faster than the other Mercedes power unit cars on the straights,” he said.

“Since we brought the new package, we've added drag to the car. And I think that has kind of scuppered people's views a bit on what's power and what's drag. As I said, you can't just draw a line in the sand and say, it's battery, it's ICE, it's chassis.”

The additional drag mentioned by Russell could potentially be a handicap in Vegas, but it is precisely in this area that his team-mate Antonelli also sees a positive for Mercedes: “I think Red Bull is going to be very strong this weekend. However, I think we're the only one who has a set of wings that is slightly less downforce-wise, so a bit less drag. Let's see if we're going to use it here, but definitely it's going to be very interesting.”

At Monza – another energy-poor circuit – Antonelli produced a particularly memorable recovery drive, his most emotional F1 win to date, but he expects the opposition in Vegas to be stronger than it was at his home race.

“I think our power unit has been very strong on the electrical side, obviously also on the combustion, but the electrical side has been very strong. I think we're probably the most efficient ones in terms of electrical power and efficiency,” Antonelli said.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Mark Sutton / Formula 1 via Getty Images

“However, Red Bull, they have a very strong power unit as well, and their car is very efficient on the straight, especially with the Macarena wing they have.

“I think our main competitor will be Red Bull this weekend, probably McLaren as well. And let’s see how Ferrari will do here. This track is an outlier, so it’s definitely going to be interesting.”

All the problems with energy management and the 2026 power units are painful to watch, but in a sense, Vegas does provide an interesting benchmark for determining who leads the way at energy-poor circuits – with one crucial caveat, as Antonelli rightly points out: tyre temperature could overshadow everything in Sin City.

Sports.title: Honda reveals key F1 power unit change for 2027
Sports.content:
Immediately after the Brazilian Grand Prix, Honda was still unable to fully explain Lance Stroll's DNF. The Canadian was forced to retire for the 14th time, equalling the all-time record for the most retirements in a single Formula 1 season.

Ahead of the race weekend in Las Vegas, Honda has gathered more information about the battery failure, with chief engineer Shintaro Orihara explaining when asked by Autosport about the problem: "After Brazil, we have done some inspection on the battery and we found, as expected, what happened.

"It's a kind of expected issue. We thought we applied a countermeasure for Brazil, but that was not enough to prevent a battery issue from happening.

"Then for this event, we brought another countermeasure to get better reliability. I can't explain the exact details of it, but after the Brazilian GP, we did the inspection and found out what happened."

The Japanese engineer immediately added that he was not sure whether the additional measure introduced for Las Vegas would be enough to prevent a repeat of the problem.

"The countermeasure we brought to this event will probably, how to say, not fully prevent it. We still need to get a complete picture and understanding."

Orihara also revealed that the battery will be one of the areas Honda changes for next year. The Sakura-based manufacturer will no longer rely solely on countermeasures, instead seeking to address the problem more fundamentally.

Shintaro Orihara, Honda Racing Corporation Trackside General Manager and Chief Engineer Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / LAT Images via Getty Images

"But for 2027, we will update the structure inside the battery to have better reliability. We're still working on it in Sakura, but they realised that they need to improve reliability of battery for next year.

"And we need to keep bringing countermeasures for this year as well, to have good reliability and to accumulate more mileage on the car."

The word 'structure' could theoretically refer to several aspects, but when asked for clarification, Honda confirmed that it concerns "the internal structure of the energy store to increase robustness and overall reliability".

The need for this change had already become apparent before Stroll's retirement in Brazil, although Orihara explained that the lessons learned from the latest failure can still be used to improve the 2027 power unit.

"For our 2027 battery, we developed another structure, but we can still learn something from this year's issue to improve our reliability," he said.

"So it was not directly leading [to the change for 2027], but in some areas, we can learn from this year's reliability. That's why we keep bringing countermeasures to improve our reliability. That will help us for next year as well."

Previous combustion breakthroughs no longer work under 2026 rules

While the battery change is primarily intended to improve reliability, Honda's focus in terms of outright performance remains on the internal combustion engine.

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing, Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

Orihara has already explained in an interview with Autosport that improving energy management or efficiency is of little use if the ICE is significantly lacking in outright power, which is why that remains the key focus for 2027.

The chief engineer acknowledged in Las Vegas that combustion works somewhat differently under the current regulations than it did previously, meaning Honda could no longer use some of the tried-and-tested solutions from the previous cycle. This initially sent the manufacturer down the wrong path.

"Under the previous regulations, we found what we call rapid combustion. That gave us a lot of performance under those regulations," Orihara admitted.

"We started our development for this year, so for this regulation, with the rapid combustion as well, but then we realised that we needed to improve combustion further beyond the rapid combustion.

"Still now, we are on the way to overcome rapid combustion. That is what we are focusing on now and for the future. Rapid combustion gave us good performance, but sometimes it's challenging to manage the combustion itself.

"The main difference under this regulation is that we no longer have a cylinder pressure sensor. Under this regulation, we need to find some other combustion style to get more performance and that's an area we are working on to improve."

Finally, Orihara acknowledged that Honda's outright peak power is at the required level at times, but that controlling it and delivering it consistently remains particularly challenging.

"If we have good control, we can keep that peak power in a wider range. But if we don't have good control, we just get peak power, but without that wider range, there’s less torque delivery or torque accuracy. So yes, we need to improve combustion control and combustion performance under this regulation."

Sports.title: Why Verstappen's ideal F1 rules would make some circuits off-limits
Sports.content:
Although the FIA's announcement was only online for five minutes, there is no doubt in the paddock that V8 engines will return to Formula 1. An agreement in principle has been reached on a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 with a smaller electrical component, which is set to be introduced in 2030 rather than 2031.

Max Verstappen is one of the biggest critics of the current regulations and therefore one of the strongest advocates for change. He welcomes F1’s future plans, but says it is too early to tell whether they could keep him in the series for longer.

"I don’t know. For sure it’s better, but I cannot tell you now what I will do after 2030. But for the sport itself, it’s a good choice," he said.

The contract Verstappen signed ahead of the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort runs until the end of 2030, meaning he will get a taste of the new regulations regardless. Alongside the V8 engines, the new rules are also expected to include a further reduction in car weight.

When Autosport asked Verstappen whether the plans for 2030 are what he himself would have come up with if he were writing the rules, the Dutchman made it clear that this is not entirely the case.

"No, but that’s also because [with my plans] you would not be allowed to race at some tracks because it would be too loud! If it is up to me, then I would take the turbo off. And I would get rid of the [electrical] power. Well, maybe you can use it as a push-to-pass, but not too much on the battery side anymore. But then on some tracks you are not allowed to race," Verstappen said, referring to the noise restrictions that many circuits face nowadays.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

For street tracks in major cities, this would logically be an even bigger problem.

Verstappen added: "Fuel consumption also goes up a lot without the turbo, so you would need a bigger tank if you don’t want to do refuelling during the races. So then, of course, I understand that you want to have a turbo."

Besides this practical argument, retaining the turbo was also important from a political perspective, for example to keep Audi and Honda on board.

With all those factors in mind, Verstappen does see this compromise as an important step in the right direction for F1.

"If it’s fully up to me, then of course I would go back to a V10 or whatever. That sounds even better, but I know that’s not something realistic.

"But this is good. This is for sure in the right direction. But again, it’s not confirmed yet, so I guess there are a few things that they still need to agree on."

Nevertheless, this agreement in principle does seem to indicate that F1 and the FIA have taken drivers' complaints about clipping, super clipping and other issues with the 2026 power units seriously when considering the future.

Verstappen agrees, but also believes that even F1's leading figures realise things cannot continue as they are, even if they would never admit that publicly: "It’s probably a combination of maybe listening to our advice, but also realising that what we have now is not what you want! So yeah, it’s probably a bit of a combination."

Sports.title: Alonso won't stay for V8 return: "F1 has lost 16 years of pure racing"
Sports.content:
Although the FIA's formal confirmation on Tuesday was only online for a few minutes before being temporarily taken down again, it is clear to everyone in the paddock that V8 engines will return to Formula 1.

The agreement in principle involves a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 – with the turbo being particularly important for Audi and Honda – and a significantly smaller electrical component. The target for its introduction is 2030, which would be a year earlier than initially planned.

Read Also: Formula 1 The factors behind the abortive 2030 F1 rules announcement

It is largely what the drivers have been pushing for, which explains the positive reactions in the Las Vegas paddock during the media day.

Fernando Alonso, however, stressed to media including Autosport that the V8 return will come too late for him. The Spaniard is currently 45 and, perhaps unsurprisingly, has no intention of remaining in the pinnacle of motorsport for another four years: "No, I will not be around for the new V8. 100%."

When it was pointed out that Alonso has surprised people in the paddock before, for example with his F1 comeback in 2021, he laughed: "Yeah, I have surprised myself in the past as well! But this time I think it's the good one. When I stop, it will be the moment, also the moment to try different things.

"It's still a long way ahead, [the V8 return], but I think it will be enough [for me before that]."

Alonso does find it frustrating, in a sense, that he will have to bow out under a set of regulations that he, like many other drivers, is far from fond of: "Yes, it's frustrating that we didn't have it in 2014 already. From 2014 to 2030 or 2031, so that means 16 years or 17 years of pure racing are lost."

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: James Sutton / Formula 1 / Formula Motorsport Ltd via Getty Images

While Alonso will no longer be competing in F1 by then, he still has his sights set on other racing categories. Even after retiring from F1, Alonso intends to continue racing for a long time.

In January 2027, he will make an appearance at the Dakar Rally, but he is also leaving the door open to other iconic races once his F1 career comes to an end.

"Dakar was on my mind. Le Mans is on my mind, the Indy 500 is on my mind," the Aston Martin driver said.

"I love competing and I love competing in race cars in which you have power when you go on throttle, and in which you have deceleration when you brake. Those are the things that we miss now in Formula 1.

"Obviously, if I continue in Formula 1, that will always be my priority and it's difficult to put things together or to combine different programs. Dakar, because it's in January, it fits a little bit better, but even that had to come with a few coincidences."

That Alonso would like to return to endurance races such as Le Mans is no surprise – he would even like to do so alongside Max Verstappen – but his mention of the Indy 500 is somewhat more unexpected.

After his last attempt in 2020, the Spaniard did not seem particularly keen on another appearance at The Greatest Spectacle in Racing at the Brickyard, but with a new IndyCar chassis on the way, his opinion could change.

"Yeah, I don't know. They will change cars soon. There's a new car coming for 2028, I think, so yeah, I don't know," he said. "I may consider it one day. It’s not in my short-term plans and not on my mind now, but I cannot say no to it 100%."

Fernando Alonso, Arrow McLaren SP Chevrolet Photo by: Michael L. Levitt / Motorsport Images

Sports.title: Cadillac retaining Bottas for F1 2027 is the logical move
Sports.content:
The longest-running contract saga of the Formula 1 season is now at an end. Not that it has been blockbuster material, since it revolves around a team struggling to lift itself from the back of the grid.

Still, the easy option for Cadillac F1's stakeholders would have been to throw Valtteri Bottas under the bus after a year in which he has been outqualified by team-mate Sergio Perez 11-9 – and finished behind the Mexican in five of the six races where they both reached the chequered flag. The optics of falling off Perez to the tune of up to two seconds a lap in Azerbaijan and Singapore were conspicuously bad.

While Bottas is liked and respected within the team, the delay in coming to a decision to trigger the extension clause within what's understood to have been a "one plus one" contract is very telling.

It's been known since the summer that there is a significant disparity between the team's own assessment of its progress and that of its ultimate owners. In common with the majority of the F1 paddock, former team principal Graeme Lowdon was wont to opine that getting two functional cars to the grid in the season opener was a tremendous achievement, given the compressed timescales involved in setting Cadillac up from scratch.

But the cars haven't always been functional and certainly haven't looked like escaping from Q1 regularly. Owner TWG Motorsports and its partner, General Motors, clearly expected much more than this, hence the summer decapitation exercise in which Lowdon was axed in favour of Marcin Budkowski, the former aerodynamicist who has latterly held senior management and technical roles with Alpine and the FIA.

Although there have been outlier DNFs caused by engine issues and ‘finger trouble', such as the cross-threaded wheelnut that eliminated Bottas from the Sao Paulo GP, a statistically significant cluster of reliability and performance problems relate to managing brake temperatures. While these have resulted in retirements through failures in the brakes and adjacent components (such as the suspension), they have also compromised performance in races the drivers actually finished (ie through having to lift-and-coast).

Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing, Sergio Perez, Cadillac Racing Photo by: Mark Thompson / Getty Images

While Lowdon often described the brake-temperature issues as symptomatic of the challenges a ‘new' team faces, this clearly didn't wash with his ultimate bosses. But here we run into the knowledge gap between experienced engineers and armchair experts. It would be very easy, with the wave of a pen or some clattering on a keyboard, to say the solution to excessive brake temperatures is to fit bigger ducts.

The actual science is rather more complicated than that, since the aerodynamic detailing required to optimise brake cooling has to consider management of the airflow and temperatures across both axles, and factor in the tyres as well. It's a delicate interplay of compromises which defies easy answers.

Bottas has also frequently alluded to unexplained fluctuations in performance the team has yet to understand.

With all this in mind, keeping faith with an experienced driver line-up makes rational sense, although it is understood to have been the topic of much debate behind the scenes. One only has to witness the usually eloquent Budkowski's tongue-tied responses to questions on the subject to realise there have been significant differences of opinion at senior level.

TWG Motorsports CEO Dan Towriss has invested a great deal of energy in supporting Colton Herta, the team's test and reserve driver, through the transition from IndyCar to Formula 2.

Cadillac's stated aim is to bring an American driver into Formula 1.

"I back myself 100 percent on everything," Herta said after his FP1 outing in Mexico. "I can be as quick as anybody. I think I have the capability of learning very quickly too, and picking up on things. So 1000 percent, I back myself in being able to do this [getting an F1 seat].

Colton Herta Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

"Whether that means next year or the following year, I really don't know what the plan is at the moment. We'll have to wait and see. I think some decisions will hopefully be made within the next month."

That prognostication came true, but the result was that Herta will remain in a holding pattern for now. It's understood that Mercedes test and reserve driver Frederik Vesti entered the conversations regarding 2027, since he is known to TWG Motorsports on account of racing for Cadillac in IMSA.

Realistically, though, Vesti is on the glide path to a career in sportscars having not competed in single-seaters since 2023, when he was Oliver Bearman's stablemate in F2 and finished runner-up to Theo Pourchaire. Mercedes insiders describe him as a safe pair of hands, but two or three tenths off the team's full-time F1 drivers.

Likewise Jak Crawford, who would tick the US-born driver box and is currently Aston Martin's reserve, wasn't considered a meaningful performance upgrade on Bottas. Esteban Ocon, fresh on the market after being dropped by Haas, wasn't even a fringe candidate given his previous bad blood with Perez, along with his well-known tendency to be spooked by the kind of technical poltergeists to which the Cadillac seems prone.

In the longer term there is Ugo Ugochukwu, who is moving up to F2 next season after taking the F3 title this year. Ugochukwu's stock has risen again after a difficult rookie F3 campaign in which he appeared caught up in the wider issues afflicting the Prema organisation, and was dropped by McLaren from its driver-development programme. But doubts remain over whether his 1.92m frame can be accommodated in an F1 car without compromising performance, given the inherent packaging limitations of the current formula.

For 2027 at least, there will be no change in the line-up. What this makes very clear is that a consensus has been reached, however uneasy, that car performance remains Cadillac's biggest shortcoming – and sacrificing Bottas won't fix that.

Sports.title: Cadillac completes F1 2027 driver pairing
Sports.content:
Incumbent Valtteri Bottas will remain with the Cadillac Formula 1 team through 2027 after the US-owned team decided against fast-tracking American test driver Colton Herta to a race seat.

Bottas will stay on board with Cadillac alongside Sergio Perez as initially planned, with both race-winning veterans having signed a multi-year deal when they initially joined F1's 11th team.

But after struggling for pace against the Mexican, Bottas’ seat came under increased scrutiny within the organisation and majority owner TWG Motorsports, led by CEO Dan Towriss, weighed up whether to give Herta a chance as early as 2027.

After all, the team had spared no expense readying the former IndyCar star for racing in F1, including a tough F2 campaign and an increasing number of FP1 outings to ensure the 26-year-old Californian would reach the required threshold of 40 FIA superlicence points.

Bottas' fortunes were not helped by a series of performance, reliability and parts consistency issues with the rookie team, which has made the Finn's form harder to judge fairly.

And with Cadillac still far removed from being a frontline F1 operation, Towriss and team principal Marcin Budkowski now appear to have agreed that Bottas' vast F1 experience - which currently spans 265 grand prix starts - is what will benefit the team the most in 2027.

Cadillac said on Wednesday: "The announcement provides continuity and stability as Cadillac builds on its first season on the grid. It continues its long-term ambition to establish a competitive team at the pinnacle of global motorsport.”

Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

This now completes the 22-car grid next year with Cadillac yet to issue an update on what's next for Herta, saying "reserve and test drivers will be announced in due course”.

Bottas, 37, who has 10 race wins, said: "To whom it may concern, I’m staying! I’m excited to continue this journey with Cadillac into 2027. We knew building a new Formula 1 team from the ground up wasn’t going to be easy, but that’s exactly what makes this challenge so special.

"We’ve laid the foundations, we’re learning and improving, and there’s still plenty more to come, I’m hungry for more, and I believe in what we’re building together. The story is only just getting started."

Towriss added: "Valtteri’s experience, perspective and commitment are important strengths for our team. Continuity gives us a strong platform as we continue developing the team and working toward our ambitions in Formula 1.

“On the eve of the Las Vegas GP, everyone in the team is pleased to have Valtteri locked in for 2027 alongside Checo and look forward to the next stage of our journey together."

Sports.title: F1 to showcase driver health data in new partnership
Sports.content:
Formula 1 has signed a deal with wearables company WHOOP which will see a number of drivers wear the company's health trackers and showcase their data on the TV broadcasts in 2027.

WHOOP will become an Official Partner of F1 in a deal that will see an increasing number of drivers start wearing tech bracelets provided by the company while inside the car. Per F1's plans, that data such as heart rate, will then be fed to into its storytelling, ranging from graphics on social media to overlays that can be used during the live TV broadcast as early as 2027.

F1 did not disclose how many drivers will use the wearables from next season, as it is understood to be in the process of finalising deals on a case-by-case basis, but at least a handful of drivers have already signed up to the programme.

Earlier this year, WHOOP signed a deal with Ferrari, making the devices available to team members to monitor their wellbeing throughout a demanding season. The wearables are able to chart metrics like heart rate and heart rate variability, sleep quality, and VO2 Max. F1 hopes the deal will better be able to showcase the physical demands of racing.

Its announcement read: "Through this groundbreaking partnership, utilising WHOOP's industry-leading wearable technology and combining it with the sport’s award-winning broadcast, fans will gain a deeper understanding into what the critical moments they witness over a grand prix weekend require both physically and mentally.

"A cornerstone of the partnership will be the development of new broadcast storytelling experiences, featuring select insights delivered in the right way in collaboration with the drivers to provide fans with a real-time window into the physical realities of racing. These innovations will help showcase the human side of the sport in ways never seen before."

Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc are already using WHOOP's wearables. Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

WHOOP CEO Will Ahmed added: "WHOOP is bringing an entirely new dimension to Formula 1 by revealing the human performance behind the wheel.

"For decades, fans have had incredible insight into the cars, but less insight into the impact that races have on the drivers. Now, for the first time, we can show what happens inside a driver's body during the most intense moments of a race. This will change how fans experience Formula 1 and ultimately deepen our understanding of human performance."

F1 CEO and president Stefano Domenicali said: "The opportunity to uncover new insights, tell new stories and showcase the world-class athleticism that goes into making F1 one of the most extreme and exciting sports in the world, is truly groundbreaking.

"I can't wait to see these insights come to life through our broadcasts, giving fans a completely new way to experience Formula 1 while highlighting the incredible strength, resilience, and determination required to compete at the highest level of motorsport."

Sports.title: The five-way fight for second is close – but no one cares about ‘winning’ it | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli may have clinched the world championship with four rounds to spare but there’s a close, five-way fight over second place.

But unlike in the constructors’ championship, which determines how much prize money each team receives, the final ranking in the drivers’ title fight matters little to the competitors. None of the drivers competing for the runner-up spot expressed much interest in taking it.

Outgoing world champion Lando Norris made it clear his priority is getting McLaren back up to third place in the constructors’ championship ahead of Red Bull. His former title rival Max Verstappen is eyeing the same goal and made it clear he doesn’t care if he holds on to second place in the drivers’ standings.

“I only care about staying in [third] with the team,” he said. “That’s the goal of the team and of course that becomes my goal.

“For me I don’t have any satisfaction in being second or third or [fourth] because that’s not what you’re here for. Of course, once you have won championships you probably just don’t really care, right, because it doesn’t get remembered anyway to be in that place. At least not for me.

“But for sure for us in this season, I think we can be very proud of the progression that we made as a team. I think that’s way more important than when we finish in the drivers’ championship, to be honest.”

Verstappen’s fellow multiple world champion Lewis Hamilton said “the constructors’ championship is the main focus” for him and second place in the drivers’ title isn’t a priority.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“It’d be nice to finish it [second], but you want to finish first,” he said. “So the main focus is making sure we solidify second in the constructors for the team, because I think that’s something that everybody, it means a huge amount to everyone at the factory, but especially to me also.

“So that’s what we’re working towards. Then if we’re able to do well and keep in the battle, in the fight, in these last few races, maybe we can climb back up from fourth and hopefully be in the top three.”

Charles Leclerc, whose best championship finish is second place in 2022, gave a similar view.

“I don’t think that it’s something that we are obsessed about, to be honest. I mean, P2 is always better than P3, and I would lie if I say I completely don’t care. But I would also lie to say that it is what I absolutely want.

“My main focus at the moment is to try and win races, and the natural result of winning races will hopefully be the second place in the drivers’ championship. But it’s not something that I’m obsessed about.”

Antonelli has said he’s prepared to help Russell to secure second place in the championship for him. But Russell, whose best championship finish is fourth in 2022 and 2025, is not concerned with his finishing position after missing his chance to win the title this year.

“For me, what’s more important is just to have some strong weekends,” he said. “That doesn’t necessarily just mean the result, it just means from FP1 through the weekend showing good performances.

“This season has been so up-and-down, even during a weekend, even my strong weekends – other than Baku – sometimes it hasn’t been every lap of the weekend so that’s the most important to me. Of course I’d love to finish as high as possible but that’s [what’s] the most important.”

Sports.title: People in the team are asking why my 2027 deal hasn’t been announced – Bearman | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Oliver Bearman is “disappointed” Haas has not yet officially confirmed he will drive for them again in 2027.

Haas announced last month Rafael Camara , who like Bearman is a Ferrari junior driver, will occupy one of their seats next year. However it is yet to name his team mate.

Bearman, who has been a full-time Haas driver since the start of last season, said he has been asked by some team members why no new deal has been announced.

“It’s certainly a bit disappointing when you have people within the team questioning why you haven’t been announced yet and things like that,” he said. “It’s certainly not ideal, not only for them but also for myself.

“From a mental side, I wouldn’t say it’s the best to be standing here at round 20-something without any confirmation. So we’re working on it and all I can say is that I’m a bit disappointed that I’m standing here without anything to tell you because there’s no excuses for that.”

Bearman said it is “not true” to suggest there is a problem with his new deal for next year, “but things have dragged on a lot and I don’t like that.”

Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu made an unexpected change to the team’s line-up when he dropped Bearman’s previous team mate, Esteban Ocon, during the Mexican Grand Prix three weeks ago. That led to Camara joining the team early. Haas has not yet confirmed whether Camara will continue to drive for them in the final two rounds.

Besides Haas, Mercedes and Audi are the only teams yet to officially confirm their drivers for next season, but both are expected to continue with their current line-ups.

Bearman still expects the team will confirm his contract for next season. “It’s just a difficult situation,” he said. “I don’t think there’s any excuse to be standing here at this stage without anything to tell you, and that’s shown by the fact that I’m the only guy who hasn’t been announced for next year.

“Even if I can tell you that – touch wood – I’m going to be driving for Haas next year, the fact it’s not official is just disappointing.”

Sports.title: Sainz won’t tolerate “being a test driver on grand prix weekends” for long | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Carlos Sainz Jnr is experiencing a dissatisfying end to his second season at Williams as the team focuses on testing developments for next season.

Having finished on the podium in two grands prix for the team last season, this year Sainz is languishing in 18th place in the championship. He said the team is focused less on competing in the races and more on solving the problems with its car.

“We’re basically evaluating a lot of our correlation, wind tunnel, CFD to track,” said Sainz. “We’ve had a lot of issues with this year’s car, not so much in terms of actual correlation, but just bringing performance to the track hasn’t been easy for us.

“We are just not quick enough. We’re slow, I think, as a team in general. We’ve struggled to understand these new regs and we’re doing everything possible to change the set-up, challenge a few things that come to the track, make sure we can give the factory the best possible feedback to know how to develop next year’s car.”

The team has only scored one point in the last 13 rounds. Sainz admitted they have little chance to add to their haul of 12 points over the final races.

“Right now, we are one second off [Racing Bulls], who are finishing P9 and P10 when the top four are not having any issues. They are taking the P9 and P10, which is two and one points on the board, and that’s one second off for us. So the chances of points really are very, very small.

“This track maybe offers a little bit more hope, but the reality is that we’d rather invest that time in becoming a test driver and testing for the team than actually doing anything else.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

However he admitted he doesn’t find it enjoyable arriving at races knowing he won’t be racing properly. “I don’t like being a test driver on race weekends,” said Sainz.

“I honestly enjoy going testing. Probably not many drivers enjoy testing, but I actually enjoy testing. I enjoy trying different set-ups, trying different things in the simulator. It is true that I like investing my time on that, and I always feel like I learn a lot from it, and I enjoy that side of Formula 1 and racing.

“But it is true that when it comes to going to a race weekend, I don’t look forward to testing. I look forward to winning and fighting for good results and this year there’s been none of that.”

Sainz extended his contract to drive for Williams earlier this year. However he made it clear he expects the team to be more competitive in the future.

“[For] one year I can take it in the chin. I think it’s been an extremely tough year, but I feel like I’ve dealt with it with patience and with good spirit. I’ve driven well this year, which probably has helped that and my motivation quite a bit.

“But it is true that I don’t foresee many more years like this, because going into race weekends without even having a chance to score a point is extremely frustrating.

“I’ve been very lucky in my career that in these 11 years I’ve always had a car to score points. Even my three years in Toro Rosso, I had a car that could get into a top 10. My years in Renault, years in McLaren, midfield cars were always on that level where Liam [Lawson] and [Racing Bulls] are, always top of the midfield, which, for the battles that you fight, actually there is satisfaction from scoring those points.

“But then it has been my first-ever season where not even with a perfect race, perfect execution, you get to score a point, and that is extremely frustrating. But we’re doing the best we can to get out of that situation for next year.”
