Sports.title: Russell explains why he chose not to use Mercedes’ turbo upgrade in Las Vegas | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell said he was involved in the decision not to use the power unit upgrade his team mate will have this weekend.

Mercedes is introducing a revision to its power unit made under the FIA’s Additional Development Upgrade Opportunity regulations. It allows them to bring a performance upgrade to reduce their deficit to leading design, which the FIA determined is Red Bull-Ford’s.

But while Andrea Kimi Antonelli will use the new turbo design this weekend, Russell will not. He has already used five turbos this year, exceeding his maximum allocation for the season, while Antonelli has used three, one less than the maximum.

Russell said the team gave him the chance to influence the decision and he felt avoiding a penalty was more beneficial than gaining the performance benefit from the new part. “The performance benefit it brings is not huge, it is just a step in the direction as a team we want to take,” he said.

“We’re obviously lucky with Mercedes that there’s eight drivers running the power unit. I think five or six of them are taking the turbo. The two or three who aren’t, including myself, it’s just because it would mean a back-of-grid penalty.

“Vegas is a track I’ve gone well at in the past, I enjoy it here and I was very much involved in the decision. They said ‘if you want to take it, you can take it, if you don’t, you don’t’.

“I was happy not to because I want to fight for the victory and I think we can do it with or without it.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Antonelli, who will take the new turbo, said the team “don’t expect any major performance gain” from the new turbo. “It will just improve some of the features that we’ve been struggling with.”

“It’s mostly to improve the feeling whilst driving. There will be a slight performance gain but we’re talking less than a tenth [of a second]. It’s mostly to improve the feeling with the driving because obviously the power unit has been very different this season compared to previous seasons.

“Drive-ability hasn’t been the best at times. So this turbo should improve that and hopefully it will make just the feeling of driving even better.”

Sports.title: Beating Red Bull to third place matters, says Norris: “It’s a hell of a lot of money” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lando Norris says claiming third place in the constructors’ championship matters “a huge amount” to McLaren because of the extra prize money it begins.

McLaren won the constructors’ championship in the last two seasons but lost the crown to Mercedes this year. They dropped to fourth place behind Red Bull two rounds ago and lie 17 points behind them with three rounds remaining.

Norris said the extra money the team would earn for finishing third makes this the goal for him and team mate Oscar Piastri in the remaining rounds.

“It’s a lot of money for the whole team, for every individual in the team,” he said. “So, as always, there’s a lot of natural pressure on me and Oscar to go out and perform well, to bring points back to the team and have two cars up there.”

Some of the extra money for finishing higher in the championship will go to McLaren’s staff as bonuses, said Norris.

“You always talk about points and constructor points and all of these things, and it’s very important, but I think you often do forget the extras, the bonuses that come with it,” he said. “Not for me, but for all the members of the team.

“It’s a hell of a lot of money from P4 to P3. All the team members that work every day also get their bonuses at the end of the year, so they want it just as much as anyone.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Obviously, then it is me going out and driving, and they rely upon me and Oscar to go out and do a good job so, I don’t know, simple things they can buy their kids cooler presents or presents or whatever it might be, and move into the new house or whatever it is. So it obviously means a lot.”

McLaren face an added complication this weekend as Piastri will take a grid penalty for a power unit parts change.

“Oscar’s taking a nice penalty this weekend, so he’s coming from the back of the grid – hopefully not even at the back, the middle of the pack,” said Norris. “But we just need consistent results.

“We need to make sure we’re there. Plenty of things can still be happening and have been happening through the races, so we need two cars up there fighting for points.”

Norris won the last race in Brazil but McLaren gained no ground on Red Bull as Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar finished on the podium while Piastri was sixth.

“Max is doing a good job and Red Bull are doing a good job,” said Norris. “Isack did a good job last weekend, so we’ve got a tough fight, but we’re up for it.”

Sports.title: Mercedes’ technical director explains how Antonelli leapt ahead of Russell in 2026 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli scored less than half as many points as his team mate in his first season of Formula 1 last year.

But he turned that around in his second season which put him in position to clinch the world championship as Mercedes produced the car to beat.

James Allison, Mercedes’ technical director who led development of their first world championship-winning car for five years, believes a shift in the handling balance arising from this year’s new technical regulations explains why George Russell lost the edge he had over his team mate.

“I would say that George – I’m more or less quoting George here – when he has been prospering, it is at a track where you can make a lot of difference from the apex and out of the corner,” he explained in a video released by the team.

“George is good at getting on the power and getting a strong exit from a corner. That certainly was true of last year’s cars and George was very strong relative to Kimi in last year’s car.

“I think this car is a little bit more conventional as a car, where a lot of the lap time is in trusting the car and the combined brake and steer on the way in: So, delivering the car to the apex, leaning on the front, trusting that the rear is not going to punish you and then arriving at the apex just that little bit quicker so you don’t have to be so aggressive on the exit.”

Antonelli’s stronger performance on the way into corners gives him an advantage when looking after his tyres, says Allison.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“That, in the race, tells because you are using less of the rear tyre. You get less tyre degradation and that – if you want to see the standout performances of Kimi this year, it’s 20 laps in when everyone else has peeled into the pits and his lap times just go level.”

Lewis Hamilton, whom Antonelli replaced at the team in 2025, has also benefited from the same change, Allison believes.

“I think that’s one of the reasons why Lewis is having something of a sort of Indian summer in his career, because that was always Lewis’s great strength is hurling the car to the apex, trusting that he’s going to manage the thing as it gets to the apex.”

Allison said he is impressed by Russell’s focus on addressing where he has fallen short compared to Antonelli this year.

“He does not hide from his own deficiencies,” said Allison. “He’s one of the most honest drivers I’ve ever had the good fortune to work with.

“He can see the areas where Kimi has been quicker than him this year and he knows that those are things that he needs to bring to the table to compete on equal or better terms with this precocious young talent. I do very much admire the fact that he looked straight down the barrel of that and I’m pretty sure that we will see, we have seen in the last couple of races some very, very strong performances from him.

“I’m pretty sure in the last three we’re going to see him, without all the burden of these championships still on any of our shoulders, looking to build the platform that is going to let him have a run at it next year, alongside an amazingly talented team mate.”

Sports.title: Matchroom Weighs Quick Teremoana Return After Ahio Fight
Sports.content:
Matchroom is considering a quick return for Teremoana Teremoana after his second-round stoppage of Hemi Ahio. Promoter Frank Smith said the team would decide within 24 to 48 hours whether to get him out again soon. Petar Milas looks like a sensible next opponent if Matchroom wants to move Teremoana up a level and give him a chance to get some rounds in.

Teremoana called for a shot at Australian heavyweight champion Ivan Ivić, saying he’d heard he was the mandatory challenger. Smith said Matchroom had already made Ivić several offers for what he called “really good money,” and the champion hadn’t taken the fight. With several Matchroom cards coming up, there’s little reason to build the next date around an opponent Smith says has already passed.

“If he wanted to get out quickly again, that’s something we are looking at right now,” said Smith after the Ahio fight. He said he wanted to give Teremoana time to rest after the fight and the training camp before making a decision.

Milas is ranked one place above Teremoana on the IBF list discussed here. That’s the kind of incremental move that makes sense on a short turnaround. Guido Vianello would be a tougher option, while Efe Ajagba or Justis Huni would represent a bigger jump. Milas is a matchmaking option, and Smith gave no indication that Matchroom had approached him.

Teremoana said he’d leave the opponent to his team. He also said he wanted Ahio to get up after the second knockdown because he wanted more ring time. That gives Matchroom a clear brief if it brings him back quickly. Find someone who can extend him past the early rounds and make him work for a win.

The bigger question is whether Teremoana’s team is trying to manufacture an artificial fighter designed to make a big killing without ever facing anyone dangerous. If this is all just artifice to build a hype job and create a pseudo star, we won’t see a true step up in opposition for his next fight.

Some fans believe Matchroom ran that exact same play with Anthony Joshua, who was matched carefully through much of his career and made massive money without beating high-level opposition. Once Joshua finally stepped in against the real thing, he lost to Oleksandr Usyk and Daniel Dubois.

If that is the blueprint for Teremoana, it could be a long time before he faces a genuinely good opponent, and by the time it happens, there will likely be huge money on the line.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster May Have to Earn Shakur at 140
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster is still pushing for a fight with Shakur Stevenson, but his path to getting it likely runs through a credible light welterweight contender first. Shakur is focused on lucrative matchups, and Foster brings a sharp counterpunching style capable of spoiling his night on the scorecards without generating the ticket sales or viewership to make the gamble worthwhile.

Foster revived the callout after Stevenson reached out to congratulate him. While Foster acknowledged the gesture and praised Stevenson as a great fighter, he made it clear that their fractured relationship keeps the matchup personal for him.

“We had a good relationship back then, but it’s where it’s at now,” Foster told Fight Hub TV. “So, you know, we still need to make that happen across the ring from each other.”

According to Foster, “stuff was said” and “the lines was crossed.” Still, the push for the bout has come almost entirely from his side. Stevenson’s message gave Foster an opening to put his name back in the mix, while Shakur has shown minimal public interest in taking the bait.

If Shakur ever warms up to the idea, he will almost certainly demand the fight at 140. That puts the pressure on Foster to move up from 130 and handle the extra weight. Foster has the patience to make Stevenson lead and work harder than he wants to, though proving he can hold his ground and make his counters hurt against natural junior welterweights remains an unanswered question.

Stepping up to 140 will make the fight against Shakur possible, and beating an established name in the division would give Foster real leverage at the negotiating table. The catch is that he would be taking on a dangerous opponent with no promise that Stevenson waits on the other side. Foster has the personal motivation to take that chance, yet Stevenson still requires a payday large enough to justify risking an upset.

Sports.title: No Handouts: Crawford Demands Canelo Shot for Lester Martínez After His Own Shortcut
Sports.content:
Terence Crawford wants to know why Lester Martínez is still waiting for a shot at Canelo Álvarez, though he is overlooking the business and boxing realities that put Christian Mbilli in line first.

Mbilli held the full WBC super middleweight title, which Canelo won from him by decision on October 31. Martínez holds only the interim belt and does not bring the leverage, name value, or resume needed to force his way into a massive payday.

Crawford and Martínez trained together under Brian “BoMac” McIntyre, who still coaches Martínez and prepared Crawford for his 2025 victory over Canelo. Loyalty to a former gymmate clearly played a role when Crawford focused on WBC president Mauricio Sulaimán on X, pointing out that Mbilli and Martínez fought to a draw:

“I don’t get it. It’s crazy how the @wbcmoro say Lester not good enough to fight @Canelo but Mbilli was. This the type of stuff I don’t like with these sanction bodies, they pick and choose. How being the interim champion not good enough for a chance at the championship.”

What Crawford leaves out is how Canelo’s career actually operates at this stage. Canelo is being paid enormous money by Turki Alalshikh, and Turki is focused on global spectacles, not charity mandatories for fighters the casual public has never heard of. Outside of hardcore boxing circles, Martínez is virtually unknown, and complaining on social media will not talk him into a fight he has not earned.

There is also a glaring double standard in Crawford’s complaint. Crawford himself received a massive shortcut in 2025 when he was allowed to skip the entire 160-pound division and jump straight to the front of the line to challenge Canelo for the undisputed 168-pound championship without facing a number one contender or grinding through the mandatory path. Nothing about that was fair.

Crawford got the fight because Turki liked him, and he was lucky to even arrive there undefeated after struggling badly in his previous bout against Israil Madrimov. Many fans felt Crawford lost that fight, yet he escaped with the decision, bypassed the sharks at middleweight and super middleweight, and walked straight into a title shot he had not earned in the division.

Even after winning the belts, Crawford did not rush to defend them against dangerous, low-reward fighters like Martínez or IBF champion Osleys Iglesias before stepping away.

Now Crawford is upset that his former gymmate is not receiving the same special treatment. Martínez has none of Crawford’s star power or backing, and his thin resume does not justify a handout. He did not look impressive in his interim title bouts against Immanuwel Aleem in March or Luka Plantić over the summer, and he was fortunate to escape the Mbilli fight with a draw after leaning heavily on excessive shoving while the referee let it slide.

If Crawford wants his former gymmate to land a fight with Canelo, the answer is simple: tell him to go earn it in the ring. Martínez needs real wins over legitimate opposition like IBF champion Osleys Iglesias, Darius Fulghum, Bektemir Melikuziev, or top middleweights moving up like Janibek Alimkhanuly and Carlos Adames. Until he beats serious threats and builds a case the public cares about, Canelo has no reason to give him the time of day.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Says Shakur Stevenson Fight “Has to Happen”
Sports.content:
Devin Haney is already talking about a fight with Shakur Stevenson like it’s a sure thing, claiming it “has to happen.” Looking at the rest of the welterweight division, you can’t blame him for eyeing that payday.

Outside of a Ryan Garcia rematch, nobody else brings the kind of money and spotlight that Stevenson does. The problem is that Haney is looking way too far ahead. He still has to survive Liam Paro first, and Garcia is lurking right behind him.

“I think that it has to happen. I think it’s just a big fight,” Haney said during an appearance on Shannon Sharpe’s Club Shay Shay. “I think that he’s going to keep winning. I’m going to keep winning, and eventually we’re going to have to meet.”

Realistically, Teofimo Lopez is one of the only other fighters who can help Haney sell a massive event. Conor Benn might get there if he keeps stacking wins, and Keyshawn Davis is still building up to that level of star power.

Guys like Richardson Hitchins, Rolly Romero, and Brian Norman Jr. would all make for solid matchups, yet none of them spark the kind of heated debate that Haney versus Stevenson does. Fans have argued for years over who has the sharper skills, and they will gladly open their wallets to settle it.

The problem Haney has is that there’s no way of knowing whether Shakur’s career will go downhill. He’s already lost almost an entire year on his extended victory lap after beating Teofimo last January. What we’re seeing here from Shakur is his chase of exclusively big paydays sidelining him, causing him to lose out on that great gig he had with Zuffa.

Haney needs to focus on putting the fight together with Shakur as soon as possible while he’s still in demand. The way his career looks now, it’s following in the same direction as the Charlo brothers. Jermell and Jermall went from headlining major events to sitting on the shelf for roughly three years, and by the time they finally resurfaced, the sport had moved right past them. Now they are stuck fighting on undercards for a fraction of what they used to make.

If Stevenson walks away from the Raymond Muratalla purse bid over low money, he is heading straight down that exact same path. That puts the pressure squarely on Haney to push for this fight immediately before Stevenson tanks his own value.

Sports.title: Chisora Claims Sparring Beating Drove Opetaia Out of Wilder Fight
Sports.content:
Derek Chisora is disputing the reason Jai Opetaia pulled out of his December 11 bout against Deontay Wilder, claiming a rough sparring session forced the Australian out of the fight while offering to step in as a replacement.

“Opetaia is not injured. He had a bad experience,” said Chisora, according to Desai. Chisora claimed the heavyweight got the better of Opetaia so badly that he left the gym and never returned. He went further, saying Opetaia couldn’t step up to heavyweight.

The massive purse for his previous fight against ‘The Bronze Bomber’ Wilder completely wrecks any realistic chance of Chisora getting the call. If $4 million to $6 million is his baseline asking price, the math simply does not work for an undercard slot as the replacement.

Fury vs. Joshua is already going to eat up the vast majority of the budget for that December 11 stadium show in Cardiff. Organizers are not going to blow another $5 million on a co-feature rematch that Wilder already won cleanly over 12 rounds back in April, especially when Chisora is demanding an eight-round cap.

From a business standpoint, paying A-side money for an aging veteran who does not move the needle on PPV buys or ticket sales makes zero sense. They can find a younger, hungrier heavyweight willing to fight 12 full rounds for a fraction of that purse. Chisora can keep floating sparring rumors all he wants, but he is pricing himself right out of the conversation.

If Chisora actually wanted the fight instead of just a headline, he would be publicly undercutting the market instead of telling gym stories.

Floating a discounted substitute rate of a few hundred thousand dollars would immediately get the organizers’ attention. On a massive stadium show where Fury and Joshua are soaking up almost the entire purse budget, promoters are looking for cheap, recognizable names to fill out the undercard without blowing up their overhead.

By demanding “the right money” while simultaneously asking for an eight-round cap, Chisora is playing his hand completely backward. He has zero leverage here. He is coming off a clear 12-round loss to Wilder in April, and nobody is clamoring to see a rematch.

If he came out and said he would take $300,000 to save the December 11 co-feature, his phone would actually be ringing. Instead, talking trash about Opetaia while pricing himself at millions just ensures the organizers move right down the list to someone hungry enough to take the smaller check.

Sports.title: Teremoana Teremoana Stops Hemi Ahio in Two
Sports.content:
Teremoana Teremoana dropped Hemi “The Heat” Ahio twice and stopped him at 1:36 of the second round to win the vacant IBF Inter-Continental heavyweight title on Wednesday at Pullman Melbourne Albert Park. The scheduled 10-round main event aired on DAZN, with Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom Boxing and Peter Maniatis’ PM Events promoting the card.

The much taller Teremoana (13-0, 13 KOs), of Brisbane, caught Ahio (25-2, 19 KOs), of Auckland, with a left to the chin midway through the first round. Ahio got up and took an eight-count from referee Ignatius Missaidis. Teremoana dropped him again with a right to the chin in the second. Ahio beat the count, but Missaidis waved off the fight.

Joel “Came KO” Camilleri (39-1, 15 KOs), of Melbourne, won the vacant IBF Australasian middleweight title with a unanimous decision over fellow Melbourne fighter Mitchell Leek (14-1, 8 KOs). The judges scored it 96-93, 96-93 and 95-94 for Camilleri.

Camilleri had a strong second round, but Leek dropped him in the third for an eight-count from referee Brett Manton. Leek also suffered a cut over his right eyebrow in the third. Camilleri appeared to be ahead after seven rounds. Leek pressed for a stoppage in the tenth and won the round on this writer’s card, but Camilleri made it to the final bell.

Ky “Hit Man” Hodgson (8-1, 6 KOs), of Melbourne, stopped Victor “The Tank” Adis-losifidis (3-1, 1 KO), of Victoria, at 2:30 of the third round to win the vacant Australasian super welterweight title. The taller Hodgson outlanded Adis-losifidis in the first. Adis-losifidis had more success in the second, though his right eye began to swell. Hodgson landed six unanswered punches in the third, prompting Manton to stop the scheduled 10-round bout.

Omar El-Abdallah (7-0, 6 KOs), of Melbourne, knocked out late replacement Nick “The Brick” Benn (5-3, 5 KOs), of Tauranga, New Zealand, at 0:37 of the seventh round of a scheduled eight-round bout. El-Abdallah outlanded Benn through the first four rounds and dropped him with a lead right to the chin in the seventh. Missaidis waved it off without a count.

Melbourne’s James Noonan (1-1-1) and Victoria’s Matt Faron (2-0-1) fought to a four-round draw in a middleweight bout. All three judges scored it 38-38. Both southpaws switched to orthodox and back in the opening round, which Faron appeared to edge. Noonan had the better of the second, and Manton warned Faron for holding in the third. Noonan appeared to take the fourth by outworking Faron.

Sports.title: Derek Chisora Still Waiting for the Right Wilder Money
Sports.content:
Derek Chisora says he still hasn’t been offered enough to fight Deontay Wilder again on the December 11 Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua undercard in Cardiff. He’s willing to step in for Jai Opetaia, but says he’ll stay home if the offer falls short. Asked how much it would take, Chisora kept the figure to himself.

“They already asked me, and I already told them, ‘Yes, give me the right money.’ So now we’re just talking about money,” said Chisora on talkSPORT. Pressed for a figure, he said, “A good number. A very good number.”

Given that Chisora reportedly earned between $4 million and $6 million for his first bout with Wilder, it is hard to see how he commands even a tiny fraction of that amount today. At 42 years old with 14 losses on his record, Chisora no longer has the O2 Arena farewell narrative he used to sell out London back in April.

If Dana White were running these negotiations, he wouldn’t just balk at a steep asking price; he would laugh Chisora right out of the room and refuse to even entertain the idea of using him.

If Chisora’s price stays inflated, the promoters have every reason to walk away and look at a younger heavyweight instead. Bringing in someone like Bakhodir Jalolov would give viewers a fresh matchup and let fans see how Wilder handles a younger southpaw with deep amateur credentials at a fraction of the cost.

Putting Chisora in the co-main slot drags down the broadcast quality rather than adding value.

To younger American fans, Chisora is basically invisible. He hasn’t been a relevant force on U.S. television in years, and casual viewers tuning in for Fury and Joshua aren’t going to care about an aging British domestic attraction who already lost to Wilder seven months ago.

Hardcore boxing fans aren’t clamoring for it either, because everyone already knows exactly what Chisora brings to the table at this point in his career.

The bigger problem is how weak it makes the top of the card look. When you pair a faded Chisora with a 41-year-old Wilder who has lost four of his last six fights, you end up with a co-main event featuring zero top-five contenders. Following that up with Fury and Joshua means the final two bouts of the night are built entirely on nostalgia rather than elite, current division talent.

If the promoters want the card to have actual credibility with hardcore fans and younger American viewers, they need a legitimate threat or a rising contender across from Wilder, not a recycled eight-round exhibition.

Jim White wrapped up the radio segment by noting that Chisora is holding out for his magic number, prompting Simon Jordan to joke about the veteran being a “greedy little swine.”

Sports.title: Teremoana Teremoana Calls For World Title Shot After Stopping Ahio
Sports.content:
Teremoana Teremoana dropped Hemi Ahio with right hands in both rounds and stopped him at 1:36 of the second to win the vacant IBF Inter-Continental heavyweight title on Wednesday, November 18, at Pullman Melbourne Albert Park in Melbourne, Australia.

Teremoana (13-0, 13 KOs) kept his perfect knockout record intact against the most experienced opponent of his professional career. Ahio (25-2, 19 KOs) got up from both knockdowns, but referee Ignatius Missailidis checked him in the corner after the second and waved off the scheduled 10-round fight.

After the fight, Teremoana said he would take a shot at a world heavyweight title in his next bout if the opportunity came up. His goal is to fight for one within the next 12 months.

Teremoana Drops Ahio in Both Rounds

Ahio came forward from the opening bell, looking to get inside Teremoana’s jab and trade at close range. Teremoana made him pay for the approach within the first minute, catching the New Zealander with a hard right hand as he tried to close the distance. Ahio got to his feet and took more punches in combination before making it out of the first round.

The second opened at a slower pace, with some clinching and work to the body. Teremoana found room for his right hand again and hurt Ahio before putting him down with another right. Ahio beat the count, but Missailidis ended the fight after looking him over in the corner.

“I knew if I stayed close, he’d try and hit me; that’s why I stayed long. I think I handled myself well,” said Teremoana after the fight.

At 6’6″ and about 269 pounds, Teremoana had six inches in height and roughly 37 pounds on Ahio at the weigh-in. His jab made the shorter man start his attacks from farther out, and the right hand caught Ahio on the way in. Ahio kept pressing after the first knockdown, but he never found a way to get inside consistently enough to keep Teremoana from throwing at full extension.

The 28-year-old Brisbane heavyweight represented Australia at the 2024 Paris Olympics, where he lost to eventual gold medalist Bakhodir Jalolov in the super heavyweight quarterfinals. He had stopped his first 12 professional opponents inside two rounds. Ahio, 36, came in with 26 professional bouts and 19 knockouts of his own. Even with that experience, he became the 13th opponent to fall before the third round.

Matchroom Boxing CEO Frank Smith praised Teremoana for dealing with an opponent who kept coming forward. Teremoana mentioned the Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury undercard as a possible place for his next fight and said he would leave the decision to his team.

In the co-feature, Joel Camilleri dropped previously unbeaten Mitchell Leek in the opening round and won a unanimous decision to claim the vacant IBF Australasian middleweight title. The judges scored it 96-93, 95-94 and 96-93.

Omar El-Abdallah knocked out Nicholas Benn in the seventh round, and Ky Hodgson won the vacant Australian super welterweight title with a third-round TKO of Victor Adis-Iosifidis. James Noonan and Matt Faron fought to a unanimous draw, with all three judges scoring it 38-38.

Ghana News.title: GMet forecasts sunny weather with isolated thunderstorms across parts of Ghana
Ghana News.content:
Ghana is set for a largely sunny day on Thursday, November 19, but residents in the coastal and middle sectors should keep umbrellas handy, as isolated thunderstorms are expected later.

According to the Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet), partly cloudy conditions will prevail across the country this morning, with mist or fog likely over some forested, coastal, and mountainous areas. The agency's 18-hour impact-based forecast indicates that as the day progresses, sunny conditions will dominate most parts of the country.

However, afternoon tranquillity will be interrupted in some regions. GMet warns that isolated thunderstorms or rain may occur over a few locations within the coastal and middle sectors from late afternoon into the evening.

Meanwhile, the northern sector will remain relatively dry, with slight haze expected over the upper parts throughout the forecast period.

Temperatures will vary significantly across the country. The coastal sector is expected to record minimum temperatures of 24 degrees Celsius and maximums of 33 degrees Celsius. The forest and transition sectors will see temperatures ranging between 22 and 35 degrees Celsius, while the north will experience the highest temperatures, ranging from 20 to a scorching 38 degrees Celsius.

The agency has also issued a warning for those travelling along the coast, noting that the state of the sea is expected to be rough.

Cities such as Accra, Takoradi, and Cape Coast are forecast to experience mist in the morning before transitioning to sunny periods with localised thunderstorms.

Inland cities like Kumasi and Techiman will also see misty mornings giving way to sunny conditions. The northern hubs of Tamale and Bolgatanga will remain dry and hazy throughout the day.

Ghana News.title: Government’s revenue target is ambitious; current primary surplus can lead to cash problem – PwC
Ghana News.content:
Professional services firm PwC has described the government’s 2027 revenue target as rather ambitious. According to the firm, since revenue is planned to rise about 18%, collection must genuinely improve and not just keep pace.

Therefore, it said the government must show how much cash each new measure brings in, counting money actually collected after appeals and refunds rather than bills issued.

“Revenue success is so important for government’s fiscal credibility, which by itself, is an anchor for the success of the 2027 budgetary goals. The economy is expected to grow about 13% in money terms, but revenue is planned to rise about 18%; so, collection must genuinely improve, not just keep pace. Government should show how much cash each new measure brings in, counting money actually collected after appeals and refunds rather than bills issued".

The government is seeking to raise GH¢323.4 billion in total revenue and grants for the 2027 fiscal year.

For 2027, the primary surplus target eases from 1.5% of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to 0.5%. This, the auditing firm said, matches the IMF’s Policy Coordination Programme path.

Again, the Finance Minister noted the government’s intention to seek an amendment to the Public Financial Management (Amendment) Act, 2025 (Act 1136) for this purpose.

“With the controlling majority that the National Democratic Congress (NDC) has in Parliament, we do not anticipate that this move to amend the law would face a challenge. However, achieving the target also depends on the quality of government’s revenue mobilisation and administration, investment management, and oversight of State-Owned Entities (SOEs)”, it stressed.

Surplus on Paper Can Still Leave Cash Problem

PwC said a surplus on paper can still leave a cash problem.

“After GH₵13.9bn of arrears payments, the Budget shows a GH₵4.8bn cash deficit before interest, and an overall cash deficit of GH₵65.8bn. Net domestic borrowing reaches GH₵85bn, before refinancing debt that falls due. The Minister reports GH₵29bn in the cedi sinking fund and offers to repay some of the February 2027 debt early, which would ease a pressure point if completed. But a balance in an account is not proof that every payment is covered, including February 2027’s GH₵11.1bn interest bill, August’s GH₵12.5bn and the Eurobond payments in January and July 2027”.

“And we know that fiscal credibility would begin to fray if repayment deadlines are missed”, it added.

Debt is in Better Shape but Fragile

On debt, it said it is in better shape but still fragile.

Debt rose from 44.7% of GDP at the end of 2025 to a provisional 47.5% in October 2026 (GH₵759.3 billion).

Further, any future rebasing of GDP could lower the debt-to-GDP ratio without producing a pesewa of repayment cash.

However, PwC said the joint IMF–World Bank Debt Sustainability Analysis (DSA) rates the country debt risk as moderate, with little room for shocks.

Ghana News.title: Guinness Ghana DJ Awards 2026: Full list of nominees unveiled
Ghana News.content:
The nominees for the 2026 Guinness Ghana DJ Awards have been announced, with some of the country's leading disc jockeys competing for honours across several categories.

DJ Millzy, DJ Lord OTB, DJ Sonatty, TMSK DJ, DJ Vyrusky, DJ Sly King and DJ Loft have been shortlisted for the coveted DJ of the Year award.

The nominations recognise DJs working across radio, clubs, pubs, digital platforms and regional entertainment scenes, as well as emerging talents making an impact in the industry.

DJ Sonatty's nomination for DJ of the Year marks a historic milestone, as he becomes the first DJ from the Central Region to earn a place in the seven-member category. He has also been nominated for Digital DJ of the Year.

The 2026 list features several competitive categories, including Best Young DJ, Scratch DJ of the Year, International DJ of the Year, Mobile DJ of the Year, Female DJ of the Year, Gospel DJ of the Year and Artiste DJ of the Year.

The regional categories also recognise DJs from all 16 regions, providing a platform for talents outside the major entertainment centres to gain national recognition.

Other categories include Artiste Collaboration of the Year, DJ's Song of the Year, Mixtape of the Year, Discovery of the Year, Record Promoter of the Year and MC/Hypeman of the Year.

The Digital DJ of the Year category, introduced for the 2026 edition, recognises the growing influence of online mixes, livestreams, digital content and audience engagement in the DJ profession.

The awards season is being held under the theme “All Out” and is powered by Smirnoff. Produced by Merqury Republic, the scheme also features activities such as Pub Fest, the Ghana DJ Clinic and nationwide engagements ahead of the main ceremony.

The 2026 awards ceremony is scheduled for December 4 at the Palms Convention Centre in Accra.

Ghana News.title: AG’s directive on suspects’ rights part of broader criminal justice reforms – Press Secretary
Ghana News.content:
Attorney General and Minister for Justice Dominic Ayine

The Attorney-General’s directive requiring investigative agencies to respect the rights of suspects forms part of broader criminal justice reforms being pursued by the government, the Press Secretary to the Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Benjamin Alpha Aidoo, has said.

He said the directive, issued by Dr Dominic Ayine, was intended to address recurring practices in criminal investigations that fall short of constitutional and legal standards.

Speaking in an interview on Joy FM’s Middaynews on Thursday, November 19, Mr Aidoo said violations during investigations could undermine the quality of cases prepared for prosecution.

"The most important thing is that there seems to be a practice where certain suspect investigations are carried out, sometimes outside the remit of the law, and that actually has consequences for the quality of cases that are built for prosecution. And so the Attorney General deems it fit that we must take steps to rein in errant officers and to ensure that we reform our criminal justice system. And so this directive forms part of broader criminal justice reforms being pursued by the government through the Attorney General," he said.

The directive requires investigative agencies to comply with legal requirements governing arrests, detention, interrogations and bail, including the constitutional requirement to bring arrested persons before a court within 48 hours.

It also prohibits torture, coerced confessions, unlawful searches and the use of investigative powers to recover civil debts.

Mr Aidoo explained that although the protections were already enshrined in the 1992 Constitution and other relevant legislation, the Attorney-General considered it necessary to reinforce compliance among investigative agencies.

"The AG, as the one who wields prosecutorial authority of the state, deems it important to issue this directive in order to stem the recurring practice where the handling of criminal investigations and of suspects fall short of constitutional and legal standards," he said.

He noted that the directive restated existing legal protections under Articles 14, 15 and 19 of the Constitution, as well as the Criminal Offences Act and the Criminal and Other Offences (Procedure) Act.

Ghana News.title: AG directs investigative agencies to respect suspects’ rights or face sanctions
Ghana News.content:
Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Dr Dominic Ayine, has directed investigative agencies to strictly comply with constitutional and legal requirements governing arrests, detention, interrogations and bail, warning that officers who violate the rules could face disciplinary and criminal sanctions.

The directive establishes minimum operational standards for criminal investigations and seeks to strengthen accountability for officers who breach the rights of suspects.

It is addressed to the Inspector-General of Police, the Director-General of the Criminal Investigations Department, the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO), the National Investigations Bureau (NIB), the Narcotics Control Commission and other public institutions with investigative powers.

Under the new requirements, officers must have lawful grounds to arrest a person and immediately explain the reasons for the arrest in a language the suspect understands.

They must also inform arrested persons of their right to legal representation and, where they cannot afford a lawyer, make them aware of the services of the Legal Aid Commission.

The directive requires that anyone arrested and not released be brought before a court within 48 hours.

It clarifies that the period must be calculated from the moment the person's liberty is first restrained, rather than when the arrest is formally recorded.

Weekends, public holidays, transfers between police stations and incomplete investigations cannot be used to justify detention beyond the stipulated period without a court order.

Investigating officers are also required to release suspects, with or without enquiry bail, where investigations can continue without keeping them in custody.

The directive prohibits excessive or unattainable sureties, cash deposits not authorised by law and the retention of title documents as conditions for granting bail.

It further emphasises that enquiry bail must be free, warning officers against demanding or accepting money, gifts or favours in exchange for releasing suspects.

Where officers apply for a remand order, they must identify the specific investigative steps outstanding and explain why the suspect cannot be released on bail. Repeated remand applications without demonstrable progress in investigations are also prohibited.

Dr Ayine said the measures were intended to address recurring practices identified by the Office of the Attorney-General, including detention beyond 48 hours without court appearance, arrests to recover civil debts, coerced statements, unlawful searches and the maltreatment of suspects.

The directive prohibits investigative powers from being used to enforce contracts, recover debts or settle land and family disputes where no criminal offence has been disclosed.

It also bars the use of investigative powers for partisan political purposes.

On interrogations, suspects must be informed that they are not obliged to make statements. Those who request lawyers must be given a reasonable opportunity to consult them before and during questioning, subject to narrowly defined exceptions.

Officers are also prohibited from altering or replacing statements after they have been signed.

The directive expressly bans torture, beatings, threats, deprivation of food or sleep, stripping and other forms of degrading treatment to obtain confessions or information.

It also places restrictions on searches of digital devices, requiring officers to remain within the scope of the relevant warrant or lawful authorisation.

Threats or force must not be used to obtain passwords, while a court order or express statutory authority is required to compel disclosure.

The directive outlines legal and administrative consequences for investigative agencies and individual officers who fail to comply.

It states that evidence obtained in breach of the Constitution or other applicable laws may be excluded at trial, potentially undermining prosecutions.

The Attorney-General's Office will also not lend its authority to prosecutions based on evidence obtained through torture or coercion. It may decline to prosecute or discontinue cases where serious violations have tainted the evidence.

Persons who are unlawfully arrested, restricted or detained may seek compensation under Article 14(5) of the 1992 Constitution. Those whose fundamental rights have been violated may also apply to the High Court for redress under Article 33.

The directive warns that unlawful detention, torture and other rights violations could expose the Republic and individual officers to civil liability. Officers may also face criminal liability under the Criminal Offences Act, 1960 (Act 29).

Heads of investigative agencies are required to take disciplinary action against officers found to have breached the directive, in accordance with their respective laws and regulations, and report the action taken to the Attorney-General.

Where a breach also constitutes a criminal offence, the matter must be referred for independent investigation and, where the evidence warrants, prosecution.

The directive establishes specific protections for children, victims and witnesses.

Children must not be questioned without an appropriate adult present. Their detention must be treated as a last resort, and they must be kept separate from adult detainees.

Their identities must also be protected.

Victims must receive complaint reference numbers and updates on their cases. Officers are prohibited from discouraging people from making criminal complaints or detaining witnesses to secure their testimony.

To monitor compliance, station and unit commanders must inspect relevant registers at least once every week.

Heads of law enforcement agencies are also required to submit quarterly reports covering arrests, bail, detention beyond 48 hours and allegations of mistreatment, unlawful searches or coerced statements.

The agencies have 90 days from the directive's effective date to incorporate its requirements into their standing orders and training programmes.

Heads of the affected institutions have also been given 14 days from receipt of the directive to bring its provisions to the attention of all investigating officers under their command.

The directive requires established breaches to attract disciplinary action, while suspected criminal offences must be referred for independent investigation and possible prosecution.

Ghana News.title: Fiifi Boafo questions Health Minister’s absence as ‘No Bed’ crisis persists
Ghana News.content:
Former COCOBOD Director of Public Affairs, Fiifi Boafo, has questioned Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh's apparent absence from hospital visits, following renewed concerns over the persistent shortage of beds and delays in accessing critical medical care at health facilities.

Mr Boafo said the minister, who previously visited hospitals to highlight challenges confronting the health sector, should demonstrate the same urgency in addressing the problems, particularly as patients continue to struggle to secure treatment.

His comments come amid renewed public concern over the case of a five-year-old boy who is still awaiting brain tumour surgery at the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, despite the payment of GH¢77,561 to the facility for the procedure.

Speaking on JoyNews' AM Show on Thursday, November 19, Mr Boafo questioned why the minister appeared to have moved away from the hospital visits through which he previously drew attention to deficiencies in the country's healthcare system.

“What happened to my friend Kwabena Mintah Akandoh? Is he no more going to the hospitals with cameras to showcase the problems we have?” he asked.

Mr Boafo acknowledged that the minister had previously visited health facilities and publicly condemned the conditions he encountered, but argued that the challenges appeared to be persisting despite those interventions.

“Yes, he went to the hospitals. He told the public, he told all of us that this must not happen. This is bad, this is wrong,” he said.

He maintained that the government must move beyond identifying problems and demonstrate its ability to implement practical solutions, warning that continued delays in addressing healthcare challenges could further undermine public confidence.

“We have solutions. I think people must act,” he stressed.

Five-year-old boy still awaits surgery

Mr Boafo's criticism comes against the backdrop of the plight of a five-year-old boy whose family received public support through the Multimedia Group to raise funds for a critical tumour operation at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital.

Despite the successful fundraising effort, the child is yet to undergo the procedure after his mother was reportedly informed that the hospital had no available bed for him.

The hospital received GH¢77,561 for the surgery on September 14, but the absence of an available bed has delayed the operation, drawing attention to the child's worsening condition and the uncertainty surrounding his treatment.

For Mr Boafo, the situation reflects a wider concern about the government's response to problems within the health sector and the growing gap between public assurances and the experiences of ordinary Ghanaians seeking medical care.

He cautioned that the continued inability to resolve such challenges could gradually erode the confidence citizens have in the government.

“When we continue doing things like this, day by day we are eroding the confidence the Ghanaian people have in us,” he said.

He further warned that the consequences of declining public confidence could have broader implications for politicians, although he stopped short of making a specific prediction.

For the family of the five-year-old boy, the immediate concern remains securing a bed and getting the operation carried out as his condition continues to deteriorate.

Ghana News.title: Investigative agencies to face quarterly scrutiny over treatment of suspects – AG’s Office
Ghana News.content:
The Attorney-General’s Office says a new directive requiring investigative agencies to respect the rights of suspects is intended to address recurring violations of constitutional and legal standards during criminal investigations.

Press Secretary to the Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Benjamin Alpha Aidoo, said the protections were already guaranteed under the 1992 Constitution and other legislation, but Attorney-General Dr Dominic Ayine considered it necessary to reinforce compliance among law enforcement agencies.

Speaking in an interview on Joy FM’s Middaynews on Thursday, November 19, Mr Aidoo said the directive was aimed at ending investigative practices that expose suspects to treatment outside established legal requirements.

"The AG, as the one that wields prosecutorial authority of the state, deems it important to issue this directive in order to stem the recurring practice where the handling of criminal investigations and of suspects fall short of constitutional and legal standards," he said.

He explained that the directive restates protections provided under Articles 14, 15 and 19 of the Constitution, as well as the Criminal Offences Act, the Criminal and Other Offences (Procedure) Act and other relevant laws.

On enforcement, Mr Aidoo said investigative agencies would be required to submit quarterly reports to the Attorney-General’s Office as an additional oversight measure.

He said agency heads were expected to take disciplinary action against officers who violated the directive in accordance with their respective institutional regulations.

Where the conduct amounts to a criminal offence, he said the officers must be referred to independent investigative bodies outside their agencies for investigation and possible prosecution.

Mr Aidoo said the directive relied on existing disciplinary procedures within the various law enforcement institutions, alongside independent investigations where criminal conduct was suspected.

The Press Secretary said the Attorney-General’s priority was to address investigative practices that could undermine the quality of cases prepared for prosecution.

"There seems to be a practice where certain suspect investigations are carried out, sometimes outside the remit of the law, and that actually has consequences for the quality of cases that are built for prosecution," he said.

He added that the directive formed part of broader criminal justice reforms being pursued by the government through the Attorney-General.

Mr Aidoo also outlined channels through which people could report alleged violations, including when they remained in custody.

He said investigative agencies had professional units responsible for receiving and addressing complaints against their officers.

He cited the Police Professional Standards Bureau (PPSB) as an example, explaining that members of the public could report allegations of police misconduct through the unit.

He added that persons whose rights had been violated could also lodge complaints directly with the Office of the Attorney-General.

Ghana News.title: NDC vows action against vote-buying
Ghana News.content:
The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has pledged to take action against any member found to have engaged in vote-buying during its recent regional executive elections.

The party, however, said it was yet to receive a formal complaint about the alleged practice.

The party's National Director of Elections and IT, Mahdi Gibrill, who said this in an interview with the Daily Graphic, said the NDC did not condone the use of money or other inducements to influence delegates, describing the allegations as a blemish on an otherwise successful electoral exercise.

“Even just the allegation is marring the beauty of the elections,” he said.

Police empowered

Mr Gibrill said the party's General Secretary had issued a directive against vote-buying and empowered the police to arrest anyone found engaging in the practice in breach of the laws of Ghana.

He said the directive demonstrated the party's readiness to allow its members to face the law, irrespective of their positions.

He added that the National Chairman had also called on the police to intensify investigations into the allegations.

However, he said videos circulating on social media would not automatically trigger action unless the matter was formally reported to the appropriate authorities.

He gave an assurance that the party would act once credible evidence was available.

Successful exercise

Assessing the regional elections, Mr Gibrill said delegates from all 276 constituencies participated for the first time, resulting in the election of all 288 regional executive members.

He said unlike previous exercises in which some constituencies were unable to participate, and certain regional elections had to be postponed because of data-related challenges, the latest polls were completed without any election-day challenges.

He described the exercise as one of the most successful in the party's recent history.

A national concern

Mr Gibrill said vote-buying was not peculiar to the NDC and called for a national conversation on the roles of both those who offered inducements and those who accepted them.

He observed that the number of delegates had grown from a handful to more than 9,000, raising questions about whether the challenge lay in the size of the electorate or the attitudes of the participants.

“The giver is also a community, and the receiver too is a community,” he said.

He cited demands by constituents for personal and community benefits from political candidates, including boreholes and the threat of “no lights, no vote”, as examples of a broader culture of inducement.

Legal framework

Sections 33 and 34 of the Representation of the People Law, 1992 (PNDCL 284), criminalise bribery and treating in public elections, while the Criminal Offences Act, 1960 (Act 29), also addresses electoral bribery.

However, the laws do not expressly extend these offences to internal party primaries.

A Private Member's Bill seeking to extend criminal liability to party primaries is before Parliament.

Background

The NDC held its regional executive elections on November 14 and 15, amid allegations of widespread inducements to delegates.

Media reports alleged that cash, television sets, fans, stoves, motorbikes and vehicles were distributed during the contests.

In the Northern Region, allegations emerged that a regional chairmanship aspirant, Godfred Apasinaba Wumbei, popularly known as Yellowman, distributed 18 pickup vehicles, one for each constituency, ahead of the polls.

He subsequently won the chairmanship with 328 votes but declined to comment on the vehicles.

In the North East Region, the re-elected regional chairman admitted providing motorbikes and other support to delegates, arguing that financing party activities was part of an incumbent chairman's responsibilities.

The allegations have attracted condemnation from party leaders and calls for investigations, with the New Patriotic Party (NPP) urging the Office of the Special Prosecutor to investigate.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Home of Bangladesh’s former leader Muhammad Yunus set on fire
World.content:
The blaze broke out during heightened violence in the country in advance of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s planned return.

Share Home of Bangladesh’s former leader Muhammad Yunus set on fire on social media

The ancestral home of the former interim leader of Bangladesh and Nobel Peace Prize winner, Muhammad Yunus, was set on fire in the port city of Chittagong, police have said.

The fire broke out before midnight on Wednesday in the city, about 300km (185 miles) southeast of the capital, Dhaka, authorities said on Thursday.

The arson was followed by protests by supporters of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Thursday, as violence swept parts of the country.

Yunus served as interim leader of the country for 18 months after a mass uprising forced Hasina to quit. She was flown out of the country by the military on August 5, 2024.

An abandoned ground-floor room in Yunus’s house was set on fire, and a police patrol spotted it and immediately doused the flames, officer Mozammel Haque told local media.

It was not immediately clear who was behind the blaze.

“Criminals set fire to the eastern side of the house. The area was being used as a storeroom,” Chittagong Metropolitan Police spokesman Aminur Rashid said, adding there were no casualties.

Authorities are investigating, and additional details were not immediately available.

Yunus has faced hostility from supporters of Hasina’s Awami League party, which has since been banned.

Grameen Bank, set up by Yunus, said 22 of its branches have been subject to arson attacks in the last few days. Police have also reported explosions of crude bombs and roadblocks in Dhaka and other locations throughout Bangladesh in recent weeks in advance of Hasina’s planned return.



The 79-year-old politician, who has been living in India since fleeing Bangladesh, announced she would return to the country in December despite facing a death sentence. She told The Associated Press news agency earlier this month that even death could not prevent her from returning to Bangladesh.

Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia last year after a court convicted her of crimes against humanity over the deadly 2024 crackdown on protesters. The government has rejected her request for a new passport and identity card that would allow her to return.

Thursday’s protests were held after a call by the Awami League for a national “lockdown” to mark the anniversary of Hasina’s sentencing last year.

Earlier this week, protesters set fire to a police station and the home of a lawmaker in Gopalganj.

Clashes there killed two members of the governing Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), police said on Thursday, adding that 107 arrests have been made since Wednesday.
