Washington — a summit day · a deal not yet seen Shenzhen — host city · three leaders, one room Ottawa — new tariff relief · quiet pride Kyiv — watching the door · fear of being discussed Moscow — wants the photograph · promises little

The region wakes up on the day the three biggest nuclear powers are due to sit at one table, and nobody outside the room knows what will come out of it. Washington is nervous about the optics, Ottawa is quietly pleased with its own week, and Kyiv is watching a door it is not allowed through.

In the United States the register is high-stakes and slightly tired, with a lame-duck Congress still haggling over Iran war money. In Canada it is calm and a little proud, after Mark Carney came home from Shenzhen with a handshake and a tariff cut.

The through-line is access. Every capital is asking who gets a seat, who gets a say, and who learns the outcome from a press release.

Key Facts —Summit. Trump, Xi and Putin are due to meet in Shenzhen today, Thursday 19 November. —Ukraine. US officials said Ukraine would stay off the agenda. —Canada. Carney and Xi agreed more tariff cuts on Tuesday, covering about US$280 million of Canadian exports. —Industry. US industrial output fell 0.4% in October against a 0.1% rise forecast, pulled down by utilities, the Federal Reserve data show. —Deadline. Federal funding runs out on 11 December, and the Iran war is the sticking point.

Shenzhen: Three Leaders, One Room, No Script

The White House confirmed on Friday 13 November that Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin would meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, known as APEC. It is set for today, Thursday 19 November, and would be the first time the leaders of the three biggest nuclear powers meet together. The mood on the eve was ceremony first, substance later, and every government outside the room is reading the guest list for clues about its own future.

The stated subject is arms control, since the last US-Russia treaty, New START, expired in February. Trump also wants to talk about the war with Iran, and a deal that somehow includes China is the prize nobody expects to be signed today. The most realistic outcome is a set of warm statements that each side reads in its own favour.

Ukraine: The Guest Who Is Not Invited

Last week US officials said Ukraine would stay off the agenda. Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelensky, has voiced concern that major powers could discuss spheres of influence without Ukraine present. That fear is the emotional centre of the summit for Europe, and it is why a vague readout would worry Kyiv almost as much as a bad one.

Ottawa: A Middle Power Takes The Win

Carney met Xi in Shenzhen on Tuesday 17 November, and the two leaders agreed further tariff cuts. China will provide additional relief on Canadian exports worth about C$400 million (about US$280 million), including frozen pork, fish and seafood, according to the Associated Press.

The timing matters because Ottawa and Washington are going through a rough patch. Canada is showing that it can open doors in Asia while it waits for a settlement with the United States, and that is a message aimed as much at Washington as at Beijing.

Washington: Hard Data And A Hard Deadline

The Federal Reserve reported on Tuesday 17 November that US industrial production fell 0.4% in October, against a forecast rise of 0.1% and a 0.7% rise in September. Retail sales rose 0.2%, in line with forecasts, and the Census Bureau’s control group, which feeds into growth estimates, rose 0.6% against 0.4% expected.

Households are still spending while utilities and mining pull industrial output down, a mixed picture that suits nobody’s talking points. The mood in the country is one of patience worn thin, as voters wait for answers on prices, jobs and the war. Funding runs out on 11 December, and several Democratic senators say they will not back a stopgap bill that lacks limits on Iran war spending.

What This Means From Latin America

A Trump, Xi and Putin photograph matters south of the border because tariffs, oil and the Iran war all sit on the same table. Latin American governments will read each readout for hints about who sets the terms of trade next year.

Canada’s new deal with China also tells Brazil and Mexico that a rival exporter is widening its buyers. Every pork or seafood contract Canada wins in China is one its competitors have to fight for.

What We Are Watching

Thursday 19 November: Trump, Xi and Putin meeting in Shenzhen — the first three-way meeting of its kind; watch whether the three readouts match, and what is said on Ukraine and Iran.

Are Trump, Xi and Putin meeting in Shenzhen today?

The White House says they will meet today, Thursday 19 November, on the sidelines of APEC. It would be the first meeting of the leaders of the three biggest nuclear powers together.

Will Ukraine be discussed at the summit?

We could not find a confirmed agenda for the Shenzhen meeting. Whether Ukraine is on the table remains unknown as of this morning.

What did Canada and China agree on Tuesday?

Carney and Xi agreed further tariff cuts. China will give relief on about C$400 million (about US$280 million) of Canadian exports such as pork and seafood.

When does US federal funding run out?

Federal funding runs out on 11 December. Several Democratic senators say they will oppose a stopgap bill that has no limits on Iran war spending.

London — summit Friday · prices edge up Madrid — debate tonight · vote nears Belgrade — parliament seated · no premier Paris — strike thins · count disputed Brussels — UK–EU summit Friday Moscow — door ajar · no date

Europe wakes on Thursday in a mood of impatient waiting. Its leaders are about to meet, its voters are about to vote, and its shoppers are still counting the cost of energy.

The register is tired rather than frightened. Strikes are thinner, polls move by a point or two, and the loudest scenes are in television studios and assembly halls, not on the streets.

The through-line is that Europe is rehearsing decisions it has not yet made. Friday’s summit in Brussels, Spain’s vote on 29 November and the unformed cabinet in Belgrade each ask who may speak for whom.

Key Facts —Summit. Prime Minister Andy Burnham meets EU leaders in Brussels on Friday 20 November. —Debate. Spain’s prime minister Pedro Sánchez and challenger Alberto Núñez Feijóo debate tonight at 4:00 p.m. ET. —Belgrade. Serbia’s parliament was sworn in on 17 November, and no prime minister has been named. —Prices. . — .

Brussels And London: A Summit Waits

Britain’s Office for National Statistics said UK inflation edged up to 3.6 percent from 3.5 percent, a touch below the 3.7 percent forecast. That calm backdrop frames Friday’s second UK–EU summit, where Burnham meets European Council President António Costa and Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on security, illegal migration, crime and red tape for farmers and food firms.

Madrid: One Night To Debate, Ten Days To Vote

Sánchez and Feijóo meet tonight at 10:00 p.m. in Madrid, which is 4:00 p.m. ET, in a debate run by Spain’s Academy of Television and moderated by María Casado. Housing, the economy, corruption and migration are on the list.

Belgrade: A Parliament Sworn In, A Leader Missing

Serbia’s new National Assembly was constituted on Tuesday 17 November after all 250 mandates were confirmed and deputies took the oath. The Student List, the movement that grew out of the protests, holds 140 seats, while Aleksandar Vučić, the former president, now sits among the opposition.

We could not confirm that a speaker has been elected, and no prime minister has been named. The majority has 90 days to form a government, and the mood is of a movement that has won the building but has not yet shown its cabinet.

Paris: The Streets Thin, The Anger Stays

France’s Interior Ministry counted 146,000 marchers on Tuesday 17 November, while the CGT, a large trade union confederation, claimed more than 500,000. Fewer than 3 percent of state civil servants struck, against nearly 10 percent on 5 November.

The crowds are thinner, but the argument over pay and prices has not ended, and each side now fights over the count as much as the cause. Ifop, a French polling firm, said on 3 November that the 2027 presidential race is settling into a duel between Marine Le Pen of the National Rally and the left’s Jean-Luc Mélenchon.

Moscow: The Door Stays Ajar

We have found no announced date or venue for the next round. The Kremlin has also not confirmed the account of US envoy Jared Kushner that Russia agreed to include Europe, so Europe has an open door with no room behind it yet.

What Prediction Markets Say

What This Means From Latin America

Europe’s energy-driven inflation and its crowded political calendar both reach the Americas through trade and capital. In our reading, a Europe distracted by strikes and elections has little appetite for ratifying the EU–Mercosur trade agreement with Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.

For exporters of beef, soy and sugar, delay is the safer planning assumption. Cheaper European energy, if a Ukraine settlement ever arrives, would show first in fertiliser costs for farmers in Brazil and Argentina.

The through-line for readers in the Americas is that Europe is rehearsing decisions it has not yet taken. Each of the stories above, from a Spanish campaign to a Serbian parliament without a prime minister, is a negotiation still in progress rather than a result.

That matters for planning, because outcomes that look settled in a headline often reopen a week later. Our advice is to read this week’s European news as a set of open questions, and to expect the answers to arrive after the votes, summits and deadlines listed below.

One practical consequence follows for investors and travellers with European exposure. Calendar risk is concentrated in the next ten days, so any decision that can wait until after 29 November carries less uncertainty than one made today.

What We Are Watching

— Housing, the economy, corruption and migration are the announced themes. Friday 20 November, 2:00 a.m. ET: UK retail sales for October — The forecast is 0.0 percent on the month after a fall of 0.4 percent.

— They show whether factories and service firms feel the energy squeeze. Sunday 29 November: Spain’s general election — Voters choose the 350-seat Congress, and 176 seats make a majority.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the UK–EU summit and what is on the agenda?

The second UK–EU summit is in Brussels on Friday 20 November. The agenda covers security, illegal migration, crime and cutting red tape for farmers and food businesses.

What do polls say about Spain’s 29 November election?

Spain votes on 29 November, and 176 of the 350 seats in Congress make a majority. Prediction markets, which are bets rather than polls, currently favour the conservative People’s Party to win, as set out above.

Has Serbia’s new parliament chosen a prime minister?

Not yet. The parliament was constituted on 17 November, and the Student List has 90 days to form a government.

How high is inflation in Europe?

UK inflation edged up to 3.6 percent from 3.5 percent, according to Britain’s Office for National Statistics. That is a little below the 3.7 percent forecast, so it does not change the mood at Friday’s summit.

Philippines — host’s glow · alliance work Indonesia — empty chair · long pause China — host’s table · careful smiles Japan — guest’s patience · price watch Malaysia — calm prices · Taiwan chill Taiwan — chip anxiety · watchful

Asia wakes on Thursday like a banquet hall with the place cards still being swapped. Three leaders are due at one table in Shenzhen, a fourth waits for a seat, and several capitals are listening at the door.

The register is formal and watchful: officials speak of dialogue and procedure, while companies and households count the cost of every pause. The loudest voice in the region this week is the one that is not in the room, because Washington, Beijing and Moscow are about to talk over everyone else’s heads.

The through-line is the seating chart, because every story this week is about who is placed near power and who is left to wait. The summit will show whether Asia’s middle powers can bargain from the sidelines or must simply read the result.

Key Facts —Table. Xi, Trump and Putin are due to meet in Shenzhen on Thursday, 19 November. —Nvidia. Jensen Huang left as chief executive on 12 November; revenue was US$115.8 billion on 17 November. —Vacancy. Indonesia’s assembly is due to elect a vice president on 9 December. —Chill. Taiwan’s investment talks with Malaysia stay suspended since 10 November. —Prices. Japan’s core inflation is due at 6:30 p.m. ET Thursday, forecast at 2.3%.

Shenzhen: Three Chairs At One Table

Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin are due to meet in Shenzhen on Thursday, and China’s foreign ministry has confirmed the three-way session. Putin arrived in the city on Tuesday, while Trump left Manila for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, the annual summit of Pacific Rim economies.

The mood is the nervous courtesy of a dinner where the seating plan is the real news. Officials have played down any big deal, so the signal will come from who speaks first, who is photographed together and what is left unsaid.

Tokyo: A Guest Who May Be Seated Last

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is making her first China trip as leader, but diplomatic sources say a formal meeting with Xi looks unlikely. Relations have been strained since her 2025 remarks that a Taiwan emergency could trigger a Japanese military response, and Beijing wants her to retract them.

Tokyo’s quiet goal is protocol: to be treated like every other leader in the room. At home, Japan’s October price data is due at 6:30 p.m. ET on Thursday, with core inflation forecast at 2.3% against 2.1% before.

Silicon Valley’s Shadow Over Asia’s Chip Belt

Nvidia, the American chipmaker whose parts power much of Asia’s electronics trade, announced on 12 November that Jensen Huang had left as chief executive and from its board, with finance chief Colette Kress as interim chief. The company reported third-quarter revenue of US$115.8 billion on 17 November and said its outlook assumes no Chinese data-centre sales. For Taipei, Seoul and Kuala Lumpur, which assemble, test or supply the chips, the leadership gap is a question about how steady their biggest customer will be.

Manila And Jakarta: Hosts Who Still Hold Questions

In Manila this week President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. hosted a US-ASEAN special summit and the first meeting in two years of the Quad, the US, Japan, India and Australia security grouping. Trump and Thailand’s prime minister also signed a joint statement that moves a trade deal forward, though Bangkok says legal drafting is still needed. In Jakarta the vice presidency has been empty since Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned on 12 November, and the People’s Consultative Assembly (MPR) is due to elect a successor on 9 December.

Kuala Lumpur And Taipei: Talks Left On The Table

Taiwan’s foreign ministry confirmed on 10 November that it had suspended investment talks with Malaysia after Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s One China remarks. Anwar told parliament on 12 November that Kuala Lumpur has asked to restart the postponed committee meeting, and that trade is unaffected.

The tone is wary patience, because both sides need the chip trade and neither wants to be first to speak softly. Malaysia’s October inflation came in at 1.9% against a 2.0% forecast, a calm reading that gives Anwar room to wait.

What This Means From Latin America

A Trump, Xi and Putin session matters to Brazil, whose soybean and iron-ore exporters depend on China’s buying and on tariff truces that can change in an afternoon. Any sign that Washington and Beijing are speaking warmly would calm Latin American commodity sellers, while a chill would send buyers elsewhere.

Nvidia’s leadership change and the Taiwan-Malaysia freeze carry a second lesson for Mexico and Brazil, which court chip assembly work. One sentence from a leader can stall an investment channel, and one boardroom decision can unsettle a whole supply chain.

What We Are Watching

Thursday, 19 November: Trump, Xi and Putin in Shenzhen — China’s foreign ministry confirmed the three-way meeting. It shows whether the trade truce and talk of arms control survive the cameras.

— China’s foreign ministry confirmed the three-way meeting. It shows whether the trade truce and talk of arms control survive the cameras. — Forecast 2.3% against 2.1% before. It shows how much price pressure Tokyo faces while its leader is shut out of Beijing’s warmth. It shows whether exports are holding up during the Taiwan chill.

Monday, 23 November, 5:30 a.m. ET: India third-quarter growth — Forecast 7.6% against 7.8% before. It shows whether Asia’s fastest big economy is cooling.

— The previous reading was 5.9% a year earlier. It shows how a trade hub carries the summit season. Wednesday, 9 December: Indonesia’s assembly elects a vice president — The vote is due after Prabowo names two nominees. It shows whether he picks from his own party or from Widodo’s network.

Frequently Asked Questions

When do Trump, Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen?

China’s foreign ministry has confirmed a three-way meeting on Thursday, 19 November, on the margins of the APEC summit. Officials have said they do not expect a concrete deal.

Who leads Nvidia after Jensen Huang?

Colette Kress, the chief financial officer, is interim chief executive since 12 November. The board has begun a search that will consider internal and external candidates.

When will Indonesia choose a new vice president?

The People’s Consultative Assembly is due to elect one on 9 December. President Prabowo Subianto must first name two nominees.

Why should a US reader follow Asia’s summit week?

The Shenzhen meetings shape US tariffs, chip export rules and farm purchases. Nvidia’s leadership change also affects the American stock market and the Asian supply chains behind it.

South Africa — prices · pump · rate day Mozambique — trial · day two The Gambia — campaign · nine names Cape Verde — vote · calm win DR Congo — plague · Ebola

Africa wakes this Thursday counting costs, from the pump in Johannesburg to the courtroom in Maputo and the Ebola wards of Ituri. The tone is steady rather than alarmed, the tone of people who have learned to budget for bad news.

The register is endurance: a fuel-driven price jump, a long trial, a campaign with a crowded field and an ongoing epidemic. Beneath it runs a quiet question, which is who pays when the bill arrives.

The through-line is the cost of carrying on. Households absorb prices, courts absorb politics, and communities absorb disease, and each decides how much more they will accept.

Key Facts —South Africa. Annual inflation rose to 5.2% in October from 4.5%, driven by fuel prices. —Mozambique. Opposition leader Venâncio Mondlane’s Supreme Court trial opened on 17 November on five charges. —The Gambia. Nine candidacies are cleared for the 5 December presidential vote. —Cape Verde. President José Maria Neves won a second term with about 64% of the provisional vote. —DR Congo. Ebola has passed 11,000 cases and 5,400 deaths.

South Africa: The Pump Sets The Mood

South Africa’s annual inflation rose to 5.2% in October from 4.5% in September, Statistics South Africa said on 18 November. Fuel did most of the work, with fuel prices up 11.8% in the month and 42.9% over the year.

The mood is of a country feeling its commute in the wallet. A shortfall at the pump travels quickly into taxi fares, food deliveries and the price of bread.

The central bank announces its rate decision at 8:00 a.m. ET on Thursday 19 November, with a hold at 7.25% forecast. The counterweight is that underlying inflation is lower than the headline, so the bank can argue the shock is a fuel story rather than a wage story.

South Africans also woke to grief this week, after police said at least 17 people were killed in two mass shootings on 15 November, in Pretoria and Pietermaritzburg. Prices and safety are the two things households say they can least control.

Mozambique: A Trial That Will Be Long

The Supreme Court trial of opposition leader Venâncio Mondlane opened in Maputo on Tuesday 17 November. He faces five charges, the gravest being instigating terrorism, which carries up to 24 years, and he denies them all. The case concerns the protests after the October 2024 election.

The mood is guarded, because supporters read the case as politics and the court insists it is not. The court rejected his lawyers’ bid on the first day to have the charges annulled, so the trial moves on to evidence.

What is not known is how long it will run and how much of it the public will see. The court has refused live broadcasts, so the record will be written rather than filmed.

The Gambia: A Campaign With Nine Names

The Gambia votes for a president on Saturday 5 December. The electoral commission has cleared President Adama Barrow to seek a third term, together with eight other candidates.

The mood is brisk and slightly weary. Ousainou Darboe of the United Democratic Party, long Barrow’s main rival, is again in the field.

A crowded list is the old worry of opposition parties, because a divided vote tends to favour the incumbent. The next fortnight will show whether any challenger steps aside for another.

For readers abroad, the point is that a third-term bid in a small, stable country is being tested at the ballot box rather than in the streets. The result will show whether voters accept it.

Cape Verde: A Calm Victory

President José Maria Neves won a second term in the vote on Sunday 15 November, with about 64% in the provisional count. His main challenger conceded defeat. The mood is of an archipelago that treats elections as routine, which is itself the news in a week of trials and campaigns.

The quiet transfer of confidence is a reminder that Africa’s democratic story is not only its disputes. A second term won without a street fight is a form of stability investors price in.

DR Congo: Ebola And Fear

Congo’s Ebola outbreak has passed 11,000 cases and 5,400 deaths, according to Africa CDC, the African Union’s health agency. Its director-general has called it serious and not under control.

The mood in the east is fatigue, because the disease now shares the news with violence. Gunmen linked to Islamic State killed at least 44 people in a series of attacks in Ituri province this week, reported on 14 November. The reading is that outbreaks end when people trust those who tell them what to do.

What This Means From Latin America

Brazil and Mexico know how a fuel shock moves through a household budget, from the pump to the bus fare to the market stall. South Africa’s reading is a reminder that central banks everywhere hold their nerve until the pass-through shows up in wages.

Latin American readers will also recognise Mondlane’s trial, where a court tries an opposition leader whose supporters call it politics. Peruvian and Brazilian observers have debated the same question, and the answer there too depended on how open the proceedings were.

What We Are Watching

What was South Africa’s inflation rate in October?

What is Venâncio Mondlane charged with?

World.title: Cost of Living in Burkina Faso 2026
World.content:
Prices look low on paper, yet food and fuel are getting dearer, cash is hard to find and two governments warn their citizens off the country. Read the official advisories before you plan a move.

Shoppers and vegetable sellers at a market in Bobo-Dioulasso. File photo, 2010, cropped. (Photo: Adam Jones, Ph.D., CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Expat Guide: Burkina Faso

Living in Burkina Faso costs less than in most Western capitals, but prices are rising and the risks are unusually high. Consumer prices were 3.6% higher in September 2026 than a year earlier, the National Institute of Statistics and Demography (INSD), the government statistics office, said in its monthly index note.

Diesel rose to 750 West African CFA francs a litre (US$1.26) on Monday 10 August 2026, up from 675 francs (US$1.13). For a US reader the prices matter less than the warnings: the UK government advises against all travel to the country, and the US State Department, Washington’s foreign ministry, rates it Level 4, its highest warning, Do Not Travel.

Key Facts Inflation. Consumer prices rose 3.6% in the year to September 2026, against 0.4% in March.

Fuel. Diesel costs 750 francs a litre (US$1.26) since 10 August, up from 675 (US$1.13).

Rent. Four-bedroom flats in Ouaga 2000, a district of Ouagadougou, are listed at US$1,006 to US$1,341 a month.

Safety. The UK advises against all travel; the US State Department rates it Level 4, Do Not Travel.

Cash. Bring US dollars: cards work in few Ouagadougou hotels and ATMs take Visa only.

Prices look low on paper, yet food and fuel are getting dearer, cash is hard to find and two governments warn their citizens off the country. Read the official advisories before you plan a move.

Rio Times membership Read everything we publish for US$1 in the first month. Then US$8.99 a month. Cancel anytime. Start for US$1

The Big Picture: Cheap Rents, Rising Prices

Inflation in Burkina Faso has moved from almost nothing to a pace households notice. INSD’s index note for March 2026 put annual inflation at 0.4%, and its note for September 2026 put it at 3.6%, with the index at about 106.9 against 103.1 a year earlier.

The sharpest rises were in food, led by meat, fish and vegetables. In the September note meat cost 17.5% more than a year earlier and fish 11.7% more, while bread and cereals were 7.3% cheaper.

The government raised diesel on Monday 10 August 2026, and Abdou-Salam Gampéné, secretary general of the prime minister’s office, announced it on state television on 9 August. Sidwaya, a Burkinabè daily, reported on 11 August that the increase aims to curb an annual loss of 70 billion francs (about US$117 million) for the state budget.

Prices slipped 0.06% from August to September, so the climb may be levelling off. The INSD notes do not compare Burkina Faso with its neighbours, and we have not found a sourced regional comparison.

File photo from 2004. Shopfronts and traffic along a street in Ouagadougou, the capital of Burkina Faso. Photo: Wikimedia Commons (CC0).

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Burkina Faso Email address Follow

Rent in Ouagadougou

Burkina Faso has no official rent statistic that we could find, so the best guide is what landlords ask. Listings on the housing portal Expat.com, read on 19 November 2026, showed a four-bedroom flat of 200 square metres in Ouaga 2000, a residential district of the capital Ouagadougou, at 800,000 francs a month (about US$1,341).

A second four-bedroom flat in Ouaga 2000 was listed at 600,000 francs (about US$1,006), and a two-bedroom flat with a pool in an area the listing calls Ouaga Trame d’Accueil at 400,000 francs (about US$671). A four-bedroom flat in Bilbalogho, an older central quarter of the capital, was listed at 300,000 francs (about US$503).

These are asking prices, posted between two and seven months before we read them, so they are a guide and not a market average. Our fuller guide to the country, Moving to Burkina Faso, covers housing and health in more detail.

Food and Daily Spending

Food and non-alcoholic drinks make up 29% of the INSD price basket (a weight of 2,904 out of 10,000), so food prices drive the household bill. In the September note this group was 3.4% dearer than a year earlier, even though bread and cereals fell.

Fresh vegetables grown for their fruit, such as tomatoes, cost 21.2% more than a year earlier. We could not confirm shelf prices for a standard grocery basket, or an official minimum wage, so we do not give a monthly budget.

Fuel and Getting Around

The 75-franc diesel rise equals about US$0.13 a litre and 11% on the old price of 675 francs. Burkina Faso has no coast, so its fuel arrives overland, a dependence we explain in our report on the six borders that decide Burkina Faso’s fuel and in our note on Ghana’s share of the supply.

The UK Foreign Office (FCDO), the British foreign ministry, says vehicle hold-ups are increasing on roads outside Ouagadougou and that travellers should avoid driving at night. It names the road from Ouagadougou to Bobo-Dioulasso, the second city, among routes with a danger of armed attacks, and we could not confirm bus fares.

Security and Travel Advisories

The FCDO, whose advice was updated on 26 October 2026 and still current on 19 November, advises against all travel to Burkina Faso. It reports a high terrorism threat throughout the country, “including increasingly in the capital, Ouagadougou”, and a very high threat of kidnapping.

A state of emergency applies in eight regions, among them Centre-Est, Est, Centre-Nord, Nord, Boucle du Mouhoun, Sahel, Hauts-Bassins and Cascades. The Ouagadougou region is not on that list.

The US State Department rates Burkina Faso Level 4, Do Not Travel, in an advisory dated 4 May 2026 that cites crime, kidnapping, terrorism and health. The FCDO also says Britain has no embassy in Burkina Faso and that consular help comes from Accra, Ghana, without in-person assistance.

The FCDO adds that the death penalty returned in October 2026 for offences including terrorism and espionage. For the political background, see our explainer on Burkina Faso’s role in Africa.

Visa, Health and Cash

The FCDO says visitors must have a visa, a passport valid for the whole stay and two blank pages. The official portal, Visa Burkina, offers an e-visa for a stay of under 90 days, but the pages we read gave no fee and did not say whether US citizens can use it.

Entry also needs a yellow fever vaccination certificate, the FCDO says. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) updated a notice on 9 November 2026 on yellow fever outbreaks in the Nando Region of Burkina Faso, and its country page recommends antimalarial medicine for travellers.

The FCDO calls medical facilities “very limited” and says serious cases need evacuation to Europe. It says a few ATMs in Ouagadougou accept only Visa cards, that few larger hotels take credit cards, and that the best option is to bring US dollars in cash.

What It Means for You

For a US reader the franc is the safest part of the budget: the BCEAO (Central Bank of West African States) fixes the West African CFA franc at 655.957 per euro, which at about 597 francs to the dollar on 19 November 2026 implies a euro near US$1.10. A stronger euro would make dollar savings buy fewer francs, and a 3.6% price rise already trims them.

The larger costs are the ones no rent listing shows, namely evacuation cover and the risk of travelling against two governments’ advice. Anyone weighing a move should read the official advisories first and treat the figures above as a guide, not as a budget.

What Is Not Known

We could not confirm the current minimum wage, the pump price of petrol, bus fares or the e-visa fee. Rents come from listings and not from a statistics office.

The date of the next INSD index note, for October 2026, is not confirmed. The same applies to any change in the US advisory after 4 May 2026.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does it cost to live in Burkina Faso?

Inflation was 3.6% in September 2026, and four-bedroom flats in Ouaga 2000 are listed at US$1,006 to US$1,341 a month. We could not confirm a minimum wage or a standard grocery basket.

What is the exchange rate for the CFA franc?

The BCEAO fixes the West African CFA franc at 655.957 per euro. On 19 November 2026 one US dollar bought about 597 francs.

Is it safe to move to Burkina Faso?

The UK government advises against all travel, and the US State Department rates the country Level 4, Do Not Travel. Both cite terrorism and kidnapping.

Do I need a visa for Burkina Faso?

Yes, the UK government says visitors must have a visa, and the official portal offers an e-visa for stays of under 90 days. We could not confirm the fee or whether US citizens can use it.

Can I use cards and cash machines in Ouagadougou?

A few cash machines in Ouagadougou accept only Visa cards, and a few larger hotels and restaurants take credit cards. The UK government says the best option is to bring US dollars in cash.

World.title: Cost of Living in Sudan in 2026
World.content:
Sudan is cheap in dollars and punishing in pounds: the currency has fallen far faster than most incomes, and the biggest costs are power, water and care that are often missing.

Omdurman National Bank and Bank of Khartoum branches beside Omdurman market, Sudan. File photo, 2015. (Photo: ASIM, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Sudan: Cost of Living

Life in Sudan now costs little in dollars and a great deal in pounds, because the currency keeps falling and prices follow it. Sudan Tribune, a Sudanese news site, put the street rate near 11,000 Sudanese pounds per US dollar on Sunday 15 November 2026, up from an April average of 4,050 recorded by the World Food Programme (WFP), the UN food agency.

For an American the first number is not a price at all: the US State Department rates Sudan Level 4, Do Not Travel, its highest warning. What follows describes what Sudanese residents pay in a war that began in April 2023, and our guide to moving to Sudan covers what a stay would involve.

Rent and food look cheap only to people who earn dollars. The costs that hurt most are electricity, clean water and medical care, which are often unavailable.

Key Facts Dollar rate. About 11,000 pounds per US$1 on the street market on 15 November 2026.

Rent. Returnee rents run from 300,000 to 600,000 pounds a month (about US$27 to US$55).

Fuel. Petrol cost 40,000 pounds a gallon (about US$3.64) in Gezira state, south of Khartoum, on 24 October.

Prediction markets. Polymarket, a prediction market, puts a ceasefire by 31 December at 11% (US$119,643 traded overall; 7:50 a.m. ET).

As of. 19 November 2026, 12:50 GMT.

Sudan is cheap in dollars and punishing in pounds: the currency has fallen far faster than most incomes, and the biggest costs are power, water and care that are often missing.

The Big Picture: A Currency in Free Fall

Sudan’s army and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a paramilitary group, have fought since April 2023, and the war has wrecked banks, farms and power lines. WFP’s May 2026 Sudan Market Monitor recorded a parallel-market average of 4,050 pounds per US dollar in April, against 3,170 at commercial banks.

Africa Intelligence One email, every weekday morning. African markets, politics and business — filed from our newsroom in Rio. Yesterday’s subject line: “Ghana's central bank cuts its rate to 11%” Get the brief

Dabanga, an independent Sudanese outlet, headlined the dollar at 10,300 pounds on 22 October 2026, and Sudan Tribune near 11,000 on 15 November. One later report of about 12,000 on 18 November could not be confirmed, so this guide converts at 11,000.

The Central Bank of Sudan’s exchange-rate page lists rates dated 12 April 2023, so we found no current official rate. Every dollar figure below is therefore a street-rate estimate and moves daily.

What Rent and Housing Cost

UNHCR, the UN refugee agency, reported returnees paying 300,000 to 600,000 pounds a month in rent, Dabanga said on 30 August 2026, citing the agency’s June report. At 11,000 pounds per dollar that is about US$27 to US$55, though the pound was stronger when UNHCR counted.

Al Jazeera, a Qatar-based broadcaster, reported on 19 May 2026 that Khartoum property prices had fallen 30 to 40% depending on location and building condition. It added that rents vary with whether a building has its own electricity generator.

Demand is rising as people return: UNHCR’s August assessment counted about 2.5 million people back in Khartoum state, Al Jazeera reported on 3 November. We found no published rent data for Port Sudan, the Red Sea port city, or for housing used by foreign staff.

Workers load donated wheat onto trucks at Port Sudan, Sudan’s main Red Sea port, in a photo from the 2000s. (Photo: USAID, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

What Food and Everyday Goods Cost

In Port Sudan on 12 November 2026 a pound of sugar cost 10,000 pounds (about US$0.91), two pieces of bread 1,000 (about US$0.09) and an egg 1,700 (about US$0.15), Dabanga reported. A kilogram of potatoes cost 12,000 pounds (about US$1.09), and cooking gas 150,000 (about US$13.64), with no cylinder size given.

Inland, power cuts add their own prices: in Rabak, a town in White Nile state, a block of ice cost 60,000 pounds (about US$5.45) and charging a phone 5,000 (about US$0.45) during a two-week blackout, Dabanga reported on 10 November. Al Jazeera reported in May that bread had reached five times its pre-war price.

WFP found the national cost of its local food basket rose 17.9% in April from March. The agency tied the rise to the pound’s fall and to disrupted supply chains.

Fuel, Transport and Power

A gallon (3.8 litres) of petrol cost 40,000 pounds (about US$3.64) in Gezira state and 35,000 (about US$3.18) in Port Sudan, Al Jazeera reported on 24 October 2026. Both dollar figures use today’s 11,000 rate, not the lower rate of that week.

Sudan’s Transport Chambers Union, the transport operators’ body, raised intercity bus fares 40% and minibus fares 30% in October, Al Jazeera reported. A cleaner who earns 400,000 pounds a month (about US$36) told it a short fare rose from 700 pounds before the war to 2,000 to 2,500.

Power and water are the bigger costs. Dabanga reported on 30 August that frequent power cuts remained the biggest obstacle to normal life in Khartoum, and that UNHCR saw a major decline in reliable clean water, so families buy it at markets.

Money, Banks and Getting Paid

Payments are fragile: Dabanga reported on 10 September that outages of Bankak, the Bank of Khartoum’s dominant mobile payment app, disrupted payments and markets. A minibus driver told Al Jazeera on 24 October that he keeps about 50,000 pounds a day (about US$4.55) after fuel and costs.

As simple arithmetic, a monthly pay of US$1,000 converts to about 11 million pounds, about 27 to 28 times that cleaner’s wage. We found no published pay data for aid staff or any guidance on whether foreign cards work.

Health, Hunger and Safety

The US State Department rates Sudan Level 4, Do Not Travel, and says the US Embassy in Khartoum suspended operations in April 2023. The UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) likewise advises against all travel, says there are no British consular staff in Sudan, and warns that travel insurance could be invalidated.

The FCDO says medical evacuation is likely to be necessary for all but the most basic treatment. The 12 October 2026 alert, citing the World Health Organization (WHO), said 37% of Sudan’s health facilities had stopped functioning.

The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), a UN-backed hunger monitor, warned on 12 October of a growing risk of famine across parts of Greater Darfur and Greater Kordofan, regions in western and central Sudan. The alert asked for urgent access to frontline areas, especially North and West Kordofan.

What Is Not Known

No official exchange rate or national price index is published, so every price here is a single-day report from one town, not an average. We found no rent data for foreign-staff housing, and the 18 November street quote of about 12,000 pounds rests on one report.

What It Means for You

For Americans with relatives or projects in Sudan, the street rate decides what a dollar buys: about 11,000 pounds on 15 November, against 3,170 at banks in April. The pound’s fall is why a dollar buys much more rent and bread in pounds than it did in April.

For anyone weighing a trip, both the US and UK governments advise against travel, and prices are the smaller question. Power, water and medical care decide daily life more than any price on this page.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, the platform where people trade real money on events, puts a Sudan civil war ceasefire by 31 December 2026 at about 11%, the midpoint between a 6-cent bid and a 16-cent ask, at 7:50 a.m. ET on 19 November 2026, with US$119,643 traded across all of the market’s dates and US$15,105 on that date. The wide spread marks a thin market, and these prices are bets, not polls.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does it cost to live in Sudan in 2026?

Prices are low in dollars but high in pounds. Rent runs 300,000 to 600,000 pounds a month (about US$27 to US$55), and petrol was 40,000 pounds a gallon (about US$3.64) in Gezira state in late October.

What is the Sudanese pound exchange rate?

Sudan Tribune put the street rate near 11,000 pounds per US dollar on 15 November 2026. We found no current official rate, and one 18 November report of about 12,000 is unconfirmed.

How much is rent in Khartoum?

UNHCR reported returnee rents of 300,000 to 600,000 pounds a month, which is about US$27 to US$55 at 11,000 per dollar. Al Jazeera reported in May that Khartoum property prices had fallen 30 to 40%.

Is it safe for Americans to move to Sudan?

No, the US State Department rates Sudan Level 4, Do Not Travel, and the US Embassy in Khartoum suspended operations in April 2023. The UK also advises against all travel.

World.title: Ghana Offers No Digital Nomad Visa, Only a Short E-Visa
World.content:
Ghana has no remote-worker visa, so the practical route is a short-stay e-visa with paid extensions, a work permit only if you take local work, and tax rules that start at 183 days.

Photo: Enock4seth / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

Ghana does not offer a digital nomad visa, even though several travel websites advertise one. Remote workers who want to spend a few months in Accra, the capital, enter on the standard e-visa, a short-stay permit that the Ghana Immigration Service (GIS, the state border and permit agency) began issuing on 25 May 2026.

That route covers weeks, not a year, and it is issued for tourism and business visits. This guide explains what the rules allow, what an extension costs, and where the legal grey areas sit for an American who keeps a foreign job while living in Ghana.

Ghana has no official digital nomad visa; remote workers use the standard e-visa.

E-visa. Launched 25 May 2026; the visa-on-arrival system was discontinued.

Stay. Portal guide: enter within 90 days, stay up to 60 days, set at the border.

Extension. GH¢65 (about US$5.54) per month for most foreign visitors, per the GIS schedule dated 15 May 2025.

Ghana has no remote-worker visa, so the practical route is a short-stay e-visa with paid extensions, a work permit only if you take local work, and tax rules that start at 183 days.

In Plain English •E-visa. An online visa applied for before travel; it replaced the old visa on arrival. •GIS. The Ghana Immigration Service, which issues visas, permits and extensions. •ECOWAS. The Economic Community of West African States, a regional bloc whose citizens get easier entry. •Work permit. Separate permission to be employed in Ghana; a visitor visa does not provide it. •Tax resident. Someone Ghana taxes on worldwide income, usually after 183 days in the country. •Cedi. Ghana’s currency, written GH¢; US$1 buys about GH¢11.73 (RT, a market-data provider, 19 November 2026).

Free download · Expat checklist Get the free checklist as PDF Moving to Ghana 2026: the step-by-step checklist. This guide condensed into 3 printable pages with tick boxes and the key official links. Email address Get the PDF Your checklist is ready. Download the PDF checklist

Is There a Ghana Digital Nomad Visa?

Legal 500, a law-firm directory, says Ghana has no remote-working visa category, and we found no government statement that one is planned. Several travel sites nevertheless list a “Ghana digital nomad visa” with an income threshold and a fee.

We could not trace those figures to any GIS page, notice or law, so we do not repeat them. If you see a price for a nomad visa, treat it as unconfirmed until the GIS itself publishes it.

The gap matters because nomad visas elsewhere let a foreign employee work legally for a stay of a year or more. In Ghana, a remote worker is simply a visitor, and every question about work and tax follows from that status.

How the E-Visa Works for a Remote Worker

MyJoyOnline, a Ghanaian news site, reported on 25 May 2026 that President John Mahama launched the e-visa portal and that African passport holders travelling for business or tourism apply online and pay no fee. Adom Online, a Ghanaian station, reported that Mahama said the visa-on-arrival system was discontinued and replaced by the e-visa regime.

The official portal, run by the GIS at evisa.immigration.gov.gh, lists the United States among the accepted nationalities and gives standard processing as 96 hours. The portal’s applicant guide says the visa must be used to enter Ghana within 90 days and allows a stay of up to 60 days, which the officer sets at the border, and a sample e-visa notice on the portal says the passport must stay valid for six months beyond the stay.

File photo of the Kotoka International Airport terminal in Accra. Photo: Rjruiziii, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0).

MyJoyOnline reported on 25 May 2026 that citizens of ECOWAS member states and of countries with visa-waiver agreements, which let their citizens enter without a visa, are not affected by the new system. An American is not in that group and needs the e-visa.

We do not quote an e-visa fee for non-African passports, because we could not confirm one on the official portal. Check the fee and the processing time, which the portal gives as 96 hours, before you pay.

Extending Your Stay and What It Costs

The GIS fee schedule that took effect on 15 May 2025, published on the GIS website, lists a visitor-permit extension at GH¢65 (about US$5.54) per month for nationals outside ECOWAS. At that rate, ten months of extensions would add up to GH¢650 (about US$55), simple arithmetic from the published fee.

We found no published ceiling on how long a visitor can keep extending. The GIS also links a revised fee document that we could not open, so confirm the current extension fee at an immigration office before you rely on it.

When You Need a Work Permit

A work permit is the legal route if you take a job or run a business in Ghana. The same GIS schedule lists, for non-ECOWAS nationals, US$1,293 for a company work permit and US$647 for an immigrant quota permit, which covers foreign staff counted under a company’s approved quota.

Yen.com.gh, a Ghanaian news site, reported on 22 February 2026 that a newer GIS list took effect on 2 March 2026 with a US$388 work-permit fee for foreign nationals. It is unclear whether that is the same permit as the US$1,293 company permit, so ask the GIS which list and fee apply before you budget.

We found no GIS statement on whether a visitor may do remote work for a foreign employer while in Ghana. That silence is the central grey area, and you should ask the GIS in writing rather than rely on a blog.

Taxes: The 183-Day Line

Starr FM, a Ghanaian station, reported in April 2024 that the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA, the tax agency) treats a person who spends 183 days or more in Ghana in a qualifying 12-month period as resident under the Income Tax Act 2015 (Act 896). Residents are taxed on worldwide income, according to the same report.

Our guide to Ghana taxes for expats explains how residency can raise your rate. Keep a day-count from your passport stamps, because the 183-day test turns on days in the country.

What Can Go Wrong

The most common risk is an unclear status: a visitor who works from a rented flat may breach immigration or tax rules without meaning to. A second risk is the fee conflict above, which can leave you with the wrong budget.

Passport validity is a third trap, because the portal requires six months beyond your stay. Overstaying is the fourth, since the same GIS schedule lists a penalty of GH¢300 (about US$26) per month for an expired visitor’s permit for other nationals.

A Practical Plan for the First 60 Days

Apply on the official portal at least a week before travel, since standard processing takes 96 hours. Read the fee on screen, check passport validity, and keep the approval on your phone and on paper.

Before the stay runs out, go to a GIS office and ask for the monthly extension at GH¢65 (about US$5.54). Ask the same office, by email so you have a record, whether remote work for a foreign employer is allowed on your permit.

For housing and daily costs, read our guides to the cost of living in Ghana, renting in Ghana and the best places to live. The Ghana country hub and our Ghana residency visa guide cover longer stays.

What Is Not Known

We could not confirm any official plan for a Ghanaian nomad visa, the e-visa fee for a US citizen, or whether remote work on a visitor permit is allowed. We also could not confirm which GIS fee list is current, or whether visitors face a cap on repeated extensions.

What It Means for You

For a US remote worker, Ghana is workable for a stay of a few months but not yet built for a year-round nomad life. Budget about US$5.54 per month for extensions, plan for a work permit only if you take local work, and count your days against the 183-day tax line.

If Accra becomes a base, the next step is a written answer from the GIS, because that single reply decides how much risk you carry.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Ghana have a digital nomad visa?

No official one that we could find. Legal 500 says Ghana has no remote-working visa category, and we saw no government announcement of one.

How long can an American stay in Ghana on the e-visa?

The GIS portal guide says up to 60 days, set by the officer at the border, with entry required within 90 days of approval. Extensions are handled by the GIS inside Ghana.

How much does an extension cost?

The GIS schedule effective 15 May 2025 lists GH¢65 (about US$5.54) per month for non-ECOWAS visitors. A newer list reported in February 2026 may change fees, so confirm at the office.

Can I work remotely for a foreign employer on a visitor permit?

We found no GIS statement either way. Treat it as a grey area and ask the GIS in writing before you start.

When do I become a Ghanaian tax resident?

Ghana treats someone with 183 days or more in the country in a qualifying 12-month period as resident, Starr FM reported in April 2024. Residents are taxed on worldwide income.

World.content:
RIO DE JANEIRO · WHAT’S ON

Updated Thursday 19 November 2026. Prices use the central bank dollar rate of 5.73 reais, set on Monday 16 November.

What is happening Rio’s November 2026 calendar runs from Turandot at the Theatro Municipal to Mariah Carey on Saturday 21 November and Pride on Sunday 22 November.

Why it matters A holiday on Friday 20 November and a Pride parade on Sunday 22 November bring crowds; banks close on the 20th.

The numbers Tickets run from about US$3 (20 reais) for a Turandot gallery seat to about US$86 (495 reais) for Mariah Carey’s standing floor.

Who is who The Theatro Municipal is Rio’s grand opera house; Vivo Rio is a waterfront concert hall; Riotur is the city tourism agency.

What to watch Turandot on Friday 20 November, Mariah Carey on Saturday 21 November, Pride on Sunday 22 November, and Bethânia on Saturday 28 November.

What it means for you Book Mariah Carey seats early, carry photo ID for half-price tickets, and check storm alerts before outdoor plans.

Rio de Janeiro in November 2026 has opera, Pride, a holiday and big concerts. Every price we have is also given in US$.

As of Thursday 19 November 2026, Rio’s big nights are Mariah Carey on 21 November and Maria Bethânia on 28 November. Turandot, which opened at the Theatro Municipal on Friday 13 November, plays again on 20 and 21 November.

Rio has one more holiday this month, Friday 20 November (Sunday 15 was also a holiday but gave no extra day off), plus the Pride parade on Sunday 22 November. Dollar prices below follow the central bank rate of 5.73 reais.

Weather in Rio in November

Brazil’s national weather institute, INMET, and the city’s Alerta Rio service publish the official forecasts and storm alerts.

Afternoon storms are common in Rio as spring turns to summer, so plan beach hours for the morning. Forecasts change daily, so check both services before outdoor events.

This Week in Rio: 19 to 27 November

“Cordélia Brasil”, a tragicomedy by Antonio Bivár about a woman who carries the care of her household, runs at the Teatro Glauce Rocha in Centro on Thursdays at 7pm: 19 and 26 November (the run began on 12 November). João Fonseca directs and Paula Goja plays the title role; the dialogue is in Portuguese, and ticket prices are available from the venue.

“Embarcação Perdue”, a stage comedy-drama about a mysterious expedition searching for what was lost in life, opened on Thursday 5 November at the Teatro Glaucio Gil in Copacabana. It runs Wednesday to Friday at 8pm until 27 November; the dialogue is in Portuguese, and ticket prices are available from the venue.

Concerts and Opera: 20 to 29 November

Turandot, Puccini’s last opera, plays the Theatro Municipal at 7pm on 20 and 21 November (it opened on 13 November).

Individual Turandot tickets run from 20 reais (about US$3) in the gallery to 90 reais (about US$16) in the boxes.

The Associação de Canto Coral, a Rio choral society, marks its 85th year with a concert of José Maurício Nunes Garcia’s Missa de Santa Cecília on 22 November, the second of two performances; the venue and times were not confirmed, so check with the society.

The Centro Cultural Justiça Federal (CCJF), a cultural centre on Cinelândia, the downtown theatre-and-cinema square, in the former Supreme Federal Court building, runs its “Natal Solidário” (Solidarity Christmas) from 17 November 2026 to 7 January 2027. The centre says it will show a custom Christmas tree about 4 metres tall in its entrance hall, the first attraction of that size there, and it opened the programme on 17 November at 6.30pm with a choir, the Coral da Tarde, on its front steps singing Brazilian popular music. The CCJF also collects non-perishable food in partnership with the National Library; ticket or entry prices are available from the venue.

Marcelo Falcão, the former lead singer of the Rio band O Rappa, plays his “O Legado” (“The Legacy”) tour at Qualistage, a concert hall in Barra da Tijuca, Rio’s western beach district, on Friday 20 November at 10.30pm. Qualistage lists the show for ages 16 and over with tickets from 87.50 reais (about US$15), and the press release promises about three hours and more than 40 songs from over 30 years.

Mariah Carey brings her Christmas show to the Farmasi Arena in Barra da Tijuca on Saturday 21 November. Standing-floor tickets cost 247.50 reais (about US$43) half price and 495 reais (about US$86) full price, with gates at 4pm.

Rio Tap Beer House, a craft-beer bar in the Flamengo district, says it marks its seventh anniversary on Saturday 21 November with an afternoon open-bar party serving draught beer from Brazilian and foreign breweries; ticket prices are available from the venue.

Dino Fonseca brings his “Barzim de Rock” show to Qualistage, a large concert hall at Avenida Ayrton Senna 3000 in Barra da Tijuca, on Saturday 21 November. The singer plays more than three hours of Brazilian and international rock classics, the press office says; the show is for ages 18 and over, the show starts at 9.30pm.

Tickets start at 85 reais (about US$15) at the ticket seller named by the venue.

Othon Bastos, 93, whom his press office calls Brazil’s greatest living actor, brings his one-man show “Não Me Entrego, Não!” (“I Won’t Give Up, No!”) to the Teatro Nova Iguaçu Petrobras for the first time. Nova Iguaçu is a city in the Baixada Fluminense, the metropolitan belt north-west of Rio. Performances are on Friday 20 and Saturday 21 November at 8pm and on Sunday 22 November at 6pm; the dialogue is in Portuguese, and ticket prices are available from the venue.

Seal, with Seu Jorge opening, plays Qualistage in Barra on Thursday 26 November. Seated tickets start at 197.50 reais (about US$34) half price and 395 reais (about US$69) full price.

Azymuth, the Brazilian instrumental trio that blends samba, jazz and funk into what it calls “Samba-Doido”, opens its celebration of 50 years of the album “Águia Não Come Mosca” at the Teatro Rival Petrobras on Thursday 26 November at 7.30pm. Founding member Alex Malheiros plays bass, with Dudu Viana on keyboards and Renato Massa on drums; ticket prices are available from the venue.

The 31st Rio Pride parade, the Parada do Orgulho LGBTI+, takes over the Copacabana seafront on Sunday 22 November. Organisers had not published a start time at the time of writing.

O Grande Encontro (“The Great Meeting”), a night of Umbanda music, fills Qualistage on Sunday 22 November at 4pm, with doors at 2pm, the press office says. Umbanda is an Afro-Brazilian religion, and the singers Sandro Luiz and Tião Casemiro play with guests Leci Brandão and Luan Pureza as part of Black Consciousness celebrations; Qualistage lists the show for ages 18 and over, with tickets from 60 reais (about US$10).

Gipsy Kings by Diego Baliardo, billed as a show of rumba flamenca and six guitars, plays one night at Qualistage on Sunday 29 November, with the Brazilian singer Sidney Magal as a special guest, according to the press office. The start time and ticket prices are available from the venue.

Free Things to Do in Rio in November

The Cinelândia – Cinema na Rua open-air series, run by the CCJF, shows “Nosso Sonho” (“Our Dream”), a film about the funk duo Claudinho & Buchecha, on Tuesday 24 November at 6.30pm on Rua Pedro Lessa in central Rio. Entry is free with no tickets handed out, and a charme and funk melody set with DJ Jacaré opens the evening at 5.30pm, the centre says.

The Theatro Municipal also runs a free midday opera series, Ópera do Meio-Dia. Its November dates were not confirmed on 3 November, so check the theatre.

Late November: Bethânia, Clássicos do Brasil and Sailing

The Festival Clássicos do Brasil fills the Marina da Glória on Saturday 28 November from 5pm and Sunday 29 November from 3pm. Saturday brings Maria Bethânia, Alceu Valença and Vanessa da Mata, and Sunday brings Alexandre Pires, Péricles and Ferrugem.

Tickets start at 120 reais (about US$21) on the festival’s own site. The festival returns on 5 and 6 December, and no line-up has been published for those dates.

Holidays, Money and Getting Around

Sunday 15 November, Proclamation of the Republic Day, fell on a weekend and gave no extra day off. Friday 20 November is Black Consciousness Day, a national holiday, and banks and public offices close.

The Banco Central do Brasil dollar rate was 5.7324 reais on Monday 16 November, so 100 reais is about US$17. Half-price tickets, the legal meia-entrada, go to students, people over 60 and others with ID.

What It Means for You

For US visitors, the busiest weekend is 20 to 22 November, when a holiday, Mariah Carey and Pride overlap. Book hotels early; the dollar has bought more reais since the 25 October runoff.

Buy tickets only from the venue or its named ticket seller. Carry photo ID, and keep a rain plan for afternoons.

What to Watch Next

Watch Friday 20 November for the holiday and bank closures, then Saturday 21 November for Mariah Carey. The Pride start time and the December Clássicos line-ups are still to be confirmed.

The central bank publishes a new dollar rate each business day, and this guide returns in December. Football dates for rounds 35 to 37, between 18 and 28 November, are not yet fixed.

What Is Not Known

Organisers had not published a Pride start time or the Ópera do Meio-Dia dates. The theatre site could not be opened on 3 November, so Turandot prices rest on published listings.

What are the holidays in Rio in November 2026?

Friday 20 November (Black Consciousness Day) is the one that remains; Sunday 15 November (Proclamation of the Republic) fell on a weekend and gave no extra day off. Banks and offices close on the 20th.

What are the best things to do in Rio in November?

The top picks are Turandot at the Theatro Municipal until 21 November and Mariah Carey on 21 November. Pride on 22 November and the Clássicos do Brasil festival on 28 and 29 November follow.

What is free to do in Rio in November?

The Amazônicas exhibition at the Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil ended on 16 November. The Theatro Municipal runs a free midday opera series; check its dates.

What is the weather in Rio in November?

Warm and humid, with afternoon storms common as spring turns to summer. Check INMET and Alerta Rio for the daily forecast and storm alerts.
