World.title: Disputed Polish constitutional court announces chief justice stripped of immunity to face charges
World.content: Why are you seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The government-backed judges who recently took control of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) have announced that the court’s chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, has been stripped of legal immunity in order to face criminal charges. Święczkowski, who was appointed to the TK under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government, has condemned their takeover as an illegal “coup d’état” and says that any decisions issued by them have no validity. In a further development, the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) announced yesterday that it has rejected a request by Święczkowski for an emergency order to suspend all proceedings against him at the TK. Trybunał Konstytucyjny zdecydował. Prokuratura może teraz stawiać zarzuty. Nikt nie stoi ponad prawem.https://t.co/trIEqa8Mh1 — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 18, 2026 A statement published on Wednesday evening on the tribunal’s website announced that motions from the prosecutor general, Waldemar Żurek, to strip Swięczkowski and the deputy head of the court, Bartłomiej Sochański, of immunity had been approved. The decision was made by the group of eight judges who dramatically took control of the TK on 30 October as riot police held back protesters outside. All of them were chosen by the government’s parliamentary majority this year, but opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki has refused to swear in five of them. After taking over the tribunal, they declared that Święczkowski and Sochański had been suspended for their failure to properly fulfil their duties. They also launched internal disciplinary proceedings against the pair, with hearings in those cases due to take place later this week. Separately, Żurek, who serves as justice minister in addition to being prosecutor general, filed multiple requests to the TK for Święczkowski and Sochański to be stripped of their immunity in order to face criminal charges. Most of those were approved today. Among the alleged crimes prosecutors wish to charge Święczkowski with are abuse of power and failure to fulfil duties for his refusal to allow five judges chosen by parliament this year to take up their seats on the court. Sochański is accused of the same offences. Święczkowski has argued that he cannot admit those judges because, under Polish law, they are obliged to first swear an “oath before the president” and have not done so. Prosecutors also allege that Święczkowski used violence against those five judges to physically prevent them from entering the judges’ chambers at the TK. The International Commission of Jurists has criticised the takeover of Poland’s constitutional court, saying it “contravenes international standards on the independence of the judiciary” But it also criticised the president for refusing to swear in judges https://t.co/2kBv3GT20d — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 4, 2026 Further allegations against Święczkowski relate to his time serving as national prosecutor under the former PiS government. Prosecutors say that he abused his powers by making unauthorised use of material gathered from surveillance. They also accuse him of abusing his power by “maliciously” reassigning prosecutors to different locations as a form of punishment, despite there being no legal basis for doing so. However, although the TK today approved the lifting of Święczkowski and Sochański’s immunities, it did not consent to them being arrested and held in pretrial detention. It also rejected two additional requests from Żurek to lift Święczkowski’s immunity for other alleged crimes. The TK found the motions contained “formal deficiencies”. Skierowałem do Trybunału Konstytucyjnego kolejny, szósty już wniosek o uchylenie immunitetu Bogdanowi Święczkowskiemu, dołączając go do pięciu wniosków przekazanych w piątek. Dzisiejsza sprawa dotyczy zakupu systemu szpiegowskiego Hermes w czasie, gdy pełnił funkcję Prokuratora… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 3, 2026 Święczkowski immediately rejected today’s decisions, saying that they had no legal validity. He describes the eight judges who have taken control as “usurpers”. However, on Tuesday, Święczkowski suffered another setback in his struggle to retain control over the TK after the European Court of Human Rights announced that it had rejected a request from him and Sochański for an interim measure ordering that all proceedings against them be suspended. The ECHR found that “the applicants had failed to demonstrate an imminent risk of irreparable harm to the core of their rights”. The decision stands in contrast to one made in May this year by the ECHR, when it ordered that the five judges Nawrocki has refused to swear in be admitted to the TK. Święczkowski ignored that order, arguing that the ECHR did not have the authority to issue it. European Court rejects request for interim measure in case concerning Constitutional Court of Poland. 🔗 https://t.co/I15bGXeeKF — ECHR CEDH (@ECHR_CEDH) November 17, 2026 Święczkowski has received backing from some other Polish institutions. President Nawrocki continues to recognise Święczkowski as the chief justice of the TK and has condemned the government-backed judges’ takeover of the court. The chief justice of the Supreme Court (a separate body from the TK), Zbigniew Kapiński, has also sided with Święczkowski and Nawrocki. Speaking to broadcaster RMF on Wednesday morning, Kapiński said that any decisions made by the eight judges who have taken over the TK “have no legal force”. Kapiński’s own status has also been subject to dispute. He was appointed to the Supreme Court under the PiS government through a judicial body overhauled in a manner that rendered it illegitimate, according to various European and Polish court rulings. On Monday, the central bank, whose governor is a longstanding associate of PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński, announced that it was suspending all outgoing payments from the TK’s bank accounts due to uncertainty over who holds legitimate control over the court. Poland’s central bank has frozen outgoing transfers from the bank accounts of the Constitutional Tribunal, citing conflicting claims over who has the authority to manage the court following a takeover by a group of judges backed by the government https://t.co/ZYkzoneojO — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 17, 2026 The recent dramatic events at the TK follow a decade-long crisis around the Polish judiciary, triggered by the contested judicial reforms and appointments made by the former PiS government and PiS-aligned former President Andrzej Duda. The current government – a coalition ranging from left to centre right led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk that came to power in 2023 – has refused to recognise the legitimacy of the TK due to the presence of unlawfully appointed judges. As a result, Tusk’s government has ignored the TK’s rulings and, until this year, refused to even nominate new judges to fill vacancies that arose on the court’s 15-person bench. That changed in March, when the ruling coalition began filling the backlog of empty seats. The eight judges it has appointed now have a majority on the 15-person court, although five of them have not been sworn in by Nawrocki. The remaining seven judges, including Święczkowski and Sochański, were appointed when PiS was in power. World.title: New Kraków mayor withdraws from metro plans and seeks to shrink clean transport zone
World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The administration of Kraków’s new mayor, Łukasz Gibała, has signalled that the city will withdraw from plans to build a metro system and will seek to shrink the size of the recently introduced Clean Transport Zone, which imposes additional costs on older, more polluting cars. “We won’t, like the previous administrations, make any promises regarding the metro,” deputy mayor Karol Wałachowski told local news service LoveKrakow. “We’re withdrawing from this project until central [government] or European funding becomes available.” The draft municipal budget for next year presented by Gibała allocates no funds towards preparation work for the metro, notes LoveKrakow. Instead, the new administration wants to establish seven new tram routes. For decades, Kraków has discussed the possibility of building a metro system, which would be just the second in Poland after Warsaw’s. In 2014, 55% of residents who took part in a referendum voted in favour of the idea. However, only in 2024 did the then-mayor, Aleksander Miszalski, who came to office that year, announce plans to build a metro. The city unveiled the planned route in 2025 and then, in July this year, it launched a 188 million zloty (€43 million) tender for “pre-design” of the project. Kraków has announced a €43 million tender for pre-design work on a planned new metro system, which would be only the second in Poland. The plans include a feasibility study, environmental report and assessment of the impact on existing buildings https://t.co/mB24RcVY96 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 20, 2026 But the idea now looks set to be abandoned after Miszalski was dismissed in a recall referendum earlier this year and Gibała was elected last month to replace him. While Gibała has often said that he would, in theory, like Kraków to have a metro system akin to Warsaw’s, he has argued that it would be impossible to build without significant funds from the European Union or Polish government. During this year’s election campaign, Gibała told news service Wirtualna Polska that he wanted to “honestly tell Kraków residents that, regardless of whether [Monika] Piątkowska [his opponent] or I win, there won’t be a metro anytime soon. We won’t build it without government funding”. Gibała said that, if elected, he would ask the government for a written guarantee of funding. “In my opinion, they won’t [give one], and the metro issue will die. I won’t spend millions more zloty on more expert teams and analyses [to prepare for the metro].” The issue has become tied up in national politics. Gibała is an independent while Piątkowska, his defeated rival, was from Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s Civic Coalition (KO) party. LoveKrakow reports, based on sources, that, if Tusk loses power at next year’s parliamentary elections, a new national government may be more willing to provide funds for the metro project. In one of his first announcements since being elected, the new mayor of Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city, has declared that he will withdraw official patronage of the annual LGBT+ equality march. He argues that the event has become too "partisan" https://t.co/SS2EbRy6Ob — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 14, 2026 This week’s announcement of withdrawal from the metro plans was criticised by one of Miszalski’s former deputy mayors, Stanisław Mazur, who told Radio Kraków that the project should have been seen as “an investment that would significantly support the development of Kraków’s economy”. Two former rectors of Kraków’s AGH University, Antoni Tajduś and Tadeusz Słomka, also told LoveKrakow that it was vital to continue with the preparatory work for the metro system because otherwise, if funding does become available, the city would not be ready to implement the project. Separately, Gibała’s new administration has also presented draft plans to reduce the size of Kraków’s Clean Transport Zone, which was introduced at the start of this year and levies additional costs on drivers of old, more polluting cars. The project has long caused controversy. It was initially meant to go into force in 2024, but was blocked by a court ruling. There have also been legal challenges to the measures finally introduced this year. Many local politicians and officials have argued that the zone unfairly burdens drivers from outside Kraków who need to enter the city, in particular people with lower incomes, who are more likely to drive older cars and are hit harder by the new costs. A court has rejected an attempt to overturn the Clean Transport Zone that was introduced at the start of this year in Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city, and which places restrictions on driving older, more polluting cars https://t.co/NoAKsDgUus — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 26, 2026 During his election campaign, Gibała said that he wanted to reduce the size of the Clean Transport Zone, so that it covered only the city centre rather than the whole city. He also pledged to put any final decision about the zone to a public referendum. This week, another of his deputy mayors, Jan Hoffman, confirmed that city hall had presented draft plans to reduce the size of the zone. However, he noted that any change would have to be approved by the city council and also suggested that any final decision should be made in a referendum. Those plans were criticised by Kraków Smog Alarm, an NGO that fights for cleaner air. They said that reducing the scope of the Clean Transport Zone would harm residents’ health and result in tens of millions of zloty in fees being lost to the city budget. World.title: Polish government seeks to introduce maximum gas prices for consumers
World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has announced plans to introduce a maximum price for natural gas to protect households from the continued impact of the US and Israel’s attacks on Iran earlier this year. The measure would be funded by a new special levy on certain energy companies. To enter into force, the bill must still be approved by parliament, where the government has a majority, and signed into law by opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki, who has vetoed a record amount of legislation. Speaking ahead of a cabinet meeting on Tuesday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk noted that gas prices have been at elevated levels due to the ongoing crisis around the Strait of Hormuz in the Middle East, which is normally a major conduit for both oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG). Tusk pointed out that the European gas benchmark price recently surpassed €100 per megawatt-hour (MWh), which was its highest level in four years. The figure has since fallen to around €85/MWh, though that is still more than double the level in January and February, before the US and Israel attacked Iran. Such costs are “unacceptable for any Polish family”, said the prime minister. “We can’t allow people to suffer because of decisions made abroad… about war in the Middle East. We don’t want Polish families to pay for it.” The government therefore wants to introduce a maximum price of 197.29 zloty (€44.15) per MWh (which is the level of the current state-regulated gas tariff) for the whole of 2027. The energy ministry estimates that this will save households that use gas for heating up to 1,863 zloty over the year. As well as individual households and housing cooperatives, the maximum price will also apply to entities providing important public services, such as schools, nurseries, hospitals and shelters. Companies selling gas to such consumers will then receive compensation from the state to cover the difference if the maximum price is below what the level of gas tariffs would normally be at that time. The costs of this compensation “will be largely covered by a new monthly gas levy” charged to “energy companies holding licences to trade natural gas with foreign countries and selling high-methane natural gas on the domestic market”, says the government. The levy would amount to 10% of net revenues from domestic sales of high-methane natural gas in 2027. Companies holding capacity rights amounting to less than 10% of the total capacity at entry points to Poland’s gas-transmission system would be exempt. While the legislation is unlikely to face obstacles in parliament, it remains unknown what Nawrocki’s position will be. The president has previously pushed for the government to lower energy prices. However, he also blocked a windfall tax on energy companies to subsidise fuel-price cuts, before eventually relenting. President @NawrockiKn has backed down and signed into law the government's proposed windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits, which he had previously blocked. In response, the government has reintroduced measures to lower prices at petrol stations https://t.co/icGEST8NAo — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 2, 2026 Earlier this year, analysis by Allianz, the world’s largest insurance company, found that Poland was among a group of 11 countries “most at risk” from a prolonged closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Poland has become a growing consumer of gas in recent years. As the country has moved away from its traditional reliance on coal, gas has increasingly been used for both electricity generation and home heating. Last year, gas accounted for a record 13.2% of electricity production, up from just 2.7% in 2015. The latest figures from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, show that in 2024 almost 21% of households use gas for heating, up from 10% in 2015. Gas consumption reached its highest ever level in Poland this week – breaking a record set in 2021 – amid freezing winter temperatures and as the fuel continues to play a bigger role in the country's energy mix https://t.co/2wEWLPCV9l — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 10, 2026 The majority of gas consumed in Poland is imported – around 82% last year, according to the energy ministry. Around 43% of imports arrive in the form of LNG, delivered to a terminal at Świnoujście on Poland’s northern Baltic Sea coast. Last year, most of that LNG came from the United States (accounting for 30.7% of Poland’s total gas imports) and Qatar (11.2%). However, LNG exports from Qatar have been severely impacted by the difficulties around the Strait of Hormuz. Earlier this month, Polish state energy giant Orlen exercised its right to terminate one of its two long-term LNG contracts with QatarEnergy, citing “the ongoing force majeure”. However, Orlen insisted that the decision “does not affect the security of gas supplies”. Most of Poland’s remaining gas imports come via the Baltic Pipe, which opened in 2022 and brings gas from Norway via Denmark. World.title: Poland’s central bank freezes constitutional court’s accounts amid leadership dispute
World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s central bank has frozen outgoing transfers from the bank accounts of the Constitutional Tribunal (TK), citing conflicting claims over who has the authority to manage the court following a disputed takeover by a group of judges backed by the government. The National Bank of Poland (NBP), which holds the tribunal’s accounts and is headed by a governor appointed under the former government, said it was not the bank’s role to determine which side was legally entitled to represent the institution. Narodowy Bank Polski wstrzymał realizację zleceń płatniczych Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. Powodem jest spór o to, kto jest uprawniony do reprezentowania TK i dysponowania środkami zgromadzonymi na jego rachunkach bankowych – poinformował NBP.https://t.co/KXwEBL6j9k pic.twitter.com/0h90bPdTLO — Rzeczpospolita (@rzeczpospolita) November 16, 2026 Last month, eight judges elected to the TK this year by the government’s parliamentary majority – but five of whom the opposition-aligned president, Karol Nawrocki, has refused to swear in – took control of the court. They declared that the chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, and his deputy, Bartłomiej Sochański, both of whom were appointed to the TK under the former government, had been suspended for failing to fulfil their duties and launched disciplinary proceedings against them. Święczkowski denounced the move as an illegal “coup d’état”. He has been backed by the court’s other six judges, also appointed under the former government. A few days later, Święczkowski submitted a statement to the NBP identifying himself as the sole person authorised to manage the TK’s accounts. Later that week, after the newly elected judges held their first meeting and made several key decisions, the NBP said it had also received documents “indicating, in principle, other persons authorised to dispose of the funds held in the Constitutional Tribunal’s bank accounts”. Meanwhile, Święczkowski also issued a legal challenge against the TK takeover at the Supreme Court, which on 10 November issued a ruling revoking the order to suspend Święczkowski and Sochański. However, the validity of that ruling is disputed. Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, the judge who has claimed leadership of the TK, said that only the tribunal itself can decide on the issue. Disciplinary hearings for Święczkowski and Sochański are due to begin later this week. Święczkowski, nevertheless, sent the Supreme Court ruling to the national bank as evidence that he remained the person legally entitled to manage the tribunal. The dispute around Poland's constitutional court risks entrenching a system of legal dualism in which judicial authority depends on political allegiance rather than broad constitutional consent, writes @AleksSzczerbiak https://t.co/mtgutqSTQh — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 10, 2026 The NBP’s governor by Adam Glapiński, who was appointed under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government and is a longtime associate of PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński. On Monday, the NBP announced that it would suspend all payment orders relating to funds held in the TK’s accounts, citing “a set of documents, which mutually cancel each other out”. “This means that payment orders are not executed, regardless of who initiates them,” the NBP said in a statement. “The National Bank of Poland has no authority to decide who is legally entitled to control the Constitutional Tribunal.” Finance minister Andrzej Domański criticised the decision, accusing the central bank of becoming embroiled in the political dispute. “The National Bank of Poland should safeguard its independence, including its political independence,” Domański said. He added that the government would “explore all available options” to secure funding for the TK and ensure that it can continue functioning. Justice minister Waldemar Żurek also condemned the NBP’s move, saying its “invocation of a non-existent document [the disputed Supreme Court ruling] to block funding for a constitutional body is…an attempt to protect an entrenched system”. Święczkowski expressed satisfaction that the NBP had denied access to the “usurpers” trying to take over the court but argued that he, as the legitimate chief justice, should be given control over the accounts, reports news website Onet. Prezes Narodowego Banku Polskiego próbuje paraliżować Trybunał Konstytucyjny, powołując się na rzekome orzeczenie Sądu Najwyższego z 10.11.2026 r.. Problem w tym, że ten papier wygląda jak wydany z pieczątką z ziemniaka, a w obiegu są już jego trzy różne wersje. Najpierw Bogdan… pic.twitter.com/7rWELZFIF0 — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 16, 2026 Recent events follow a decade-long crisis surrounding the TK. Since the current government – a coalition ranging from left to centre right led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk – came to power in 2023, it has refused to recognise the court’s legitimacy. That is because three of its judges were unlawfully appointed under the former national-conservative PiS government, which was widely seen to have brought the court under political control. As a result, Tusk’s government has ignored the TK’s rulings and, until this year, refused to even nominate new judges to fill vacancies that arose on the court’s 15-person bench. That changed in March, when the ruling coalition began filling the backlog of empty seats. However, Nawrocki has refused to accept the oath of most of those judges, citing concerns over how they were chosen or their qualifications. World.title: Kraków church holds mass for perpetrator of deadly attack just metres from where he shot victims
World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. The historic St Mary’s Basilica in Kraków has hosted a holy mass for Michał Oksiński, the man who carried out the recent attack in the city and later died of injuries sustained in a shootout with police. The six people who died in the attack and more than a dozen who were injured were shot by Oksiński on the square where the church stands, some of them just a few metres from its doors. St Mary’s Basilica says that the mass is “an expression of the Christian faith in God’s mercy” and “in no way indicates justification for the crime”. On the afternoon of 7 November, Oksiński launched his attack on Kraków’s famous market square, which was packed with locals and tourists. He shot at random from his car while driving through the square and surrounding streets before police managed to bring his rampage to an end. Later that same day, the dead bodies of Oksiński’s parents and sister were found in his home. They had each been shot in the head while sleeping. Two days after the attack, Oksiński himself died in hospital. On Sunday, Łukasz Wantuch, a former city councillor, shared a photograph of an announcement that there would be “a holy mass for the late Michał Oksiński and the deceased members of his family” at the Roman Catholic St Mary’s Basilica on Monday morning. The church, built in the 14th century, is one of the most famous in Poland and dominates the skyline in Kraków’s historic, UNESCO-listed city centre. It stands on one corner of the market square, just a few steps from where some of Oksiński’s victims were shot. “I won’t hide the fact that I find this somewhat shocking,” wrote Wantuch. He noted that the announcement referred to the “blessed memory” (świętej pamięci) of Oksiński. However, that phrase is standard usage in Polish to refer to someone who has died (the equivalent ot the English “late”). “But perhaps that is what faith is about: praying even for a murderer,” added Wantuch. Among the more than 1,000 comments under his Facebook post, many agreed with that sentiment. “The whole of Christianity is based on forgiving the unforgivable,” wrote one. “I don’t think anyone needs God’s mercy more [than Oksiński],” said another. However, some others were critical of the fact that the mass was being held in that particular church among the dozens in Kraków. “It is the height of impudence that they’ll celebrate mass for him in the very church he murdered in front of,” wrote one commenter. Later on Sunday, St Mary’s Basilica issued a statement, signed by parish administrator Father Mariusz Słonina, saying that the holy mass “is a private initiative of one of the priests, not of St Mary’s Parish”. However, Słonina added that “praying for the deceased is an expression of the Christian faith in God’s mercy” and “in no way indicates justification for the crime, a lessening of the perpetrator’s responsibility, or a trivialisation of the suffering of the victims”. Local news service KR24 reported that uniformed police officers were posted outside the church for today’s mass while plainclothes officers were inside, with one of them right next to the altar. Three priests were present, including Słonina, who presided over the mass. Only around a dozen faithful were in attendance, with KR24 suggesting that many did not even seem aware for whom mass was being held. Separate private funeral ceremonies will take place for Oksiński, his parents and sister, who lived in the town of Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, about 160 km from Krakow. On Sunday, their family issued a statement asking the media to “respect the privacy, dignity and mourning of our family and loved ones”. Meanwhile, police and prosecutors continue to investigate the possible motive behind Oksiński’s attack, which they are treating as a terrorist offence. Last week, the justice minister said that there were “very strong traces of right-wing extremism” in the perpetrator’s online activity. Two police officers, Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański, who were seriously injured in the shootout that debilitated Okisński, have been recovering in hospital after undergoing emergency surgery. World.title: Poland detains neo-Nazi teens accused of terrorist plot

Poland has detained and charged three teenagers who are allegedly linked to “an international neo-Nazi network” and had been planning terrorist attacks, including with the use of homemade explosives. The arrests were announced on Monday morning by Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of the security services, who revealed that the suspects are Polish citizens. Two are aged 17 and one is 16. “The teenagers not only promoted Nazi and fascist ideology but had also already taken steps toward committing terrorist offences,” wrote Siemoniak. Funkcjonariusze @ABW_GOV_PL zatrzymali 3 obywateli RP, 16-latka i dwóch 17-latków, związanych z międzynarodowym środowiskiem neonazistowskim. ▶️ Nastolatkowie nie tylko propagowali ideologię nazistowską i faszystowską, ale podejmowali już działania zmierzające do popełniania… — Tomasz Siemoniak (@TomaszSiemoniak) November 16, 2026 The National Prosecutor’s Office revealed that the trio were “fascinated by the activities of an international neo-Nazi terrorist organisation…[that] has an ideology based on hatred against people of Jewish descent, immigrants, black people, the LGBT community, politicians and state security officials”. Though prosecutors did not name the organisation, they said that members of it have been involved in planning terrorist attacks in the United States, Germany and the United Kingdom. In some countries, including the UK, Canada and Australia, it has been outlawed and designated a terrorist group. Poland’s Internal Security Agency (ABW) had found that the three suspects’ online communication indicated “an interest in constructing explosive devices, modifying weapons and using such items to carry out terrorist activities”. During a search of the home of one of the 17-year-olds (named only as “suspect 1”), officers found chemicals that are precursors for the production of explosives. That suspect has also been charged with possession of a so-called pipe bomb, which prosecutors say he wanted to “transfer to a neo-Nazi terrorist group”. Suspect 1 was found to have discussed with the other 17-year-old, named as suspect 2, how to construct an explosive device and detonate it in a specific residential building where someone they knew lived. Suspect 1 had also “incited extremist behaviour and hate-motivated violence” in his online activity, while the 16-year-old, named as suspect 3, had “promoted fascist content” (a crime in Poland) and encouraged someone to assault another person based on their race. Each suspect has been charged with three crimes, relating variously to terrorist offences, possession or attempted production of explosives and weapons, promoting Nazism, fascism and racial hatred, and inciting others to commit violence based on racial differences. Prosecutors note that Polish law generally allows people to face full criminal liability from the age of 17. The two 17-year-olds have therefore been placed in adult pretrial detention, while the 16-year-old is being held in a juvenile facility. Śledztwo w sprawie neonazistów i planowanych aktów terroru kryminalnego Szczegóły w komunikacie: ⬇️https://t.co/dQpdgiTYJD — Prokuratura Regionalna w Gdańsku (@Prok_Regio_GDA) November 16, 2026 The arrests come in the context of recent concerns over radicalisation of young people in Poland. Earlier this month, a 24-year-old carried out a terrorist attack in the city of Kraków, killing six people by firing a rifle from his car. He had earlier killed his parents and sister in their home. In the aftermath of the attack, justice minister Waldemar Żurek revealed that investigators had found “very strong traces of right-wing extremism” in the attacker’s online activity, though he emphasised that the motive was yet to be determined. In the space of a few days last month, three knife attacks took place in Polish schools, resulting in one case in the death of a member of staff. Dozens of young people were arrested in the aftermath for making threats and/or possessing weapons. In September, the security services detained three teenagers accused of being part of online groups promoting neo-Nazism and violence. One of them has been charged with planning terrorist attacks on targets including a mosque and a school. World.title: GTA VI Launch Week Comes With Special Food Menus Across Prague
World.content:
With Grand Theft Auto VI arriving on November 19, Bolt Food has teamed up with Prague restaurants to offer exclusive gaming menus, discounts and a competition to win PlayStation 5 consoles and copies of the game.

After years of anticipation and two delays, Grand Theft Auto VI finally arrives on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on Thursday, November 19. For many players, the launch is likely to mean long gaming sessions and late nights. In Prague, there will also be plenty of food options to go with them.



From November 9 to 22, Bolt Food is running a special Gaming Campaign, bringing together local restaurants that have created menus inspired by the new game. The selection includes burgers, pizzas, sushi, chicken dishes and larger sharing meals, available exclusively through the delivery platform.

The campaign also includes discounts on selected offers and a competition featuring PlayStation 5 consoles and copies of GTA VI.

Win a PlayStation 5 or GTA VI

Bolt Food is giving away three PlayStation 5 consoles and 36 copies of Grand Theft Auto VI as part of the campaign.

To enter, customers need to order one of the participating gaming menus or place an order worth at least CZK 350 from a participating restaurant. Each qualifying order automatically counts as one entry, with no additional registration required.

Some orders may also include surprise gifts from Niceboy.

The competition runs in Prague until November 22. Full terms and conditions are available through Bolt Food’s Czech Instagram account, @boltfood_cz.

What Prague Restaurants Are Offering

Several restaurants have put together special dishes and combinations for the campaign. Here are some of the options available through Bolt Food.

Burgers and Comfort Food

Hoxton Burgers – Chorizo Smash

The burger restaurant has prepared a special smash burger featuring chorizo.

Želva – Trevor Burger

A substantial combination of a 170-gram beef patty, double cheddar, bacon chutney, blue cheese, maple syrup, crispy onions, jalapeños and chipotle mayonnaise, finished with a poutine topping.

Master Burger – Sunrise Burger

Beef, cheddar, bacon and a fried egg make up this burger, which takes inspiration from a classic breakfast combination.

Amici – Gaming Pizza and Burger Menus

Customers can choose between special gaming-themed pizza and burger menus.

Pizza for Sharing

Three Prague pizzerias have also joined the campaign with exclusive combinations.

Davinci offers three options: Street Hustler, Five Star Chase and Million Dollar Slice.

Presto Italiano has created three pizzas named after GTA-inspired characters: Jason’s Pizza, with chicken, pepperoni, bacon and red onion; Lucia’s Pizza, featuring pepperoni, bacon, chilli and Parmesan; and Raul’s Pizza, with a cream base, chicken, bacon, Gorgonzola and garlic.

Caruso is serving a Gaming Pizza topped with ham, bacon, spicy salami, smoked scamorza and onion.

Sushi and Japanese Food

Sushi fans can choose from several campaign-specific options.

Doebikokota – Respect +

The combination includes Philadelphia Classic rolls, crispy chicken gyoza and Coca-Cola.

Aurum Sushi has introduced three gaming options: Hot Pursuit, The Big Score and Wanted.

Imperial Sushi is offering several dishes, including Geisha Roll, Salmon & Tuna Snack, Office Snack, Baked Chicken on Iceberg Roll and Baked Chicken Tamago Roll.

Hasu Sushi – Hasu Gaming Challenge Set**

The special 18-piece set includes salmon nigiri, salmon maki and Sunshine Roll.

Chicken and Wraps

For those looking for something easy to eat during a gaming session, two restaurants are offering chicken-based options.

Chickin has introduced the GTA Power Griller and GTA Quesadilla, both available in double-bacon versions.

Louisiana Chicken is serving the Six Stars Sandwich, featuring crispy chicken strips with bacon-chilli sauce, tomato and iceberg lettuce, as well as the Wanted Wrap, which combines chicken nuggets with the same sauce.

Wraps, Kebabs and Sharing Combos

Other participating restaurants have opted for larger combinations and meals designed for different group sizes.

Burrito Loco – Crunchy Wrap Gaming Menu

The menu includes a drink and a choice of churros with chocolate dip or chips and salsa.

Mahir Kebab offers three combinations: Solo Mission, Duo Heist and Full Crew Combo, with portions designed for one, two or three people.

Matoka – I’m The Gamer Set

A special menu created for the campaign.

Something for the End of the Night

For those looking for a more substantial meal or something sweet, two more restaurants have joined the line-up.

Lasagneria – Spicy Lasagna and Oreo Tiramisu Combo

The main course combines Italian salsiccia sausage, chilli, béchamel and Grana Padano. Dessert comes in the form of Oreo tiramisu with mascarpone cream and espresso.

Na Květnici – Jason Duval Menu

A special menu named after one of the two main characters in GTA VI.

How to Order

All campaign menus are available through the Bolt Food app. Customers can browse the participating restaurants, select their preferred dishes and order directly for delivery.

The Gaming Campaign runs until November 22, meaning the special menus will only be available for a limited period.

Whether you’re planning a gaming night with friends or simply looking for something different to order this week, Prague’s restaurant line-up has plenty of options.

World.title: Prague Christmas Markets 2026 – Dates, Locations and Opening Hours
World.content:
Prague’s Christmas market season will begin on November 20, with the first stalls opening at Náměstí Míru.

The main markets in the city centre will follow on November 28, when the Christmas tree in Old Town Square will also be illuminated for the first time.

Markets and Advent events will take place across the Czech capital, from the historic centre to neighbourhoods such as Vinohrady, Smíchov and Karlín. While some will close on Christmas Eve, others will remain open until January 6, 2027.



Prague Christmas Markets 2026 – Full Schedule

Náměstí Míru | Nov 20 – Dec 24 |

Náměstí Republiky | Nov 25 – Dec 24 |

Tylovo náměstí | Nov 26 – Dec 24 |

Anděl, Smíchov | Nov 27 – Dec 31 |

Mariánské náměstí | Nov 27 – Jan 6 |

Old Town | Nov 28 – Jan 6 |

Wenceslas Square | Nov 28 – Jan 6 |

Jiří z Poděbrad Square | Nov 28 – Dec 23 |

Karlínske náměstí | Dec 6 |

When Will the Christmas Tree in Prague Be Lit?

The Christmas tree in Old Town Square will be illuminated for the first time on Saturday, November 28, marking the opening of Prague’s main Christmas market.

According to organiser Taiko, the tree will be installed on November 23 and 24. This year’s Norway spruce comes from Šimonovice in the Liberec Region. It is approximately 60 years old, stands 23 metres tall and has a trunk circumference of more than two metres.

After the Christmas season, apprentices from Jarov Secondary Vocational School will process its wood into products for social organisations in Prague.

Where to Find the Main Christmas Markets

Old Town Square

November 28, 2026 – January 6, 2027

Daily, 10:00–22:00

Prague’s largest Christmas market will feature wooden stalls selling decorations, handicrafts, gifts and traditional seasonal food. The Christmas tree and its lighting ceremony will once again be the main attraction.

Wenceslas Square

November 28, 2026 – January 6, 2027

Daily, 10:00–22:00

Located a short walk from Old Town Square, the market will offer Christmas decorations, gifts, handicrafts and refreshments.

Náměstí Míru

November 20 – December 24, 2026

Daily, 10:00–20:00

The first Christmas market of the season will open around the Church of St Ludmila. Stalls will sell Advent wreaths, candles, decorations, sweets and seasonal refreshments.

Anděl

November 27 – December 31, 2026

Daily, 8:00–20:00

The market in Smíchov’s pedestrian zone will remain open until New Year’s Eve, making it one of the few locations operating after Christmas.

Other Christmas Events in Prague

Several additional events will take place during Advent.

– Bavarian-Czech Advent Market: November 27–29 at Chotek Palace, with regional food, nativity scenes, woodcarving demonstrations and workshops.

– Christmas Craft Markets: December 5–6 at Výstaviště Praha, featuring around 150 artisans. Admission is free.

– Lemarket: December 11–13 at Galerie Mánes, showcasing Czech designers, independent brands, fashion and handmade gifts.

– New Town Advent: December 13 at the New Town Hall, with craft stalls, workshops, performances and free admission.

World.title: Chinese National Circus to Make Czech Debut in February 2027
World.content:
The National Circus of China will perform in the Czech Republic for the first time in February 2027, bringing its production ZENSATION: Grandmasters of Balance to Prague, Brno and Ostrava.

The show combines traditional Chinese acrobatics with contemporary stage production, drawing on an artistic tradition that dates back more than 2,000 years.



Titled ZENSATION: Grandmasters of Balance, the production brings together some of the circus’s best-known acts in a programme featuring performers trained at China’s leading circus academies.

Many have spent most of their lives mastering acrobatic disciplines, with years of intensive training behind the precision and control required for each performance.

The programme is designed as a retrospective of the Chinese circus, revisiting celebrated routines that have received awards at international festivals and attracted audiences around the world.

Rather than relying on elaborate visual effects, the production puts the emphasis on the performers themselves, highlighting balance, coordination, physical strength and precision.

Its approach combines established acrobatic techniques with a contemporary presentation, placing the human body and its capabilities at the centre of the show.

The production is directed by Raoul Schoregge, artistic director of the Chinese National Circus in Europe. Under his direction, the show brings together highlights from the circus’s long history in a format intended to appeal to both established fans of acrobatics and audiences encountering the tradition for the first time.

The February 2027 tour will visit three cities:

– Ostrava – February 2027

– Brno – February 2027

– Prague – February 2027

Tickets are available here.

World.title: Could You Crack the Case? English-Language Detective Game Comes to Prague
World.content:
On November 29, The Globe Bookstore & Café will host The Edenmoor Case, an interactive detective game that challenges teams to solve a fictional crime by examining evidence, questioning witnesses and putting their theories to the test.

Set in 1928 in the fictional town of Edenmoor, Louisiana, the game invites participants to step into the role of investigators.

Armed with an initial case file, players must uncover what happened, determine who can be trusted and build a convincing case before their time runs out.



Unlike traditional escape rooms, The Edenmoor Case does not rely on elaborate physical sets or theatrical performances. Instead, teams gather around a table and conduct their investigation through a digital platform, accessible from a laptop, tablet or smartphone.

The platform allows players to explore different locations, question witnesses, examine documents and uncover new leads. But the information they encounter is not always straightforward. Witness accounts may contradict one another, seemingly important details can lead nowhere, and a single overlooked clue could change the direction of an investigation.

Much of the experience unfolds through discussion between team members. Players compare their findings, challenge one another’s assumptions and decide which leads are worth pursuing.

With limited time and multiple possible interpretations of the evidence, reaching a shared conclusion becomes part of the challenge.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by The Edenmoor Case | Detective Game Prague (@edenmoor.case)

The game also introduces a competitive element. Several teams investigate the same crime simultaneously, working with identical evidence and under the same two-hour time limit. Each team must submit its conclusions, with the challenge focusing on the strength of the investigation rather than simply who finishes first.

Designed for groups of two to eight people, the English-language experience offers an alternative to traditional group activities in Prague. Friends, couples and colleagues can take part together, while individual participants are also welcome to register.

The next session takes place on Sunday, November 29, at The Globe Bookstore & Café, Pštrossova 6, Prague 1. Doors open at 4:00 PM, and the investigation begins at 5:00 PM.

Tickets cost 300 CZK per person in advance or 330 CZK at the door.

World.title: Samosas, Biryanis and Tandoori: Three Reasons to Visit Ekant in Prague
World.content:
Karlovo náměstí is not usually the first place people think of when planning a dinner out in Prague.

It is central, but it lacks the restaurant scene of neighbourhoods such as Vinohrady or Karlín. There are plenty of reasons to pass through, but perhaps fewer to stay for dinner.

Ekant Indian Restaurant is one of them.



The restaurant serves a broad menu of North Indian dishes, from curries and tandoori specialities to biryanis, samosas and freshly baked naan.

If there are two things worth ordering, they are the samosas and the biryanis. The latter are a particularly good alternative to the usual curry-and-rice combination, while the samosas make an easy choice to start a meal.

The menu also covers chicken, lamb and seafood dishes, alongside a sizeable vegetarian selection. Vegan options are available, too, and the restaurant can accommodate certain dietary requirements on request.

There is plenty of choice, whether you are visiting for a quick lunch, a relaxed dinner or a meal with friends. The restaurant has a casual dining room, with table service, takeaway and delivery available.

World.title: Need a Plumber or Electrician in Prague? This App Can Help
World.content:
Finding a reliable plumber, electrician, cleaner or handyman can be time-consuming, particularly for foreigners living in the Czech Republic who may not know where to look or whom to contact.

A Czech platform called Helplii aims to make the process easier by bringing customers and local service providers together through a single online marketplace.



Instead of searching through multiple websites, social media groups or personal recommendations, users can describe the job they need done and post a request through the Helplii app. Local professionals can then respond with offers, allowing customers to compare prices, availability and reviews before deciding whom to hire.

The process is designed to cover everything in one place. Once an offer has been accepted, customers can communicate directly with the provider through the app, share details and photos, and arrange the work. Payments are also handled through the platform.

Helplii covers a wide range of everyday services, including plumbing, electrical work, home repairs, cleaning, furniture assembly, gardening, moving assistance and pet sitting.

The platform also lists services such as IT support, accounting, tutoring, photography and translation.

According to the company, its marketplace currently covers more than 25 service categories and 16 cities and towns across the Czech Republic.

The platform focuses primarily on freelancers and small businesses, although larger service companies can also register. To offer services in the Czech Republic, providers must have a registered business identification number (IČO).

Helplii also includes several features intended to make transactions more transparent. Providers submit their own prices, customers can review ratings and feedback from previous jobs, and communication takes place within the app. Phone numbers remain hidden until an offer is accepted.

For service providers, the platform offers another way to find customers without having to rely entirely on advertising or personal contacts. They can receive requests matching their skills and availability, submit their prices and build a reputation through customer reviews.

Helplii is available for both iOS and Android devices.

World.title: West Ham Star Tomáš Souček Launches English Autobiography in Prague
World.content:
Tomáš Souček has presented the English edition of his autobiography at the British Embassy in Prague, with the book set to reach UK readers ahead of Christmas.

British Ambassador Matt Field welcomed the West Ham United midfielder to Thunovský Palace on Monday, November 16, for the launch. The event marked the next step for the autobiography, which was first published in the Czech Republic a year ago.

The English edition will be titled Tomáš Souček – My Story and will initially be available through West Ham’s official fan shop. Souček said the decision to translate the book had been made from the beginning, with the aim of making it accessible to supporters in England.



“I’m living a second life in England. My children are growing up there, and I feel right at home. That’s why I’m so happy we can bring this book to West Ham fans. I have an incredible connection with them, and they deserve it,” Souček said to Prague Morning.

The launch also featured an unusual alternative to the traditional champagne toast. Instead of pouring sparkling wine over the book, Souček and Field blew bubbles above its cover, referencing West Ham’s pre-match tradition and the club anthem I’m Forever Blowing Bubbles.

“In England, seeing a bubble blower means seeing West Ham. Besides, I’m not really a fan of being doused in alcohol. Bubbles are a much better fit for this book,” Souček said.

Field, meanwhile, recalled watching the Czech midfielder lift the UEFA Europa Conference League trophy in Prague in 2023.

“I’ve been a fan ever since. I know he’s scored more goals in the Premier League than any other Czech footballer. But apparently, that wasn’t enough for him, so he decided to write a book, too. As a diplomat, I can only hope he doesn’t decide to try his hand at my job as well. That would start to look like a hat-trick,” the ambassador joked.

The autobiography was written by Souček together with football journalists David Čermák and Jan Palička. It covers both his professional career and personal life, including his struggles with insomnia and depression at different stages of his football journey.

The English edition includes an additional chapter covering West Ham’s relegation season, the disappointing World Cup campaign in the United States and Souček’s return to football after a serious ankle injury.

World.title: Furiant Is Back: Prague’s Czech Sweets Pop-Up Reopens November 27
World.content:
Furiant, the Czech pastry pop-up that attracted long queues and sold out daily during its first run, will reopen on November 27 at its original location inside the Parnas restaurant.

The project brings together Jiří Matějka, former head pastry chef at Karlín’s Eska and Café Slavia, and Jozef Onderka, owner of Café Slavia, SmetanaQ and the Forbína cocktail bar.



Their idea was to create a modern Czech confectionery focused on traditional sweet dishes rather than the croissants and French-style pastries found in many of Prague’s newer bakeries.

When Furiant first opened in October 2025, the response exceeded expectations. Operating from Thursday to Sunday, the pop-up sold out every day, sometimes closing earlier than scheduled.

The team initially struggled to keep up with demand, choosing not to increase production at the expense of quality.

Matějka developed the concept after several years working in Berlin, where he began to miss traditional Czech sweets. His experience at Eska and abroad helped shape an approach that combines familiar dishes with contemporary pastry techniques and carefully selected ingredients.

The menu puts the spotlight on Czech sweet meals, including semolina porridge, rice pudding, plum dumplings, pancakes and buchtičky se šodó (small sweet yeast buns served with vanilla custard).

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Furiant (@furiant_prague)

One of Furiant’s defining characteristics is its deliberately limited menu, which changes regularly according to the season and availability of ingredients.

The kitchen works with Czech flour, dairy products from the Struhy farm, chocolate from the Herůfek family and locally sourced poppy seeds, which are ground on-site.

The reopening will give Prague residents another opportunity to visit the pop-up at Parnas, overlooking the Vltava River and Prague Castle.

World.title: Hungary’s Ministry of Defence signed contract with fugitive businessman wanted by the government
World.content:
Hungary’s Ministry of Defence has come under scrutiny after one of its offices signed a HUF 661 million (approximately EUR 1.79 million) furniture procurement contract with a company overwhelmingly owned by businessman György Stofa, just five days after police issued an arrest warrant for him in connection with the scandal surrounding the National Bank of Hungary.

Company of businessman linked to the Matolcsy scandal earns government contract

The agreement with Gyulai “Fafém” Bútor Zrt. was signed on 26 October by the Defence Economy Office, a background institution of the Ministry of Defence. Stofa owns 99 per cent of the company indirectly through another business, Fur-Real Kft., according to corporate records cited by 24.hu.

The businessman was declared wanted on 21 October in an investigation into alleged financial fraud involving the central bank. An international and a European arrest warrant were subsequently issued against him.

Furniture contracts worth hundreds of millions

According to documents obtained by 24.hu, Gyulai “Fafém” Bútor won the procurement in a consortium with Miskolc-based Iroda 2000 Kft. The companies were contracted to supply office chairs worth HUF 503 million (EUR 1.36 million) and manufacture built-in cabinets for a further HUF 157 million (EUR 425,400). The furniture is intended for the military’s Logistics Support Command and the Hungarian Defence Forces’ Materials Supply Depot.

The procurement was carried out under a framework agreement established last year, during the previous Orbán government. The Public Procurement and Supply Directorate had organised a wider tender worth up to HUF 50 billion (EUR 135.5 million) for office furniture for state institutions. Under the framework, suppliers compete again when individual orders are placed.

The arrangement has raised questions about how a company linked to a wanted businessman was selected after an arrest warrant had been issued against its owner. The Public Procurement and Supply Directorate confirmed to 24.hu that the contracts had been signed on 26 October, but said no fulfilment had yet been recorded on its procurement portal. The Ministry of Defence was also sent questions about the deal.

Links to former central bank leader Matolcsy

Stofa is closely associated with Ádám Matolcsy, the son of former National Bank of Hungary governor György Matolcsy. Prosecutors suspect the two businessmen of economic fraud in a case involving the central bank. Neither has reported to the authorities, and their whereabouts remain unknown.

György Matolcsy, who led the central bank from 2013 to 2025, has also been detained in connection with the investigation. Stofa previously held management positions in several companies linked to the central bank and was involved in business activities surrounding Villa Nicole in Mykonos, associated with Ádám Matolcsy. His name has also emerged in connection with the Kégl Castle property in Székesfehérvár-Csalapuszta.

The Ministry of Defence also awarded a separate HUF 731 million (EUR 1.98 million) furniture contract to IMG Office Kft. and Garzon Novum Kft. IMG Office is linked to Gábor Szentgyörgyi, a former wrestling partner of Győző Orbán Jr, the brother of former prime minister Viktor Orbán.

The contracts have prompted questions about due diligence in state procurement, particularly when companies are linked to individuals wanted in a major financial investigation. The Ministry of Defence so far has not answered to questions.

World.title: Official: Budapest’s Buda Castle district to ban Airbnb-style rentals
World.content:
Budapest’s District I council has approved new regulations on short-term accommodation, introducing a complete ban on such rentals in the Buda Castle District from 1 January 2028. Other parts of the district will face different restrictions, depending on the type of building in which the accommodation is located.

The local council adopted the regulation on Thursday, introducing a differentiated approach to short-term accommodation services across the district.

Complete ban on short-term rentals in the Buda Castle District

Privately operated and other types of accommodation establishments registered in the Castle District by 31 December 2026 will be allowed to continue operating until 31 December 2027.

Once this transitional period ends, a complete ban on short-term accommodation services will come into force in the area from 1 January 2028.

Different rules for apartment buildings outside the Castle District

In areas outside the Castle District, the regulation distinguishes between accommodation establishments operating in condominium-style residential buildings and those located in other types of properties.

For establishments in condominium-style buildings, a transitional period will also apply. Those registered by 31 December 2026 will be allowed to continue providing accommodation until 31 December 2027 without having to prove that they have obtained the consent of the condominium.

From 1 January 2028, however, such approval will become mandatory.

The regulation covers not only traditional condominiums but also housing cooperatives and jointly owned residential buildings that have not been legally converted into condominiums but contain at least three flats.

By contrast, accommodation establishments located in buildings that do not fall into the condominium-style category will be allowed to operate throughout the year, without any such restrictions.

Buda Castle District. Budapest, Hungary. Photo: Unsplash

Fines of up to HUF 2 million for violations

The district notary will be responsible for monitoring compliance with the new rules. In cases of violations, they will be authorised to impose fines and order the temporary closure of an accommodation establishment for up to 45 days.

The maximum fines will be:

HUF 200,000 for private individuals and sole traders.

for private individuals and sole traders. HUF 2 million for legal entities and other organisations.

According to the preliminary impact assessment, there are currently 420 registered private and other accommodation establishments operating in District I, of which 19 are located in the Castle District.

The new regulation will enter into force on 1 January 2027.

World.title: Hungary to reopen railway line closed by former government to make way for battery giant
World.content:
Hungary’s new government plans to rebuild and reopen the railway line between Debrecen and Nagykereki, which was closed last year to make room for the expansion of Chinese battery manufacturer CATL’s factory in Debrecen. Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy says reconstruction work will begin next year, with passenger services returning as soon as possible.

Railway line closed despite local investment

In a Facebook post on Thursday morning, Vitézy recalled that passenger services on line 106, connecting Debrecen with the Bihar region and ending in Nagykereki, were suspended more than a year ago following a decision by former transport minister János Lázár.

The line was reportedly closed because it stood in the way of the expansion of CATL’s battery factory in Debrecen. At the time, it was one of Hungary’s busiest regional branch lines.

Vitézy also highlighted the efforts made by local communities to save and develop the railway. In 2015, 13 municipalities joined forces and secured HUF 500 million (approximately EUR 1.4 million) in EU funding to renovate several stations and improve their surroundings. Better connections with local bus services and the introduction of a regular timetable by Hungarian State Railways (MÁV) also helped make the line more attractive to passengers.

According to the minister, the project demonstrated that smaller communities were willing to invest in railway development rather than simply demanding new roads.

However, passenger services were discontinued in October last year.

Tisza government stopped land expropriation

Vitézy said the new Tisza government had made reopening the line a priority from its first day in office.

Following the government’s formation in May, the authorities immediately halted the land expropriation process and ensured that the railway land remained available. Preparations for reopening the line began at the same time.

The minister also revealed that representatives of the government had made the issue clear during their first negotiations with CATL: passengers’ interests would come first, and the railway would be reopened.

If you missed it: Budapest’s busy suburban rail line set for major renovation

Reconstruction to begin next year

The railway line will need to be redesigned and rebuilt before passenger services can resume, Vitézy explained. Construction is scheduled to begin next year.

The project will involve more than simply relaying the tracks. Several billion forints will also be spent on railway maintenance, with the aim of eliminating existing speed restrictions and ensuring competitive journey times.

“Instead of destroying railways, we promised railway development – and that is exactly what we are doing in Debrecen and throughout the country,” the minister wrote.

No exact reopening date has been announced yet, but the government says it intends to restore services as soon as the necessary work allows.

World.title: Budapest’s busy suburban rail line set for major renovation
World.content:
Budapest’s Ráckeve suburban railway line, known as the H6 HÉV, is set for a major upgrade aimed at making services faster, more reliable and more accessible, Hungary’s Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy has announced.

Hungarian government to modernise the suburban rail

The renovation will initially focus on the existing line, particularly the section between Dunaharaszti and Tököl, with plans also covering the surrounding towns of Szigetszentmiklós and Szigethalom. Vitézy said the improvements would offer passengers a more modern service and make public transport a more attractive alternative to travelling by car.

The minister said plans for the refurbishment had already been drawn up several years ago at the Budapest Development Centre. Their implementation has now become possible thanks to European Union funding, he added.

New trains and improved stations

The project will involve modernising suburban railway infrastructure and stations, with a particular emphasis on accessibility and better connections between suburban trains and buses. Planned improvements include more comfortable stops, step-free platforms, high-capacity park-and-ride facilities and bicycle storage areas. Bus stops will be moved closer to HÉV stations to make transfers easier, while passengers will benefit from real-time audio and visual travel information.

A major element will be the creation of an intermodal transport hub at Szigetszentmiklós-Gyártelep, designed to make it easier to switch between different forms of transport. The government also intends to launch a tender for new HÉV trains using EU funding. This could allow the rolling stock and railway infrastructure to be upgraded at the same time.

Extension to city centre remains a later phase

The development will be carried out in several stages. The first phase is expected to modernise the existing H6 line, while a proposed extension to Kálvin Square in central Budapest would be considered as part of a later planning and development stage.

Vitézy criticised the previous government’s handling of suburban railway development, saying that former construction and transport minister János Lázár had halted all related investment projects during the previous parliamentary term. He also pointed to the cancellation and subsequent unsuccessful relaunch of a rolling-stock procurement tender.

The minister said the current administration had to make up for years of inaction. The plans were also due to be presented at a public forum in Szigetszentmiklós, where railway specialists and designers would discuss the proposed improvements and answer residents’ questions.

World.title: Magyar government terminates Mészáros’ 35-year motorway concession, Orbán’s office reacts
World.content:
At Wednesday’s cabinet meeting, the government decided to terminate the 35-year motorway concession, Péter Magyar wrote on Facebook. “We are taking back the operation of the motorways from Lőrinc Mészáros and László Szíjj,” he wrote. In turn, Viktor Orbán’s former prime ministerial office has accused the government of planning to hand Hungary’s motorway assets over to foreign companies.

The statement, issued on Wednesday, came in response to a video posted by Prime Minister Péter Magyar on Facebook ahead of a cabinet meeting. Magyar described the motorway concessions as one of the largest and most significant cases of “Orbán-era corruption and theft”.

He added that payments to the consortium led by businessmen Lőrinc Mészáros and László Szíjj over the 35-year period would have cost Hungarian taxpayers HUF 23,000 billion (approximately EUR 62.4 billion).

“We are now closing this case. The government will make a final decision on it,” Magyar said.

Magyar and Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy announced on 18 September that they would terminate the concession agreement. According to them, there are several grounds for unilaterally terminating the contract; however, they wish to bring it to an end through negotiations and by mutual agreement, Telex wrote.

In early October, Péter Magyar said that the Mészáros–Szíjj partnership accepted the government’s decision and was prepared to terminate the HUF 23,000 billion motorway concession; shortly afterwards, however, the Mészáros family’s company stated that they were still in discussions with the government.

Orbán’s office warns against handing over national assets

In its statement, the former prime minister’s office claimed that the government was continuing to sell off the country and serve the interests of foreign companies. It called on the cabinet to put Hungarian interests first and avoid squandering national assets.

According to the statement, Péter Magyar is “telling all sorts of lies” about why it would benefit Hungary to place a motorway network that has so far operated under Hungarian ownership, and is one of the fastest-developing in Europe, under foreign management.

The office also claimed that people remembered that “foreign companies are interested in nothing other than taking their profits out of the country”.

“By contrast, the national government established a concession system that prioritised the interests of Hungarian motorists, families and hauliers, enabling unprecedented development of Hungary’s motorway network,” the statement said.

The 35-year motorway concession at the centre of the dispute

The large-scale motorway concession agreement came into force in September 2022, during Orbán’s time in office, and was signed for a period of 35 years.

Under the agreement, MKIF Hungarian Concession Infrastructure Development Plc (Magyar Koncessziós Infrastruktúra Fejlesztő Zrt.), a consortium involving seven private equity funds linked to businessmen Lőrinc Mészáros and László Szíjj, took over the rights to operate, renovate and expand 1,237 kilometres of Hungary’s expressway network.

Government cites major potential savings from ending the contract

On 18 September, Prime Minister Péter Magyar announced at a government press briefing that the government would terminate the motorway concession agreement, file a criminal complaint and initiate criminal proceedings.

Meanwhile, Dávid Vitézy said the state could operate and maintain the motorways 53 per cent more cheaply than MKIF. He added that major maintenance works could also be carried out at a 61 per cent lower cost if the state took over these responsibilities instead of leaving them with the concessionaire.

World.title: Russia warns Hungary of ‘serious consequences’ if it pushes Rosatom out of Paks II
World.content:
Russia has warned Hungary that cancelling its agreements on the Paks II nuclear power plant or removing Russian state-owned company Rosatom from the project could have serious financial and legal consequences. Moscow says the company is ready to address the new Hungarian leadership’s questions, but insists that the next move is now up to Budapest.

“You cannot terminate the agreements concluded on the Paks II project without consequences,” Russian Ambassador to Hungary Yevgeny Stanislavov told the Hungarian weekly Demokrata. He warned that excluding Rosatom could carry a heavy financial and legal price for Hungary.

The ambassador made clear that Moscow expects the existing agreements to be honoured. While Russia remains open to talks, he said, the Hungarian side must decide how the project should proceed.

Russian ambassador to Hungary Yevgeny Stanislavov. Photo: hungary.mid.ru

Moscow points to Bulgaria and Finland

To support his warning, Stanislavov referred to Bulgaria and Finland, both of which have had disputes involving Rosatom.

According to the ambassador, Bulgaria abandoned its planned partnership with the Russian company, subsequently paid millions of euros in compensation and ultimately failed to build a new nuclear power plant. Regarding Finland, he pointed to an international court case that Rosatom recently won.

Stanislavov said Rosatom was willing to discuss the project’s future directly with the Hungarian government and answer questions about its technical and financial aspects. He dismissed reports about a possible replacement of the main contractor as speculation, arguing that any such decision would require concrete proposals, prices and financial terms.

If you missed it: Hungary’s energy minister dismisses head of Paks nuclear power plant with immediate effect, announces new leader

Hungary is still reviewing the nuclear project

The warning comes as Hungary’s new government is conducting a comprehensive review of Paks II. The assessment covers not only technical and financial matters but also the project’s technological and legal conditions.

Attila Ságodi, chairman of the board of Paks II Ltd, told Russian state news agency TASS in mid-November that the review was expected to be completed by the end of 2026.

Prime Minister Péter Magyar has previously said that the project’s costs may have risen to as much as twice the original estimate, while the initial deadlines are no longer achievable. Rosatom chief executive Alexey Likhachev, meanwhile, has said the company is ready to provide detailed figures in response to technical and financial questions, although it has not yet received a formal request from the Hungarian government.

Ambassador urges Hungary to maintain Russian energy ties

Stanislavov also argued that continuing Russian natural gas deliveries would serve Hungary’s interests. He criticised EU restrictions on Russian energy, claiming they were causing significant damage to the European economy as well.

He declined to provide details about negotiations between Hungarian oil and gas company MOL and Russia’s Gazprom Neft concerning the sale of a stake in Serbia’s NIS energy company, but said the process had not yet been concluded.

The ambassador also criticised the new Hungarian government’s approach to Ukraine. He questioned whether Budapest had received sufficient guarantees from Kyiv regarding the rights of the Hungarian minority in Transcarpathia.

Stanislavov further recalled September’s diplomatic dispute, when Hungary expelled ten Russian diplomats. He described the move as unfriendly and unjustified at the time, while Moscow announced that it would expel Hungarian diplomats in response.

The ambassador said it remained to be seen whether Hungary’s new leadership wanted to avoid further diplomatic tensions. As for Paks II, however, the immediate decision now rests with Budapest.

World.title: Hungary among EU’s worst countries for gender equality, new report reveals
World.content:
Hungary is among the lowest-ranking European Union countries in the gender equality index published by the European Institute for Gender Equality (EIGE), along with Cyprus and Czechia, the institute’s report published on Wednesday shows.

EU gender equality progress remains slow

The Gender Equality Index tracks progress on gender equality across the EU. It brings together 27 indicators from all Member States across six areas of life: work, money, knowledge, time, power and health. The data is combined into a score from 0 to 100, where 100 means full gender equality, showing where gaps remain and where policy can have the greatest impact.

According to the annual report, the European Union scored 64.5 points on the scale measuring gender equality, an improvement of just 0.9 points compared with the previous year and of 5.6 points since 2020. The results show that progress remains extremely slow, and improvement in one area does not necessarily go hand in hand with advances in others, the report said.

France leads the ranking with 74.8 points, ahead of Sweden, Denmark and Spain.

Meanwhile, Hungary is among the 14 member states that improved their results but whose gap relative to the EU average widened further. This group also includes Belgium, France, the Netherlands, Romania and Slovakia. By contrast, 13 member states, including Czechia, Poland and Austria, improved while narrowing their gap to the EU average.

Decision-making remains the weakest area

Europe-wide, the area of decision-making remains the weakest of gender equality and modest improvements are largely thanks to quotas required by law. In seven member states, women already fill at least 40 percent of the seats on the boards of the largest listed companies.

Progress elsewhere is considerably slower, however. In education, a setback has been measured since 2020 in 11 member states, while in health, progress has essentially stalled.

Also, significant differences remain between women and men in the sharing of child-care and family responsibilities.

Gender equality could boost the EU economy

According to EIGE’s research, promoting gender equality could increase per-capita EU GDP by 6.1 to 9.6 percent by 2050 and could contribute to the creation of as many as 10.5 million new jobs.

PM Magyar calls for historic breakthrough in women’s rights

In what he called a “historic breakthrough” in the protection of the rights of women, Prime Minister Péter Magyar recently called on parliament to support the government’s related aims, including ratification of the Istanbul Convention. He asked the parliamentary groups to agree that decisions regarding women’s lives, bodies and futures should be made in consultation with them, and to adopt the package together “on behalf of the entire nation”.

World.title: Hungary moves to end tobacco wholesale monopoly introduced by the Fidesz government
World.content:
The Magyar government has proposed ending the exclusive tobacco wholesale and supply rights held by the National Tobacco Supply Company, opening the market to competition from 1 June 2027.

Hungary to shake up tobacco wholesale

The move would dismantle a key part of the tobacco distribution system established under the Fidesz government, although the state-controlled retail network of national tobacco shops would remain in place for now.

The bill, submitted to parliament late on 17 November, would terminate the company’s concession without compensation. Tobacco shops would be able to source their products from multiple suppliers, provided those businesses hold the necessary excise licences.

Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy said the government wanted to end a system in which business interests linked to former transport and investment minister János Lázár had benefited from substantial profits without meaningful competition.

Government challenges decade-long concession

The National Tobacco Supply Company received its exclusive distribution rights in 2015, without a public tender, under a concession originally intended to last 20 years. Between 2015 and 2025, it generated HUF 67.3 billion in profit, of which almost HUF 64 billion was paid out in dividends, according to figures cited by Vitézy.

The company recorded HUF 11.4 billion in profit in 2025 alone, distributing the entire amount to its owners. Vitézy argued that the arrangement had effectively guaranteed the company revenue while exposing it to limited commercial risk. The government also questions whether awarding the exclusive rights without a competitive tender complied with Hungarian and EU competition rules.

Under the proposal, the company would still be allowed to supply tobacco shops, but would lose its monopoly. The government says this means there is no justification for compensation.
