"Your experience with previous governments has been so bitter that I am having to bear the consequences.

This is not the old government; this is a government of friends. It knows how to honour friendship, and you are my true friends. So, without hesitation or reservation, please write to me openly about what still needs to be improved," he said.

He added that the government was willing to consider suggestions from industry and urged business leaders to communicate their requirements directly to him.

The Prime Minister also said India's progress depended on recognising the contribution of different sections of society, including farmers, entrepreneurs, industries, wealth creators and taxpayers.

World.title: Is Asim Munir Pakistan's Gorbachev? Why he wants to divide Pakistan and what it means for India
World.content:
Pakistan's proposed division into smaller provinces is being pitched as administrative reform. But strategic affairs analyst Sushant Sareen believes there is a larger political and financial agenda behind it.

In an interview with me on Faultline on Times Axis Youtube channel, he argued that the Pakistan military wants to fragment the country's political landscape so that no political party can challenge its dominance.

âIt's not an army. It's a political party. It's like the Communist Party of China,â he said.

Sareen believes the proposed restructuring could weaken Pakistan's major political parties, particularly the

in Sindh and the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz in Punjab.



If Karachi is separated from Sindh, he argues, the PPP could lose much of its political influence.

âIf People's Party loses Karachi, there's no point running Sindh because Sindh without Karachi is nothing,â he said.

The same dynamic, he believes, could play out in Punjab. Smaller provinces could weaken established political dynasties while creating opportunities for local leaders to become chief ministers.

âIt's better to become the chief minister of a smaller part of Punjab than be just a member of the provincial assembly or a minister in Punjab,â Sareen said.





He believes the restructuring is being pushed by the military establishment rather than emerging from a genuine political or administrative process.

âThis is by diktat of a dictator, or a quasi-dictator, or an undeclared dictator,â he said.

Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has suggested holding a referendum on the proposal. Sareen questioned whether a referendum could bypass the constitutional process for creating new provinces.

He also warned that the restructuring could trigger political backlash, administrative confusion and instability.

âIf

wants to be the Gorbachev of Pakistan, I'm the last person to stop him from doing that,â Sareen said.

Is mineral wealth another motive?

Sareen also pointed to concerns that the proposed restructuring could give the establishment greater control over the mineral wealth of Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

He believes the military wants greater control over resources, while also seeking a larger share of Pakistan's revenues.

The existing revenue-sharing arrangement gives provinces around 57 per cent of the divisible pool. Sareen argued that the federal government already receives the lion's share of the country's overall resources.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âGreed has no limit,â he said.

He believes the military's financial interests could be another factor driving the proposed restructuring.

Why India should watch closely

Would a reorganised Pakistan become more stable? Sareen doubts it.

He believes instability in Pakistan could benefit India, but only if it remains controlled.

âInstability in Pakistan is very good for us, but provided it's a controlled instability,â he said.

An uncontrolled crisis in a country of around 250 million people could become a serious problem for India.

The military's attempt to restructure Pakistan could therefore have consequences far beyond its domestic politics.

World.title: Next door, worlds apart: India's child malnutrition puzzle
World.content:
AI generated picture

Good news nationally, with a catch

India's fight against child malnutrition is showing progress, but not on every front. While fewer children are falling behind in height, weight-related problems remain stubbornly persistent.

Does living near a big city help?

India's latest child nutrition data reveals striking inequalities even between neighbouring districts

The districts that were carved out

What lies behind the gap

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

A common refrain in India is that birth is a lottery, where a child is born can, in many ways, determine how their childhood is shaped, if not their entire life. But even children born in neighbouring districts may have very different courses in life. This interesting facet has emerged from an analysis of district-wise malnutrition data published in the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6).In Nagpur district, roughly one in five children under five is classified as stunted, or too short for their age under standard child-growth measures. In neighbouring Chandrapur, also in Maharashtra's Vidarbha region, it is more than two in five. The latest survey puts childhood stunting at 20.2% in Nagpur and 42.4% in Chandrapur. The two neighbouring districts show remarkably divergent statistics.The previous survey makes the gap harder to explain. In NFHS-5, conducted in 2019â21, Nagpur's figure was 27.6% and Chandrapur's 37.3%. Since then, Nagpur's estimate has fallen and Chandrapur's has risen.In November 2025, TOI reported on a programme for 915 mothers and children through 27 Anganwadi centres in Chandrapur's Jiwati taluka. The people running it described low literacy, reliance on subsistence farming and little variety in children's food.It is a reflection on how authorities are trying to reverse the worrying trend.The World Health Organization links stunting to poorer learning and school performance, more frequent illness and lower wages in adulthood. The first 1,000 days, from conception to a child's second birthday, are particularly critical. Growth lost during this period can have lasting consequences. While some catch-up growth is possible, full recovery is often difficult.India has made a substantial gain against stunting, which reflects the effects of poor nutrition, repeated illness and other disadvantages over a child's early years. The national estimate fell from 35.5% in NFHS-5 to 29.3% in NFHS-6.Children's weight-related indicators have barely changed, though. Wasting â being too thin for one's height â went from 19.3% to 19%. Underweight prevalence, which reflects both long-term and more recent nutritional problems, remained nearly flat, going from 32.1% to 31.8%. Severe wasting did fall, from 7.7% to 5.2%. Put simply, fewer of India's children are now classified as too short for their age, but almost one in five is still too thin for their height.TOI compared published figures for 680 districts and single-district Union territories with usable estimates for all three principal measures in both rounds. In 235, all three percentages were lower in the newer survey. In 196, stunting was lower but wasting and underweight were both higher.Vidarbha is not an exception. In Madhya Pradesh's Malwa belt, Indore reports 22.8% stunting, against 38.6% in neighbouring Dhar. The share of underweight children is 30.8% in Indore and 53.2% in Dhar, where more than half of young children are underweight.In Maharashtra's Marathwada, Beed's stunting estimate is 24.8%, while Hingoli's is 43.1%. In Odisha's KBK region, the historically disadvantaged belt associated with Kalahandi, Balangir and Koraput, Kalahandi reports 26.9% and Rayagada 47.2%. The two districts share a boundary.Often, it appears to. Nationally, stunting is estimated at 23.9% among urban children, compared with 30.9% among rural children. Look at Nagpur or Indore, and the obvious explanation might be jobs, hospitals and markets. Lucknow, too, reports a lower figure than neighbouring Sitapur: 31% against 45.5%.Tamil Nadu, though, bucks the trend. Coimbatore has a major industrial city, yet its district stunting estimate is 28%, compared with 15.6% in neighbouring Tiruppur, itself an industrial centre. The same is true in Bihar. Patna district, which contains the state capital, records 42.7% stunting, more than neighbouring Vaishali's 36.1%. On the underweight measure, the pattern reverses: Patna's estimate is 29.8% against Vaishali's 36.4%. A district with a large city also includes the villages beyond it, and its average mixes both.Research backs up the complexity of this relationship. A study of more than 443,000 children using earlier NFHS rounds found strong associations between stunting and household resources and mothers' education. After accounting for other characteristics, urban residence on its own was not a consistent predictor in the later rounds. A family's circumstances counted for more than its address.The clearest example is in Gujarat, where an official report acknowledged that averages were hiding disadvantage.Until September 2007, Tapi was part of Surat. The old district combined Surat's large urban economy with remote tribal areas. A Gujarat government human-development report, published in 2015, said combining them in one statistical profile had obscured conditions in places needing more development attention. Tapi was created from five predominantly tribal rural talukas. At the 2011 Census, Scheduled Tribes made up about 84% of its population.In NFHS-6, the stunting difference is relatively small: 30.4% in Surat and 33.9% in Tapi. The gap shows up in weight. Wasting stands at 14.1% in Surat versus 26.9% in Tapi, where more than one child in four is too thin for their height. Underweight prevalence is 32.2% versus 43.9%.The same pattern appears where other districts were divided. Chhota Udaipur, carved out of Vadodara in 2013, reports 51.5% stunting, affecting more than half its young children, compared with Vadodara's 35.5%. Palghar, separated from Thane in 2014, reports 42%, against Thane's 29%. State government figures based on the 2011 Census put the Scheduled Tribe share at 37.39% in Palghar and 5.27% in the reorganised Thane district. Palghar itself spans the urbanising VasaiâVirar belt and remote settlements, so its average hides further differences within the district.In Haryana, Nuh was formed in 2005 from five blocks of the former Gurgaon district. The region had been receiving special development attention well before that: Haryana established the Mewat Development Board in 1980. Today, the stunting estimates for Nuh and neighbouring Gurugram are 46% and 21.6%. The survey's separate measure of adequate diets among children aged six to 23 months also shows a wide gap, at 8.1% and 19.6%.Mizoram has a similar case. Mamit was carved out of Aizawl district in 1998. The latest stunting figures are 41.2% in Mamit and 23.1% in Aizawl. The Mamit administration's 2011 Census profile identifies it as one of the state's least urbanised districts.NFHS-6 found that just 15.3% of children aged six to 23 months nationally met its standard for an adequate diet, based on a combination of food groups and feeding frequency. That is up from 11% in the previous survey. It still means more than eight in ten children at that age miss out on enough variety in their food, enough meals in a day, or both.Family circumstances show up clearly in the data. An analysis of NFHS-5 found stunting among about 46% of children whose mothers had no formal education, compared with 23% among children whose mothers had higher education â half the rate. Education overlaps with household wealth, maternal health and living conditions, so this is an association, and the separate effects are hard to untangle.There are limits to these comparisons. NFHS is not a census of every child, and its rounds do not follow the same children. District estimates have sampling uncertainty, which this analysis has not independently quantified. Research using earlier surveys has also found that the season of measurement affects wasting. Yet, as India looks to become more prosperous, the onus is on ensuring that none of the next generation falls through the cracks. That would be a big step towards becoming a developed nation.

World.title: ‘TN becoming Vice City’: Stalin targets Vijay over Rs 140-crore heroin haul in Chennai
World.content:
DMK president

on Thursday criticised the ruling TVK government over the law and order situation and alleged narcotics smuggling in Tamil Nadu, accusing Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay's administration of allowing the state to turn into a "Vice City".

Reacting to the seizure of heroin worth Rs 140 crore in Chennai by the Union government's Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), Stalin said the central agency had been carrying out major drug busts in the state every month.

In a post on X, the former chief minister recalled that the DRI had busted a narcotics network worth Rs 270 crore in Nagapattinam last month, allegedly linked to a TVK functionary. He questioned why the Tamil Nadu Police had failed to detect such large-scale

in the state.



"Are they unable to catch them, or are they turning a blind eye?" Stalin asked, alleging that a state once known as a leading destination for investors had now become a "favourite destination" for methamphetamine and heroin smugglers.

Stalin shares 'TVK Vice City' graphic, targets Vijay government

Accompanying his post, Stalin shared a satirical graphic titled "TVK Vice City", modelled on the cover art of the video game Grand Theft Auto: Vice City.





The graphic features illustrated portraits resembling Chief Minister Vijay and a TVK functionary against a neon-lit coastal skyline, along with images of narcotics, syringes, a laboratory setup, a crime scene outline and a silhouette of a person behind bars.

It also incorporates television news clippings highlighting recent controversies, including a report on the National Commission for Women seeking an explanation from the Director General of Police (DGP) and another report dated November 9, 2026, quoting a man who alleged that he was threatened into recording a video statement.

Stalin also accused the state's DGP of citing crime statistics a day earlier to divert public attention from the prevailing situation.

He said merely responding to incidents by stating that "a case has been registered" was insufficient, and questioned why state agencies and the 65 special task force teams formed to curb drug trafficking had failed to apprehend smugglers.

World.title: India, Italy target €20bn trade by 2029, explore economic corridor linking Asia and Europe
World.content:
India and Italy have set a target of raising bilateral trade to â¬20 billion by 2029, from â¬14.2 billion in 2025. The two countries also plan to set up task forces to ease business operations and explore an economic corridor linking Asia and Europe.

The decisions were discussed during a meeting between Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal and Italian deputy prime minister and foreign minister Antonio Tajani in Rome on November 18, according to Italy's ministry of foreign affairs.

The two sides also discussed the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), which aims to connect Indian markets with Europe through the Middle East using rail and maritime networks.



Italy is looking to strengthen the role of its Mediterranean ports in the proposed corridor. Tajani identified the port of Trieste as a potential gateway for goods moving towards Central and Eastern Europe.

Separately, the two countries have agreed to establish task forces in India and Italy to help businesses overcome bureaucratic and administrative hurdles. According to the Italian foreign ministry, the task forces will work to simplify procedures and facilitate trade and investment between the two countries.





The Italian foreign ministry said IMEC could create new opportunities in trade, logistics and energy connectivity. For India, the proposed route could offer an additional link to European markets and help diversify supply chains.

India and Italy are also exploring the establishment of an Innovation Hub in India, modelled on Italy's INNOVIT Centre in San Francisco. The proposed hub would bring together startups, businesses and research institutions to promote technology partnerships, innovation and investment.

According to India's Press Information Bureau (PIB), sectoral discussions focused on technology transfer, joint research, electric mobility, food processing and advanced manufacturing.

The meeting also covered the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA). According to the PIB, both sides welcomed the conclusion of negotiations and discussed how the pact could improve market access, boost investments and strengthen supply chains. World.title: Female infanticide reported in Rameswaram; three booked
World.content:
A newborn baby girl was buried alive on the premises of the parents’ house at Sambai in Rameswaram on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), as it was the second female child for the couple.

According to the police, the crime came to light after the mother, Logananidhi, developed health issues after the delivery and was rushed to Rameswaram Government Hospital.

The doctors found out that the woman had delivery-related health complications and sought details about the newborn baby. The family members claimed that the child, a preterm baby, had died immediately after birth.

During inquiry, the mother reportedly admitted to the crime committed by her husband Nagapandi, father-in-law Krishnan and sister-in-law Muneeswari, despite her pleas and attempt to save the infant.

The family members then exhumed the body of the infant and brought it to the hospital, following which the hospital authorities alerted the police.

The police have booked all the three accused under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita on the charge of culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

World.title: Areca growers stage protest in Shivamogga, allege injustice in awarding compensation under weather-based crop insurance scheme
World.content:
Farmers from Tirthahalli, Sagar and Hosanagara taluks staged a protest in front of the Deputy Commissioner’s office in Shivamogga on Thursday, alleging that areca growers have been denied their due under the weather-based crop insurance scheme.

The protesters said they would not call off the agitation until their demands were met. They were joined by elected representatives, including Shivamogga MP B.Y. Raghavendra and Tirthahalli MLA Araga Jnanendra.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Raghavendra said farmers had paid premiums in the hope of compensation when adverse weather damaged their crops, but had been let down on a large scale. “Farmers in many villages have not received even the premium they paid, let alone the sum assured. Insurance companies have saved more than ₹30 crore from the total premium collected, including the contributions of the State and Central governments,” he said.

He said he had expected farmers to receive fair compensation once faulty rain-gauge stations were repaired. “However, the injustice continued even after the repairs. Officers draw up the term sheets in consultation with the insurance companies, and these are designed to favour the companies, not the farmers. A large number of growers were denied fair benefits because of these faulty term sheets,” he said.

Mr. Raghavendra urged the State government to come to the farmers’ rescue. “The insurance companies saved about ₹20 crore last year and another ₹30 crore this year. This is money paid by farmers as premium. We demand that the companies distribute the savings among the growers who suffered losses,” he said.

Jnanendra, a former Minister, said the Centre had launched the scheme with great ambition, but it was not benefiting those in need. “The entire process of fixing the compensation amount is not transparent. There are no officers to address grievances, and there are large discrepancies in finalising the amounts,” he said.

The MLA, who chairs the Public Accounts Committee, said he had held a meeting with the officials concerned in Bengaluru the previous day and concluded that the entire process was unscientific. “There is no proper system for identifying backup rain-gauge stations when a station develops a technical fault. The cooperative societies that collect premiums from growers have been kept in the dark about the scheme,” he said.

The protest was jointly organised by several farmers’ bodies, including the Shodha Crop Insurance Struggle Committee, areca growers’ associations, farmer producer companies, and cooperative societies from the Malnad taluks of the district.

World.title: Financial dispute behind Bagalur scrap dealer shootout; business partner, associate arrested
World.content:
A long-standing financial dispute between two scrap dealers is suspected to have led to the pre-planned murder of Imraz Pasha, who was shot dead near Bagalur on Monday. The accused allegedly used his licensed pistol to fire at the victim. The alleged murder weapon is yet to be recovered.

The Bagalur police have arrested the prime accused, Naveed, and his associate Mubarak in connection with the murder.

Imraz Pasha, 45, lived in Gottigere off Bannerghatta Road and ran a scrap business in Yelahanka. On Monday, he reportedly received a call from Naveed asking to meet him. He informed his son before leaving for the meeting, never to return. This call proved crucial in cracking the case, sources said.

According to the police, Naveed and Pasha had been in a long-term business partnership but developed differences over financial transactions. The dispute allegedly prompted Naveed to plan the murder.

As part of the plan, Naveed had reportedly visited the crime scene a day before the incident to conduct a recce. On the day of the murder, he allegedly called Pasha and asked him to meet. Naveed and Mubarak arrived on a two-wheeler and reportedly spent nearly two hours moving around the layout while waiting for Pasha. When he arrived, they called him aside for a conversation. A heated argument reportedly broke out over the financial dispute, following which Naveed allegedly pulled out his licensed pistol and fired three rounds at him.

Pasha sustained bullet injuries, including a fatal wound to his head, and died on the spot. The accused subsequently fled on the scooter they had arrived on.

CCTV footage capturing the accused’s entry into and exit from the locality proved crucial in helping the police identify and track them down.

Confirming the arrests, Deputy Commissioner of Police (North East) Mithun Kumar said three bullet injuries were found on the victim’s body. “We have information about the weapon and it will be seized soon,” he said.

World.title: Anna Stadium in Tiruchi to get new synthetic track
World.content:
The Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu (SDAT) plans to lay a new synthetic track by replacing the decade-old turf at Anna Stadium at Race Course here.

The existing eight-lane track was laid in 2016. With the inauguration of the track approved by the International Association of Athletic Federations, Tiruchi, became the fourth city to get the facility after Chennai, Coimbatore, and Madurai. The all-weather court track served the organisers to conduct many tournaments for track and field. It provided a consistent surface for competitors to test their athletic ability unhindered by adverse weather conditions.

However, the track developed many spots and uneven surfaces because of the wear and tear, affecting practice of the players, SDAT trainees, district-level players, and so on. The players complained that the ageing track with bubbles and worn patches affected grip and speed while running.

Taking into account the demands of athletes and trainees, the SDAT has decided to lay a new synthetic track.

District Sports Officer Kannan told The Hindu that the district had prepared a proposal for the project. The project was estimated to cost ₹9 crore. It would be laid on the existing 400-metre track by removing the existing turf. The project would be implemented once it received the financial allocation from the State government.

The DSO said it would be a boost to the athletes and trainees. Similarly, it was decided to illuminate the area around the compound wall of the stadium with bulbs. It was aimed at improving the safety of those walking around the stadium on Race Course Road.

World.title: Welfare assistance distributed in The Nilgiris
World.content:
The Nilgiris District Collector Lakshmi Bhavya Tanneeru distributed welfare assistance amounting to ₹19.45 lakh to 24 beneficiaries recently as part of the Ungalai Thedi, Ungal Ooril scheme in The Nilgiris.

The benefits included financial assistance for death and funeral expenses; assistance to six beneficiaries under the Chief Minister’s Accident Relief Fund; and bank loans through the Tamil Nadu State Rural and Urban Livelihoods Mission.

“Subsequently, the District Collector inspected the schemes being implemented and the registers being maintained at the Udhagamandalam Taluk Office. She also received petitions containing various grievances and requests from members of the public and instructed the department officials to take appropriate action on them,” a press release from the district administration read.

The Collector also inspected fair price shops in Udhagamandalam, including one at Indu Nagar, where she checked the availability and quality of commodities. She also inspected the Government Udhagamandalam Medical College and Hospital, where she oversaw the quality of treatment being provided at different departments. She then visited a government-aided school at Fingerpost, where she inspected the quality of midday meals being provided to schoolchildren.

World.title: Vizag railway station soon to enter top 5 in platform count: MP Sribharat
World.content:
Visakhapatnam Railway Station is undergoing redevelopment at an estimated cost of ₹660 crore to meet growing passenger demand and upgrade infrastructure to international standards, Visakhapatnam MP M. Sribharat said on Thursday.

The MP inspected the ongoing works with senior railway officials. He said that the project outlay had been revised from the initial ₹480 crore to accommodate future traffic requirements.

Interacting with the media, Mr. Sribharat said that the Railway Board had approved increasing the number of platforms from eight to 14, which would place Visakhapatnam among the top five railway stations in the country in terms of platform count.

To minimise train delays, quadrupling the railway line between Gopalapatnam and Visakhapatnam and capacity augmentation along the Duvvada–Gopalapatnam corridor were underway, alongside the Simhachalam bypass line.

These measures are expected to improve train punctuality from the current 73–74% to 95–96%, he added.

A 72-metre-wide air concourse, designed like an airport terminal to accommodate around 4,000 passengers at a time, is being built to connect the new station buildings on both sides. The upgraded complex will house food courts, retail outlets and air-conditioned lounges. Parking facilities for about 450 cars and 2,000 two-wheelers, besides dedicated bays for cab aggregators, are also being developed.

Emphasising sustainable infrastructure across the 60-acre station premises, Mr. Sribharat said rooftop solar panels would be installed and urged officials to implement rainwater harvesting and sewage treatment systems. Stating that the first phase is targeted for completion by December 2027 and the entire project by December 2028, he stressed timely execution without compromising quality or passenger convenience.

Modern rail connectivity, he added, was vital to support Visakhapatnam’s industrial, commercial and tourism growth.

World.title: IND vs NZ, 1st Test: Nicholls, Phillips revive New Zealand after early hiccups
World.content:
Jasprit Bumrah bowled his heart out. But Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips rescued New Zealand with an unbroken 173-run association for the sixth wicket to prevent India from running away with the game on the opening day of the first Test at the Basin Reserve on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

Riding on Nicholls’ unbeaten 113 (221b, 14x4) and Phillips’ 94 not out (182b, 13x4), New Zealand finished the day at 243 for five. Had a miscommunication between Devdutt Padikkal at short fine-leg and Rishabh Pant not resulted in the former dropping a top-edge extracted by Prasidh Krishna when Nicholls was on 102, India may have held the edge. But after being reduced to 70 for five early in the second session, the host’s will be the happier dressing room.

The softer ball and clear skies made conditions easier to bat, but Nicholls and Phillips pounced on virtually every scoring opportunity. Their partnership not only arrested the slide but also ensured India’s four-pronged pace attack had little to show for its toil after lunch.

India’s decision to field after winning the toss appeared vindicated early on, with Bumrah striking in the opening over. Tom Latham shouldered arms to the third ball, only to see it nip back and knock over his off-stump. The Indian spearhead returned closer to lunch to remove Daryl Mitchell, who walked down the wicket but failed to keep the ball down, allowing Yashasvi Jaiswal to take a sharp catch at forward short-leg.

Anshul Kamboj and Akash Deep, preferred over Mohammed Siraj, kept the pressure on with probing spells. Kamboj had Devon Conway driving at a full-length delivery, with Pant pouching the edge behind the stumps. He was also unlucky when Rachin Ravindra nicked him behind in the 21st over, only for India to be denied a review after the TV umpire ruled the ball had made contact with the bat first.

Testing times: Editorial on India’s two-Test series against New Zealand

Bumrah’s dismissal of Tom Blundell after lunch briefly threatened to extend India’s dominance. Blundell hung his bat out and Gill took a neat catch at first slip. But Phillips countered with a crisp cover drive and survived a contentious DRS review off Bumrah, with the ball appearing to make multiple impacts before the TV umpire ruled bat-first.

Nicholls, meanwhile, grew increasingly assured, bringing up his maiden Test fifty against India with a pull off Kamboj. Phillips made the most of the fuller deliveries from Prasidh Krishna, while Washington Sundar, preferred ahead of Ravindra Jadeja, failed to break the partnership.

India had its opportunity late in the day, but Padikkal dropped a sitter. Nicholls and Phillips capitalised, leaving the visitors to rue a promising start that yielded no further reward.

Total: 243-5 (49 Overs)

Fall of wickets: 1-2, 2-12, 3-51, 4-52, 5-70
